A man fascinated with vampires and satanism who placed deer heads and slaughtered lambs with inverted crosses at churches across the New Forest has been detained under the Mental Health Act.

Benjamin Lewis, of Totton, Southampton, previously pleaded guilty to five counts of religiously aggravated harassment and two counts of theft of lambs between February and August 2025.

Sentencing the 48-year-old, who appeared by videolink at Southampton Crown Court, to be detained in hospital with restrictions, Judge William Mousley KC said: “These offences taken together would otherwise have justified substantial sentences of imprisonment.”

Laura Deuxberry, prosecuting, told the court that lambs had been stolen from two small farms in the local Hampshire area.

Lewis had killed them by slitting their throats before dumping their bodies at four churches as well as at a mental health facility where he had previously been treated.

She said that in February 2025, a deer’s head was found with an inverted wooden cross at St Theresa’s Church in Totton followed by a lamb being placed on a light fixture below a statue of Mary along with another inverted cross.

open image in gallery Benjamin Lewis, of Totton, Southampton , previously pleaded guilty to five counts of religiously aggravated harassment and two counts of theft of lambs between February and August 2025 ( PA Archive )

Ms Deuxberry said that Canon Simon Treloar had initially attempted to make light of the first incident by telling the media that he would have “preferred sausages” and said that sausages had later been left at the church as well as the animal bodies.

The prosecutor added that children had seen the dead lamb and been “very distressed as a result”.

She added that Canon Treloar told police that he believed the perpetrator had targeted the church during the Easter period and he felt “targeted and disturbed”.

At Christ Church in Emery Down, Lewis also dumped a deer without a head on one date in February followed on a later date by a deer’s head being placed in the church’s pulpit on top of a cross which had been moved from the altar.

Ms Deuxberry said that blood staining had forced the church to dispose of the cross.

Lewis also targeted St Peter’s Church in Bramshaw, where a dead lamb was placed on flagpole with a tarot card next to it and a deer’s head “crawling with maggots” was placed on a pew on a later date.

At Christ’s Church in Colbury, a lamb was placed on a tree stump with an inverted stone cross next to it, Ms Deuxberry said.

open image in gallery A lamb was placed on a tree stump with an inverted stone cross next to it at Christ’s Church in Colbury ( Google Maps )

The prosecutor said a deer’s head with an inverted cross was put on the gates of the Anchor House mental health facility in Totton where Lewis had previously been treated.

Ms Deuxberry said there had been a number of previous incidents dating back five years that the prosecution were not pursuing.

Lewis was also convicted of religious harassment in 2003 in the first case of its kind in the country.

The prosecutor said that when Lewis was arrested deer blood was found in the boot of his car, with mixed animal blood in the vehicle.

She added that when his home was searched by police, officers found satanic symbols and ritual notes as well as sketches of vampires and “concerning books about vampires and how best to kill humans”.

A suitcase containing inverted crosses and images of “people cutting and sucking blood from each other” was also found.

Ms Deuxberry said the members of the public who had found the dead animal parts had been “distressed and disturbed”, and the owner of some of the stolen lambs had considered moving from her farm where she had lived all of her life.

She said by targeting churches, Lewis had caused upset to congregations and added: “It’s meant to be a place of sanctuary but unfortunately these incidents caused them to be fearful of going to their sanctuaries.”

open image in gallery At Christ Church in Emery Down, Lewis also dumped a deer without a head on one date in February followed on a later date by a deer’s head being placed in the church’s pulpit on top of a cross which had been moved from the altar ( Google Maps )

Consultant forensic psychiatrist Dr Gauruv Malhan told the court that Lewis had been diagnosed with severe autism and obsessive-compulsive disorder as well as mixed personality disorder and a mild learning disability.

He said Lewis had “fantastical thinking patterns” and had “limited insight” into his condition.

He added that his autism dated from birth and at the age of 13 had placed a dead frog on a cross inside a church.

Andrew Price, defending, said: “He is very sorry and wants it to be known and clear that he recognises that he has done wrong, that he recognises the situation and circumstances of the victims.”

Lewis told the court after he was sentenced: “I want to just apologise to the victims because they said they were worried about me if I was to come out, I do not want people to worry about me.”

News.title: Madison mayor demands barricades be removed from site where Black man was killed by cops
News.content:

The mayor of Madison, Wisconsin, has called for the immediate removal of barricades and tents blocking a city intersection where a Black man was shot and killed by police last month, warning that the growing protest encampment has become unsafe and unsustainable.

Mayor Satya Rhodes-Conway issued a statement over the weekend requesting a “respectful transition” at Williamson and South Baldwin Streets. The intersection has remained closed to traffic since July 22, when four officers confronted 38-year-old Corey Ruiz on suspicion of attempting to break into parked cars. Ruiz wrestled with cops as they tried to detain him and was shot dead. Video of the shooting sparked immediate outrage.

While the site initially emerged as a vigil and protest area, Rhodes-Conway noted that the gathering has shifted and is now increasingly occupied by people experiencing homelessness.

“The occupation of the intersection is neither a safe nor a sustainable solution for the unhoused or the surrounding community,” Rhodes-Conway said. “At this point, it is distracting rather than supporting the dialogue and organizing that need to happen to make lasting change. And it is deeply harming the Marquette neighborhood.”

The prolonged road closure has disrupted local businesses, blocked residents’ access to their homes and forced detours for a nearby fire station, raising concerns over emergency response times.

open image in gallery The mayor of Madison, Wisconsin, is demanding the removal of barricades and tents blocking a city intersection where Corey Ruiz, a 38-year-old a Black man, was shot and killed by police on July 22 ( Reuters )

“The barricades must come down; people need to be able to access their homes and jobs so they don't lose them; and businesses need to be able to open,” the mayor said, adding that the city stands ready to assist anyone on the site willing to help clear vehicles, take down tents and deconstruct the barriers.

Rhodes-Conway said that the city intended to preserve artwork and memorial items from the site, working with the Ruiz family and local residents to establish a permanent memorial.

However, she urged community members to redirect their grassroots energy toward existing social services, specifically pointing to the city’s soon-to-open Bartillon men's shelter.

The mayor also clarified that the Madison Police Department was not leading the investigation into the shooting and held no authority regarding potential charges or arrest decisions.

open image in gallery Makeshift barricades stand outside a memorial for Corey Ruiz at the site where he was shot and killed by police on July 22 in Madison, Wisconsin ( Reuters )

The Wisconsin Department of Justice’s Division of Criminal Investigation is handling the case independently, and the Dane County district attorney will ultimately decide whether to file charges.

The mayor’s statement comes after days of mounting tension in the city over the killing. Bystander video of the encounter shows four officers wrestling Ruiz to the ground before one officer pulls a gun and shoots him three times.

The department stated that officers chased Ruiz on a bicycle before a physical struggle began in the street. According to police, Ruiz drew a fixed-blade knife and injured an officer, who then fired his weapon after an attempt to use a Taser failed.

open image in gallery Kah'liyah Aliomar, the daughter of Corey Ruiz, wipes away tears as attorney Ben Crump speaks at a news conference on July 24 in Madison, Wisconsin ( AP )

The incident sparked immediate outrage, leading to widespread protests and calls for police reform. At a news conference following the shooting, Ruiz’s mother, Elsa Ruiz, tearfully remembered her son as a devoted father.

“He was my love,” she said. “He loved his daughter, he loved his family. He did not deserve to be taken out like that. They took my baby from me.”

City officials have urged the public to remain calm while state authorities complete their investigation.

“What remains true is that the occupation of the intersection is neither a safe nor a sustainable solution for the unhoused or the surrounding community,” Rhodes-Conway said in her statement. “It cannot make the independent investigation move faster or change state law.”

News.title: Norwich City renews partnership with BetWright ahead of 2026/27 season
News.content:
Championship club Norwich City has announced the renewal of its partnership with gambling brand BetWright ahead of the 2026/27 season.

BetWright featured as the sponsor on the back of the men's first-team shorts last season, and both parties have decided to renew their agreement “following a successful first campaign as principal partner”, according to a statement on the club website.

The brand was launched in 2024 by Onyx Gaming Ltd., and runs both online bookmaker and online casino sections. As part of the agreement, BetWright branding will also feature across the club's partner section, alongside a programme of fan-focused activations, dedicated social media activity and more.

Ed Turnham, commercial director at Norwich City, said that the club is “pleased to extend our partnership with BetWright ahead of the 2026/27 season”, explaining: “The relationship has grown considerably during our first season together and we're excited to continue building on that success.

“We look forward to seeing the BetWright logo on our men's first team kit again, as well as supporting our purpose driven mission,” he added.

“Norwich is a club that gives back to its city, and we want our partnership to reflect that on and off the pitch,” said BetWright’s chief marketing officer Yarry Troshchey.

“Year one was about introducing ourselves to the Canaries faithful. Year two is about building on it. We've learned a lot about what resonates with this fanbase, and we've got bigger plans for the season ahead - on the community side especially,” he added.

The renewal is the latest in a string of football clubs agreeing sponsorship deals with betting brands, with Premier League side Leeds United having recently announced their own deal with Irish brand Boyle Sports.

New research is revealing more about the planet Neptune than we ever knew – including shining light on a huge celestial disaster that ‘destroyed ancient worlds’.

A catastrophe occurred on the solar system’s outermost planet billions of years ago in which a Pluto-sized interloper caused chaos, observations from NASA's James Webb Space Telescope show.

Scientists looked at the composition of three of Neptune's small inner moons — Proteus, Larissa and Galatea — and ⁠its inner dusty rings, and detected clay minerals that one might expect to find deep inside certain worlds in the outer reaches of the solar system.

These magnesium-rich minerals are known to exist on the dwarf planet Ceres, which orbits in the main asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter, and in some meteorites. "These minerals require prolonged contact between liquid water and rock to form," said planetary scientist Ryleigh Davis, a postdoctoral researcher at the University of California, San Diego, and lead author of the study published in the journal Science Advances.

"The ⁠moons themselves are far too small and cold for that chemistry to have occurred ​in ⁠place, so the clay had to come from somewhere else — the deep interior of a much larger ancient world. Finding this material on Neptune's inner moons points to a catastrophic event in Neptune's past that destroyed those ancient worlds and exposed their deep interiors, with the small moons ⁠and rings we see today re-forming from that wreckage," said Davis, who worked on the study while at Caltech.

The researchers said the culprit ​behind this ⁠cataclysm appears to be Triton, which currently is Neptune's largest ‌moon but previously resided farther out in the solar system in a region called the Kuiper Belt. They said that sometime during the first billion or so years after the solar system's formation roughly 4.5 billion years ago — a chaotic time when the large gas planets were still migrating to their current ‌orbits — Neptune's gravitational pull captured Triton.

open image in gallery This montage of images taken by the Voyager spacecraft of the planets and four of Jupiter’s moons is set against a false-color Rosette Nebula with Earth’s moon in the foreground ( Nasa )

Triton is a bit larger than Pluto, another Kuiper Belt resident, ‌though smaller than Earth's moon.

After being captured, Triton's own gravitational forces stirred up Neptune's original moons and caused most of them to collide with each other. Neptune's current inner moons eventually formed from some of the resultant debris.

"The interiors of large icy moons are normally permanently hidden from us, buried beneath thick shells of water ice and accessible only through models and inference. Neptune's inner moons may be ⁠the only place in the solar system where we can directly observe that material, because this catastrophic event essentially turned those ancient worlds inside out," Davis said.

Triton is the solar system's only large moon that orbits in the opposite direction of its planet's spin. This fact provides further evidence that Triton was captured after forming elsewhere rather than forming as one of Neptune's original moons.

Interloper

The other three large gas planets — Jupiter, Saturn and Uranus — each has a system of large moons that formed around the planet, orbiting in a roughly circular path in the same direction that the planet rotates.

"Neptune is the only giant planet in the solar system without an ordered system of large regular satellites," Davis said. "So, Neptune ended up with a captured interloper dominating its satellite system ‌rather than the orderly family of moons we see at the other giant planets."

open image in gallery The planet Neptune, including its 'Great Dark Spot' - a storm in the atmosphere and the bright, light-blue smudge of clouds that accompanies the storm - is seen in this image taken by the NASA spacecraft Voyager 2 less than five days before its closest approach of the planet on August 25, 1989 ( Reuters )

Triton makes up more than 99% of the mass ​of Neptune's entire satellite system - its moons and rings.

Neptune, located about 30 times further from the sun than Earth is, has 16 known ‌moons. Nereid, one of Neptune's outermost moons, displays among the most ⁠elliptical orbits of any moon in the solar system. The researchers said Nereid's composition, as revealed in another study, suggests it was the ⁠sole survivor among Neptune's original moons, somehow avoiding Triton's wrath.

Triton, thought to be similar in composition to Pluto, has nitrogen ice, methane ice and carbon dioxide on its surface, as well as a thin ‌nitrogen atmosphere.

The researchers said another possible, though ​less likely, explanation for their observations is that another Pluto-sized Kuiper Belt world passed ‌too close to Neptune and was ripped apart by its gravity.

The story ​of Neptune's moons, Davis said, is a reminder that the solar system has a violent history.

"It's a vivid example of how a single random event can fundamentally alter a planetary system's architecture," Davis said.

There are many ways to spend a nice afternoon on the Isle of Man, but Noel Edmonds has, by his own admission, picked a typically “bizarre” one.

Together with his wife, the former host of Deal or No Deal took it upon himself to release store-bought lobsters into the water at Peel Harbour on the Isle of Man.

He had purchased the crustaceans earlier at a local farm shop after feeling “uncomfortable” at the sight of the crustaceans confined in the tank.

“All right, this is one of those bizarre things that happens with us,” the 77-year-old confessed in a video he shared to Instagram last week.

“We were at a place where there were some lobsters in a tank, and we’re a little bit uncomfortable about the lobsters and tanks, so we bought the lobsters and now Liz is going to release them. So here we go… nice clear water in Peel Harbour,” continued Edwards, watching on as his wife, Liz Davies, released the animals.

“Wonderful place,” he said of the spot, which is located on the west coast of the island. “And we know this is nice fresh water because a moment ago a seal went past.”

His good intentions, however, may well produce precisely the opposite effect, with some of Edmonds’ 146,000 followers chastising him for his actions.

“Lovely sentiment, but from a marine biologist perspective it's best not to release captive lobsters,” one person said, with another writing that the TV presenter has “basically killed” the captive animals by releasing them into the wild.

open image in gallery Noel Edmonds has attracted criticism over his decision to release store-bought lobsters into the Irish sea ( Noel Edmonds )

“The seals are waiting to pounce,” said a third person, while another joked: “Noel Edmonds releases lobster for it likely to be caught again.”

Edmonds’ actions did, however, prompt a moment of reflection from the owner of the farm shop where he bought the lobsters who said he is considering moving the tank to a less visible position in the shop, or removing it completely.

“I’m sensitive to people’s feelings,” Matt Harrison told local news outlet Manx Radio. “But the vast majority of people want us to keep it and for us to keep supporting small businesses, which is the whole point of the shop.”

The lobsters released by Edmonds and his wife were caught near Peel by a local shellfish fisherman, according to Harrison.

“I’m still mulling over whether to keep [the tank],” he continued. “There are still lobsters in there; they’re really healthy. We’re just going to see what happens. But customers will be able to buy it in plenty of other places along the Peel seafront.”

open image in gallery Noel Edmonds pictured with his wife Liz Davies ( ITV )

Dubbed “Lobstergate” by Edmonds’ followers, the naturelife debacle – which has caused much debate on Facebook – is just the most recent example of Edmonds’ eccentric online persona.

The TV presenter regularly shares snippets of his life on the Isle of Man with his followers on social media, including highlights such as a clip of himself wiggling his toes last year accompanied by the caption: “Good morning. Take a minute to wiggle those magical little grounding antennas at the end of your feet.”

The quirky star made his name on Deal or No Deal, of which he presented 3,000 episodes before the show came to an end in 2016, but has also had a go at various other TV formats.

Last year, he launched ITV’s Noel Edmonds’ Kiwi Adventure, which followed he and his wife as they attempted to establish a bar-restaurant in New Zealand.

News.title: The 13 best castle hotels in England
News.content:
Few places capture the imagination quite like a castle, and England is home to some of the most remarkable places to spend the night. If it’s not the romance of waking up in a canopied four-poster bed, or losing ourselves in centuries-old tapestries and visceral oil paintings, we are lured by tales of brave knights and plotting dignitaries, duplicitous royals and ghosts parleying secrets in the hallways.

Part of the magic is spending an afternoon wandering grounds and gardens followed by evenings in front of a roaring fire, or dining in a banquet hall that may have hosted medieval kings and queens. While not every castle has crenellated battlements, glistening moats or royal connections, each stony stronghold on our list has something special that makes it worth travelling for. In this modern age that might include a spa, fine-dining restaurant or extra touches like free admission to exhibitions and museum tours. Here’s our pick of the best castle hotels in England.

News.title: Careless Liverpool concede same goal twice in second-half capitulation against Leeds
News.content:
Soldier Field in Chicago hosts an all-Premier League tie encounter as Liverpool take on Leeds as both sides bring their US tours to a close. Both Premier League encounters between these sides last season ended in draws; a 3-3 draw at Elland Road was followed up by a 0-0 stalemate at Anfield. The draw at Elland Road was immediately followed by Mohamed Salah speaking to the media, claiming he had been thrown under the bus.

It is a new era at Liverpool as former Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola has replaced Arne Slot at Anfield. They kicked off the Iraola era in Nashville, Tennessee, with a 4-2 win over Sunderland, following that up with another victory in New York on Wednesday night, beating Wrexham 1-0, and will be aiming to make it three wins from three on their US tour.

“I think it [the US tour] has been really, really useful,” Iraola said in an interview on the official Liverpool website. Obviously, you spend a lot of time with the players, with the staff, you get all the information you can. And I think there is also an evolution, it has to be. We start to understand each other better, what we need to do. Every game, I hope we can get closer and closer and put ourselves in a position where the few players that still are not here start to train also, they are helped by the others.”

Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo resumed training back on Merseyside whilst Alexis Mac Allister, Alisson and Victor Munoz are yet to return to training following their World Cup exploits. The trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch are all set to feature for the first time this pre-season.

Leeds’ pre-season campaign began with a 3-2 loss to Championship Wrexham in Tampa, Florida before beating Sunderland 1-0 in New Jersey courtesy of a long-range strike from Lukas Nmecha. Former Liverpool man Harry Wilson joined Leeds on a free from Fulham this summer.

“Really tough but that is expected,” Wilson said. That is what pre-season is for, building up a base for when the season starts, making sure you are in the best physical position you can be to attack the season. It has been good. I played against them [Leeds] twice last year when I was at Fulham. Both games were really, really tough games.

“I think when the fans have got a good team to support, I think that [the atmosphere at Elland Road] goes up a notch. I think the size of the club was a massive part of me coming. Then speaking to the guys, the chairman, the sporting director, and seeing kind of the plans and the aims for the club, it is something I wanted to be a part of.”

Team news to follow shortly.

News.title: Oil plummets as Trump calls off Iran strikes
News.content:
Oil prices have plunged after Donald Trump called off strikes and said the US and Iran would hold further peace talks.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, sank as much as 9.5pc early on Monday to less than $82 a barrel after the US president said he had halted plans for “disastrous” strikes.

Mr Trump said: “Obviously, they don’t want to be attacked. They knew the extent of the attack because they saw it forming.

“Now what we’re doing is we’re talking to them in the form of a negotiation. It begins tomorrow afternoon.”

Mr ‌Trump also ordered oil companies to lower petrol prices for American ‌consumers ‌and criticised ⁠Chevron’s chief executive for not crediting his administration for supporting the fossil fuel industry.

The president said that he had been asked by Iran as well as US partners Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar to hold off on strikes. He halted plans for a major attack against Iran on Saturday, which he said would have been the biggest since the Second World War.

Mr Trump claimed the sides were on the “perimeter” of a peace deal.

Oil’s sharp fall also sent the cost of government borrowing lower on Monday over hopes that it would ease inflation.

The yield on 10-year UK gilts, a benchmark for what the Treasury pays to borrow money, dropped from 5.05pc to 4.98pc, while the equivalent US bonds dropped from 4.74pc to 4.69pc.

Stock markets in Europe also rose, with the FTSE 100 up 0.2pc, the Cac 40 in Paris up 0.3pc and the Dax in Frankfurt climbing 0.1pc.

News.title: Inside the trial for a vaccine to end malaria
News.content:
A small group of brave volunteers were given an experimental vaccine in Oxford this week in a bid to bring to an end the centuries-old scourge of malaria.

“I’m on my second vaccine now. Then I’m due to have my third vaccine soon, and then in November, I’ll be given malaria,” said an upbeat Mike Luciw, a 32-year-old local who works in recruitment.

“The hope is to help find something that could save millions of people.”

There are already two licenced vaccines for malaria but the new Oxford “RH5” shot is not like anything that has come before.

The existing jabs only act against malaria as it moves towards the liver in the early stage of infection, and provide only partial protection.

The new combination vaccine, in contrast, is designed to fight it off both at the liver stage and in the wider bloodstream, effectively knocking it out altogether.

The project is being run by the husband and wife team of Simon Draper, Professor of Vaccinology and Translational Medicine at the University of Oxford, and Professor Angela Minassian, an infectious disease specialist and clinical lead for their malaria programme in Oxford’s Department of Paediatrics.

“The dream for malaria … has been to have these two lines of defence, liver and blood, so if the first line fails, you’ve got a second,” says Prof Draper, who leads on the science.

“Our dream is to have a vaccine that gives over 90 per cent efficacy in African children,” adds Prof Minassian, who heads the clinical trials for the new jab.

News.title: Dowman weaves his magic and new signing shines as Arsenal hit ground running
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage for this pre-season friendly between Girona and Arsenal at Estadi Montilivi in Catalonia.

With the transfer speculation surrounding Vinícius Júnior’s and Bruno Guimaraes’ potential moves to Arsenal ramping up, the reigning Premier League champions are in action against Girona as they step up their preparations ahead of the upcoming campaign.

Unlike other Premier League heavyweights, Arsenal have kept their pre-season tour relatively local with a selection of games in Spain, Ireland and England, before they face Manchester City in the FA Community Shield on August 16 at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff.

Arsenal beat League One side MK Dons 3-0 in a behind-closed-doors friendly on July 25 at the Sobha Realty Training Centre, thanks to goals from Reiss Nelson, Ethan Nwaneri and Ceadach O’Neill.

After featuring in this victory and setting up Nelson for the opener, Christos Tzolis will be looking to continue his positive momentum with his new club, after joining Arsenal for £34m earlier this summer. Many fans will be keeping a close eye on the recently-signed winger given that various core members of last season’s Premier League-winning squad are yet to return from their post-World Cup breaks, having progressed deep in the competition.

Tournament winners David Raya, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino, Norway captain Martin Odegaard, as well as England internationals Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke are all missing for this game, while France’s William Saliba is out injured and set for an extended period on the sidelines.

Those who exited the World Cup earlier than the aforementioned players, including Gabriel Magalhaes, Gabriel Martinelli, Piero Hincapie, Kai Havertz, and Viktor Gyokeres, have all joined up with the squad in northern Spain.

Mikel Arteta’s men will play a wounded Girona, who suffered relegation from the top flight of Spanish football last season due to a 19th-place finish.

Kick-off is at 19:00, with team news arriving shortly.

News.title: Josh Kerr turns ‘race of the century’ into one-sided show of power
News.content:
“It means everything – absolutely incredible,” said Kerr, who joined the rendition of Flower of Scotland before closing his eyes to soak up the moment in a stadium where he had competed as a child in even the shot put.

“To do it in front of a Scottish crowd, where I learned how to race, doesn’t get any better,” he added. “I came here week after week growing up as a kid. This was the championship of my season with the world indoors and going after the record. This was on the calendar before any of that. I think a British crowd deserved more from me and I owed them that.”

Of the tactics compared to his world record, where he had to hold an even pace throughout, Kerr stressed the importance of staying calm and not being tempted into pushing too soon. “London was a big stress, pushing my body to the extreme limit,” he said. “Doing a championship race is a nice clean slate; using your brain instead of your body. It’s how I love to race.

“When you’re running that slow, your job is not to waste energy and I did that. I knew an opportunity would open up. Then it was about staying awake and alive and trying to get some space. felt like I had plenty of gears left in me.”

Kerr had emerged to a huge home ovation and, with the Proclaimers booming out as the runners completed the first two laps, he was content to stay in the pack even as Myers followed. There was then only one brief moment of concern as the runners began gathering themselves during the penultimate lap and Kerr became momentarily boxed in.

News.title: Exciting young talent JJ Gabriel makes debut as Man Utd beat Atletico Madrid
News.content:
Manchester United 2 Atletico Madrid 1

JJ Gabriel showed glimpses of his potential as he made his Manchester United debut in their 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid in Stockholm.

The 15-year-old may have been introduced with only eight minutes remaining, but, given how highly rated he is, it was a significant move by Michael Carrick to give him game time in the senior team.

There were hints of why Gabriel is so well regarded during those eight minutes, as he found space in the centre of the pitch and linked well with Leny Yoro. But he was also on the receiving end of some physical challenges – something he will have to grow accustomed to the more he plays at senior level.

Yoro, who himself made his senior debut as a 16-year-old for Lille, was impressed by Gabriel and said: “He’s a really good player. He is still really young and still has a lot to learn and a lot to improve on but he’s really humble and still working, so I’m happy for him to get his first minutes. I hope, for him, it’s going to continue like that.”

News.title: City fire blanks in shoot-out as Maresca’s opening game ends in defeat by Inter
News.content:
Manchester City 1 Inter Milan 1; Inter win 3-1 on pens

Manchester City lost the Asahi Super Dry Trophy 3-1 on a penalty shoot-out against Inter Milan.

Enzo Maresca took charge of the Premier League runners-up for the first time since his arrival as Pep Guardiola’s replacement, though he was without many of his stars who had yet to return from World Cup duty.

One of the players missing was Elliot Anderson, the £116m signing from Nottingham Forest, though Jeremy Monga, 16, was an unused substitute after being brought in from Leicester City in the summer transfer window.

City took the lead on 14 minutes through Divin Mubamba as he tapped in an Antoine Semenyo cross, but Inter’s experienced defender Benjamin Pavard levelled just six minutes later when City failed to clear a corner.

The Premier League side dominated possession in the second half after an even first 45 minutes but could not find a way through. Phil Foden, the captain, was again underwhelming after a difficult year last season, but with the season still to come he had plenty of time to show his best form once more after signing a new contract at the Etihad.

The game went to penalties after full-time with no extra time played, and only Claudio Echeverri held his nerve for City as Inter Milan scored three of theirs, Matteo Lavelli netting the winning spot-kick.

Both teams learnt little from the match as Inter made 11 changes and City eight, though Maresca will have been impressed by Ryan McAidoo’s performance as a second-half substitute, as he regularly threatened from the right wing. The 18-year-old forward will surely be in demand from other clubs looking to loan him, and City may yet be tempted to keep him around for the coming season.

Sports.title: Chelsea confirm shock free transfer for Jordan Henderson, 36, weeks after freak England injury
Sports.content:
JORDAN HENDERSON has completed a shock move to Chelsea – and revealed the chance to head to Stamford Bridge was impossible to ignore.

The Blues tempted the midfielder, 36, away from Brentford after boss Xabi Alonso prioritised bringing in more experience.

And Chelsea quickly agreed personal terms with Henderson when they firmed up their interest in a free transfer.



The one-time Premier League title winner, who has penned a two-year deal, has revealed he could not snub the Blues’ advances.



Henderson said: “Given the size of the club, the manager, who I have great admiration for, and the quality of the players, this was a huge opportunity I couldn’t turn down.

“I was also so impressed with how much the ownership want Chelsea to be successful and move in the right direction.

“For me, it’s about giving everything every single day, both on and off the field, to help the players around me and the team as much as possible. I’m very excited to get going.”

Henderson, who has made a whopping 463 Premier League appearances, suffered a freak injury while at the World Cup with England last month.

The Liverpool icon lost his footing when attempting to climb over the advertising hoardings following the Three Lions’ stunning win over tournament co-hosts Mexico.

He landed awkwardly on his left forearm and had his World Cup cut short after being forced to go under the knife.

Henderson notched 32 top flight outings as Brentford narrowly missed out on European qualification last season.



And he is desperate to challenge for silverware after lifting a trophy EIGHT times during his time on Liverpool’s books.

Alonso recently revealed his push to land Henderson and Danny Welbeck, who joined last week, came after wanting the ideal blend of youth and experience.

He said: “You need the right balance of personalities, of maturity stages, early twenties with early thirties and in between, players in different stages of their careers.

“There’s not a formula for that, but there is a feeling for that.

“For me, this is as important as tactics. First it is the team spirit. After it is playing good football. After it is winning games.



“I felt much more responsible for the team than in my earlier years as a player.

“I wanted to not just think about myself but think about my team-mates and about how we were going to play and about supporting the young players.”

Football nut

Sports.title: Champions League winner’s son makes Barcelona debut aged 18, 28 years after dad’s first game for club
Sports.content:
THE Kluivert family’s Catalonian legacy continued after Patrick’s son Shane made his official Barcelona bow against Birmingham City.

Almost 28 years after Dutch legend Patrick Kluivert first pulled on the Blaugrana shirt, his youngest son has followed suit at the tender age of 18.



Father Patrick netted 122 times for the Catalan giants and tasted La Liga glory in his debut season, before passing the Barcelona baton on to his offspring.

Shane has long been a known talent on the wing, and was scouted by Barcelona‘s iconic La Masia academy in 2017.



A first sponsorship deal with Nike swiftly followed when Kluivert was just nine years old – making him the only European athlete under ten with a clothing contract at the time.

Hansi Flick gifted the versatile attacker the opportunity to strut his stuff with the first team this summer after he racked up six goals and an assist for Barcelona’s Juvenil and Atletic sides last season.



Another of his father’s former clubs, Ajax, where he won the Champions League, were also reportedly sniffing around for Shane’s signature earlier this year, but he opted to extend his contract in Catalonia until 2028.

Hopes that Kluivert would have a dream debut were ultimately dashed however.

Birmingham City held Barcelona to a 2-2 draw at St Andrew’s, before the Blues triumphed 3-2 on penalties as hometown boy Jude Bellingham watched on.

Shane’s unofficial debut proved more reminiscent of his father’s exploits for Barca, with daily sports newspaper Mundo Deportivo quick to hail the attacking starlet as “one of La Masia’s most promising talents”.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The Kluiverts are starting to build a serious football dynasty, with three of Patrick’s sons now playing for Europe’s top teams.

Attacking midfielder Justin Kluivert recently featured at the World Cup for the Oranje and will form a critical part of Bournemouth’s Europa League campaign next season.

Meanwhile, his younger sibling Ruben has pedigree of his own as a pacy centre back, and recently helped Lyon qualify for the Champions League.

Sports.title: England Lionesses hero Ella Toone takes to sauna in blue bikini as she enjoys Lake District getaway with husband
Sports.content:
ELLA TOONE chilled out in the sauna in a blue bikini as she enjoyed some downtime in the Lake District ahead of the WSL season.

The Lionesses star is taking a break from football with Manchester United not in Women’s Super League action until September.



And the 26-year-old took the opportunity to kick back with a spa retreat alongside partner Joe Bunney.

The newlyweds travelled to the Lake District to relax at the Low Wood Bay resort and spa.



The midfielder worked up a sweat in the sauna as she uploaded a picture of herself in the bikini on Instagram.

She then snapped herself smiling with Joe outside as they took a dip in a hot tub.

Toone was later seen relaxing on a sofa bed wearing an LED light therapy face mask.

And they had more chillout time together as they took a selfie while wearing their dressing gowns.

She posted the pictures online and wrote in the caption: “Thank you for having us @lowwoodbay.”

Fans raved about her appearance the comments as one said: “You look gorgeous.”



Another wrote: “Lovely photos.”

Ella and Joe only tied the knot last month in a lavish countryside party.

The pair wed in the grounds of private country estate Colshaw Hall in Cheshire.



Ella – who had England team-mate Alessia Russo as her maid of honour – wore a classic cowl neck dress.

Former EFL footballer Joe looked very dapper in a white tux, black bow toe and waistcoat.

Toone joined United in 2018 and won the FA Cup with the team in 2024.

She has also picked up 69 caps for England, helping Sarina Wiegman‘s side win back-to-back European Championships in 2022 and 2025.

Sports.title: Yan Diomande’s transfer to Real Madrid ‘being held up by lawsuit from forgotten ex-Premier League star’
Sports.content:
YAN DIOMANDE’S blockbuster move to Real Madrid has reportedly hit an unexpected snag – with forgotten former Premier League winger Max Gradel at the centre of the row.

The highly-rated Ivory Coast youngster is on the verge of completing a dream switch from RB Leipzig to the Spanish giants.



But the transfer has reportedly been delayed by a legal dispute over who is entitled to represent the player.

Former Bournemouth winger Max Gradel, through his agency Maxidel Management, has filed a complaint with Fifa claiming it had an existing agreement with Diomande.



However, global agency Roc Nation Sports, founded by rap superstar Jay-Z-currently represents the winger and handled negotiations with Real Madrid.

Maxidel alleges Roc Nation breached its agreement with the player by negotiating the deal despite the agency’s existing contract with Diomande.

The agency previously arranged Diomande’s move from Leganes to RB Leipzig and claims it remains the player’s legitimate representative.

The dispute has now reached Fifa and could temporarily delay the completion of one of the summer‘s biggest transfers.

Under Fifa regulations, unresolved disputes involving player representation can affect the processing of an International Transfer Certificate, which is required to complete an international transfer.

Real Madrid are understood to believe they have done nothing wrong and were unaware of the disagreement between the two agencies.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The Spanish giants expect to be cleared of any wrongdoing but must now wait for Fifa’s review before the deal can be fully completed.

One possible outcome is that Diomande is granted provisional registration while the dispute over agency commissions is resolved.

Almost every other part of the transfer has reportedly already been agreed, including the transfer fee with Leipzig, the payment structure and the player’s long-term contract at the Bernabeu.

The final obstacle is Fifa’s investigation into the competing claims.



WHO IS MAX GRADEL?

Football fans will remember Gradel from his spell with Bournemouth after joining the Cherries from Saint-Etienne in 2015.

The Ivory Coast international struggled to make an impact in the Premier League before later moving to Toulouse after loan spells away from the south coast.

Following his playing career, Gradel moved into football management and player representation, launching Maxidel Management.

The agency has since built a growing client list, with Diomande regarded as one of its standout young talents.

Maxidel has even pinned a photograph of Diomande signing for RB Leipzig to the top of its Instagram page, highlighting the role it says it played in securing the move.



JAY-Z LINK

Roc Nation entered the picture more recently after Diomande joined the agency’s roster.

The company, headed by music icon Jay-Z, boasts a number of elite football clients and has a particularly strong presence in Brazil.

During his post-World Cup holiday in the United States, Diomande visited Roc Nation’s New York headquarters and attended a show at Yankee Stadium as a guest of Jay-Z.

The invitation was arranged by Roc Nation Sports president Michael Yormark, while Jay-Z had also greeted the player pitchside during the World Cup.



It was Roc Nation that conducted negotiations with Real Madrid.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Now, both the Spanish giants and Diomande are waiting for FIFA to resolve the disagreement before the transfer can finally be completed.

Until then, the winger remains with RB Leipzig as he waits for the green light to complete his move to Madrid.

Sports.title: Arsenal wonderkid, 16, posts five-word message as he bids Emirates Stadium farewell to join Newcastle
Sports.content:
TEENAGE talent Kyran Thompson has broken his silence after snubbing a new deal at Arsenal to join Newcastle.

The Gunners were desperate to convince the winger, 16, to pen scholarship terms when arch-rivals Tottenham were pushing to lure him away.



But Newcastle have won the race for Thompson’s signature despite boss Eddie Howe’s resignation leaving the Magpies in limbo.

And the highly-rated youngster headed onto social media to post a five-word statement as he bids farewell to the Emirates Stadium.



In an Instagram post, alongside an image which said goodbye, Thompson wrote: “Thank you for everything, Arsenal.”

The up-and-coming gem trained with the Gunners’ senior squad, after catching the eye of chief Mikel Arteta.

He also featured regularly for Arsenal’s Under-18s before his agreement expired at the end of last month.

Thompson, who was plucked from West Ham two years ago, was even rewarded with his Under-21s debut in a draw with Southampton last November.

But now the wonderkid will be looking to make an instant impact in Newcastle’s youth ranks.

Matthias Jaissle, who is poised to replace Howe in the Tyneside giants’ dugout, is on course to run the rule over Thompson.



Arsenal are hoping Magpies skipper Bruno Guimaraes is set to head in the opposite direction.

The Brazilian, 28, is ready to request a move to North London after jetting into Newcastle’s pre-season training camp.

And Arsenal are lining up a £75million-plus bid for Guimaraes, who was pinpointed as a top transfer target by Arteta.

Newcastle appear to be preparing for his exit after reportedly removing banners around St James’ Park showing him posing in the club’s new kit.



Guimaraes made 41 appearances in all competitions last season, notching nine goals and eight assists along the way.

The midfielder then played a key role in Brazil’s World Cup campaign before they crashed out against Norway in the last-16.

Sports.title: Man Utd wonderkid JJ Gabriel, 15, BLOCKED from changing with team-mates in dressing room this season
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED starlet JJ Gabriel will be blocked from getting dressed in the first-team changing room this season.

The 15-year-old prodigy was forced to get dressed alone and away from Michael Carrick‘s squad before stepping out for his senior debut against Atletico Madrid.



Strict Premier League and club safeguarding rules mean Gabriel must change separately down the corridor from the main Old Trafford dressing room this season.

Gabriel turns 16 in October, so he is officially able to make his Prem bow this term, despite not being able to sign a pro deal until he turns 17 next year.



Prem regulations state that any player under 18 must suit up away from the senior squad for both training sessions and matchdays.

The teenager will be allowed back into the dressing room to hear Carrick’s team talks once all of his team-mates are dressed.



Although it doesn’t affect Gabriel and United because they are sponsored by Snapdragon, regulations also mean that players Under-18 cannot wear betting sponsors on their kits.

Gabriel was subbed on alongside midfielder Jim Thwaites in the 82nd minute of United’s 2-1 win over Atletico in Stockholm on Saturday.

The wonderkid now has the chance, however slim, to become United’s youngest EVER player when the League Cup kicks off in September.

His bow against Atletico didn’t count officially, meaning David Gaskell’s 1956 record — set under Sir Matt Busby at 16 years and 19 days old — still stands.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Arsenal‘s Max Dowman was similarly fast-tracked and had to change away from Mikel Arteta‘s Prem winning squad last season.

Gabriel has played above his age for England’s Under-17s already amd is gearing up for a potential adult appearance by hitting the gym.

United promised Gabriel a first-team pathway when club chiefs, including director of football Jason Wilcox, personally convinced him to stay last summer amid interest from Barcelona.

The youngster went onto win the Under-18 Premier League player of the season last term despite only being 14 when the campaign began.



He was first called up to Carrick’s matchday squad for United’s trip to Trondheim, where he was an unused sub.

Gabriel was a stand-out performer last term, scoring 29 times in 32 appearances, helping them reach the FA Youth Cup and Under-18 cup finals.

Sports.title: Newcastle appear to remove all reference to Bruno Guimaraes from St James’ Park as Arsenal transfer edges closer
Sports.content:
NEWCASTLE UNITED have seemingly removed all mention of Bruno Guimaraes from St James’ Park amid his Arsenal transfer links.

The Brazilian midfielder has been heavily linked with a move to the Premier League champions this summer.



And it seems that a deal may finally be progressing, with reports emerging of contact being made between the clubs for the 28-year-old.

And if news wasn’t bad enough for Magpies fans, it now seems the club have taken the step of removing his likeness from their home stadium.



Banners showing the star posing in the club’s new kit have reportedly been replaced by banners with other stars, per The Mag.

The move could be a coincidence, with advertising materials prone to being changed by the club at any time.



But fans holding out hope for another year of Guimaraes in midfield are growing concerned that the change could signal his imminent departure.

The Brazil international is believed to have expressed his desire to leave the club this window during their pre-season preparations.

The transfer saga was not helped by the sudden departure of Eddie Howe last week.

The boss shared a strong relationship with Guimaraes, who penned a heartfelt letter to the coach after his exit.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Guimaraes, who captains the North East side, would be a huge problem for Newcastle this late in the window.

New coach Matthias Jaissle is expected to take over in the near future, but he will already have a significant rebuild on his hands and very little time.

Guimaraes’ departure would follow on from Sandro Tonali‘s move to Tottenham Hotspur, leaving a hole in the midfield.

And Anthony Gordon‘s switch to Barcelona has also given him a headache in attack.

Sports.title: Ex-Premier League star blocks £113m Real Madrid transfer as FIFA receive complaint
Sports.content:
Ex-Premier League star blocks £113m Real Madrid transfer as FIFA receive complaint

Max Gradel, the ex-Bournemouth winger, has filed a complaint to FIFA that has thrown Yan Diomande's reported £113million move to Real Madrid into doubt

View 2 Images Real Madrid have reportedly agreed a deal to sign RB Leipzig star Yan Diomande (Image: (Photo by Stuart Franklin/Getty Images))

Former Premier League winger Max Gradel has filed a compliant to FIFA regarding Yan Diomande's proposed £113million move to Real Madrid.

‌



Diomande, 19, who is viewed as one of the most exciting attacking talents in world football, has agreed a club-record deal to join Jose Mourinho's Madrid side this summer. The Ivory Coast international netted 13 goals and added 10 assists in 36 matches for RB Leipzig last season and appears destined for Los Blancos.

‌



But the transfer has run into a major stumbling block due to a legal dispute over representation rights, according to AS and Defensa Central. Real Madrid struck the deal with Roc Nation, the sports agency founded by rapper and businessman Jay-Z, under the belief they were Diomande's sole representatives.

‌



Liverpool transfer need brutally exposed as Leeds stun Andoni Iraola - 5 talking points READ MORE :

Ex-Man Utd star tipped for bright future by Alex Ferguson speaks out on being clubless READ MORE :

However, Maxidel Management, headed up by ex-Bournemouth, Leeds United and Leicester City forward Gradel, have launched a lawsuit to FIFA alleging a breach of contract. Maxidel brokered Diomande's switch from Leganes to Leipzig last summer and maintain they hold his rights until he departs the German club.

The dispute has brought the deal to a grinding halt, despite Diomande previously being on the verge of putting pen to paper on a five-year contract at the Santiago Bernabeu.

Real Madrid are said to be absolutely furious over the situation, feeling misled by the lack of transparency throughout negotiations. Having reached a broad agreement with Roc Nation, the sudden emergence of Maxidel's claim has thrown serious complications into the mix.

‌



Ivorian journalist Malick Traore shed light on the club's frustrations, saying: "Real Madrid are angry with Diomande's representatives at Roc Nation, after discovering that the player is still tied to a contract with other agents."

View 2 Images Former Premier League star Max Gradel has put a halt on Yan Diomande's move to Real Madrid (Image: Getty Images)

The fury is aimed solely at Roc Nation, not at Diomande himself. Real Madrid now face a precarious predicament, as settling a commission with the incorrect agent could trigger severe sanctions from FIFA.

‌



Gradel, 38, started his senior career at Leicester and made his breakthrough during the Foxes' League One title-winning season in 2008/09, scoring some important goals including an equaliser in a 2-2 draw at MK Dons.

He went on to leave Leicester in 2009 and join Leeds on loan and then on a permanent deal. He played a pivotal role in propelling the Whites to promotion from League One before delivering the standout campaign of his career in the Championship, netting 18 times across 41 appearances.

That impressive spell secured him a transfer to Saint-Etienne in Ligue 1, where he remained for four seasons before heading back to England with a Premier League switch to Bournemouth. Gradel subsequently turned out for Toulouse, Sivasspor and Gaziantep before transitioning into life as a football agent.

Sports.title: Frank Lampard green lights £89m Chelsea transfer reunion after signing son of ex-teammate
Sports.content:
Frank Lampard green lights £89m Chelsea transfer reunion after signing son of ex-teammate

Frank Lampard's Coventry City have enquired about facilitating a reunion for the Chelsea icon by making contact over a current Blues star

View 2 Images Frank Lampard is looking to equip his team for the Premier League (Image: Pete Norton/Getty Images)

Frank Lampard could be set for a reunion with Mykhailo Mudryk after Coventry City made contact with Chelsea about his availibility. The newly-promoted side are one of three Premier League sides to have reached out.

‌



Lampard coached the Ukrainian winger during his spell in charge of the Blues in 2023 and now has the possibility of utilising his services once again but in more positive circumstances. The Chelsea icon led Coventry to the Championship title last season in his first role since a difficult second stint in the Stamford Bridge dugout when he replaced Graham Potter on an interim basis.

‌



Mudryk, meanwhile, has made his return to football, having not played since November 2024 against Heidenheim. The 25-year-old tested positive for meldonium but the FA has now ended its anti-doping proceedings after Mudryk accepted breaching anti-doping rules.

‌



The parties agreed to a suspension equal to the one year and eight months already served by the ex-Shahktar Donetsk player. His return has led to no shortage of interest, with three Premier League teams and three more from Europe making contact about Mudryk's future.

The Chelsea speedster, who signed for the Blues in a deal worth up to £88.5m, is in Hong Kong with the west London side as Chelsea's pre-season tour continues. Xabi Alonso gave little away about Murdyk's future.

Alejandro Garnacho takes brutal swipe at Chelsea immediately after Aston Villa debut READ MORE :

Chelsea squad's immediate reaction to Mykhailo Mudryk bombshell and imminent return READ MORE :

"We need to see," he said. "It's too early to tell, to see how he is in terms of fitness, in terms of this game time that you need to be involved again, so it's still early to tell."

‌



"We can expect that [it will take longer to get back to full fitness and sharpness]," Alonso added. "We have the Mudryk that [we had], it will take time, but once there is a change, things start moving, and for him it's a massive change.

"So he trained on his own every day, and I think it had to be really, really hard, because he wanted to play football, he wanted to be part of a team, and he was not allowed to do that for such a long time.

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



View 2 Images Mykhaylo Mudryk has not played for Chelsea since November 2024. (Image: Sebastian Widmann - UEFA, UEFA via Getty Images)

"So once this big change has happened, now things will move on, and afterwards we will see if it's quicker, if it's slower, but we need to be aware of that."

It comes after Coventry added to Lampard's squad over the weekend. Teenage goalkeeper Jack Ruddy joined Coventry from Norwich.

Article continues below

Ruddy is the son of former Norwich and Newcastle United shotstopper John Ruddy, who left the Magpies at the end of last season. Lampard was team-mates with Ruddy senior on the international stage with both selected for England in 2021 for a win over Italy.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino and Donald Trump meeting not happening as third nation calls out FIFA boss
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino and Donald Trump meeting not happening as third nation calls out FIFA boss

Gianni Infantino's future as FIFA President has been the subject of speculation following the failed FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposals

View 2 Images FIFA President Gianni Infantino is under immense pressure (Image: Alex Pantling/FIFA via Getty Images)

Gianni Infantino has not scheduled a call with members of Donald Trump's Cabinet in a bid to save his FIFA job, the Mirror has been told. Claims that the under-fire FIFA president requested a call where he was reportedly set to appeal for support have also been denied by the US government.

‌



Infantino’s future as FIFA President has been a topic of speculation ever since controversial proposals emerged, which would have seen the federation sell shares in its major tournaments, including the men’s and women’s World Cups, as well as the Club World Cup.

‌



FIFA have since confirmed that the plans, which were named the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), have been dropped after the widespread criticism which has followed.

‌



As a result, speculation has been swirling about Infantino’s future as FIFA President, with the New York Post now reporting that a meeting has been arranged with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

Leandro Paredes sparks uproar for unsportsmanlike act weeks after World Cup final ‘punch’ READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino was set to earn huge salary from World Cup plan as staggering figure revealed READ MORE :

Mirror Football understands that, despite the recent reports, no meeting is scheduled to take place between Infantino and members of the Trump administration, including the US Secretary of State.

Assistant Secretary of State for Global Public Affairs Dylan Johnson has written in a post on X, formerly known as Twitter, to deny that such a meeting is taking place between Rubio and Infantino.

‌



England and Wales have already called for a leadership change at FIFA, with both nations withdrawing their support for Infantino’s re-election bid as President.

Serbia recently became the latest country to withdraw their support for Infantino to be re-elected as FIFA President.

In a statement released on Monday, they said: "We recall that FA of Serbia formally expressed its support for Mr Infantino in writing on 25 May this year, but after a thorough consideration of the developments that have seriously undermined the reputation and credibility of both FIFA and its President in the past period, this is the only logical and rational move.

‌



View 2 Images FIFA President Gianni Infantino said the controversial FFE proposal will not proceed (Image: VCG via Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"Football Association of Serbia is of the opinion that the future of world football must be founded on transparency, dialogue, mutual respect, and partner relations among all confederations and national associations.

‌



"We believe that no decision of strategic importance for the future of football should be made without broad consensus and open consultation with all relevant stakeholders.

"Football Association of Serbia remains committed to cooperation with FIFA, UEFA, and all national associations for the purpose of development and improvement of football, but is also of the opinion that at this moment a new trust is needed, as well as a new approach, and management that will contribute to restoring dialogue, unity, and the credibility of international football institutions."

Sports.title: Vinicius Jr to Arsenal transfer hint as key figure flies into London
Sports.content:
Vinicius Jr to Arsenal transfer hint as key figure flies into London

Vinicius Junior might have reported back to Real Madrid for pre-season training, but he is still the subject of growing speculation over a transfer to Arsenal

View 3 Images Vinicius Junior is being eyed for a blockbuster move to Arsenal (Image: (Antonio Villalba/Real Madrid via Getty Images))

Vinicius Jr continues to be linked with a move to Arsenal - and now the president of the agency that represents him has confirmed he is going to be in London. The Gunners have launched a stunning move to sign the Real Madrid star, as Mikel Arteta looks to add some quality to his title-winning squad.

Vinicius, who reported back to Real on Monday for pre-season training, has scored 128 goals in 375 appearances for the La Liga giants, who are keen to keep hold of him this summer. So much so that they have been trying to renew his deal for a number of months now.

The Brazilian's deal expires next summer, and Real opened further talks with him last week in a bid to reach an agreement. But with nothing forthcoming, the La Liga giants have informed the 26-year-old’s camp that the latest contract offer they submitted is final and there will be no further increase or another round of negotiations.

‌



If Vinicius accepts, his deal will be renewed; however, if he rejects the offer, Madrid will open the door to a sale this summer to prevent the Brazilian from entering his final year of contract and leaving for free later, according to Spanish publication Marca.

But now, in an interesting development, the president of Roc Nation Sports confirmed on Monday morning that he is travelling to London. Michael R. Yormark took to Instagram to post an update saying: “London, here I come. Let’s go!”

Arsenal receive immediate response after finally submitting first Bruno Guimaraes offer READ MORE :

Mikel Arteta sends Vinicius Jr transfer message ahead of Real Madrid meeting READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

View 3 Images Michael R. Yormark's post on Instagram

Amid the speculation around the attacker’s Real future, Roc Nation took the unusual step on Sunday by hitting out at 'fake and damaging' reports in a statement shared by Yormark on Instagram. It's not clear whether Roc Nation were speaking about Vinicius and the ongoing rumours surrounding a Real Madrid exit and a move to Arsenal or something else.

But the statement said: "Roc Nation Sports International and our entire team cannot stand idle when unprofessional and uninformed media publish fake and damaging information for attention-seeking purposes.

‌



"This is especially unacceptable when it personally targets our clients without any foundation. It is disruptive, harmful and libellous. Media outlets and journalists need to hold themselves more accountable."

The Gunners have already bolstered their attacking options this summer with the £34million signing of Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge earlier this month. And as well as Vinicius, they're also working on a deal to sign Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle United, but have seen their opening offer rejected.

View 3 Images Christos Tzolis in action for Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

‌



And speaking over the weekend, Gunners boss Arteta admitted: "A lot is happening. We all know about the context of this transfer window.

"From ownership to the board, the sporting director and myself, we know that we want to take this club to a different level. That is going to require a better squad, better individuals.

"We have identified where we have opportunities to grow and to improve and to evolve our game and what is going to be needed to achieve that. Hopefully, very soon we can start to put things in a very concrete way."

Sports.content:
Jack Grealish 'offered incredible transfer' after making spiky Man City statement

Manchester City star Jack Grealish has been absent from the club's pre-season tour and is being linked with a move away from Enzo Maresca's side this summer

View 2 Images Jack Grealish could be on the move again this summer (Image: David Davies/PA Wire)

Atletico Madrid are reportedly considering a shock summer move for Manchester City star Jack Grealish. The forward has been left out of City’s tour of Asia, revealing on social media that he is recovering from a long-term injury.

‌



Grealish returned to the Etihad Stadium this summer following a loan spell at Premier League rivals Everton. The former £100million man spent last season with the Toffees, but saw his contributions limited after picking up a foot injury.

‌



Saudi Pro League side Al Hilal are reportedly considering a move. The Middle Eastern club have already raided West Ham for Crysencio Summerville, and Grealish is now on their radar as they eye quality on the flanks.

‌



Jack Grealish could take unlikely Man City exit route as record transfer snubbed READ MORE :

Jamie Carragher teams up with Gary Neville for star-studded charity gala READ MORE :

But Al Hilal are reportedly not the only team interested in City's former treble-winning star. The Sun claim that Spanish La Liga side Atletico are looking at a possible deal.

It is claimed that the Atleti hierarchy admire Grealish's work rate both in and out of possession. The reports states that he is viewed as a strong fit for manager Diego Simeone's tactical system.

FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

‌



Grealish clarified the reason for his absence during City's pre-season tour. The 30-year-old said: "Just to let you know I'm still recovering from an injury so I'm not training yet. Haven't been 'left out' so stop talking poo poo thanks."

And new City boss Enzo Maresca is still not giving up on the former Aston Villa player though. The Italian worked with Grealish when he was City's assistant manager under Pep Guardiola in the club's 2022/23 treble-winning campaign before he left that summer to become Leicester City's boss.

He said: "At the moment, he's here. He's a Man City player. I always said the same.

"In any club I join, I like to know if there are players that belong to the club. It's my duty to try to coach them.

"Jack is here. I have a good relation with Jack since I left. Also, we keep in touch, and the reason why is because he has a big heart and he's a very good guy. So this is the reason why. And then we see what happens."

Grealish has made 157 appearances for City in all since his mega-money switch from boyhood club Villa. In that time, he has scored just 17 goals but contributed to three Premier League titles and a Champions League success.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino is FINISHED as FIFA president - and it's time for one of game's greats to step up
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino is FINISHED as FIFA president - and it's time for one of game's greats to step up

Gianni Infantino's days in office are almost certainly numbered but there are no ex-players expected to put themselves forward when an election to find his successor takes place

View 3 Images Gianni Infantino is clinging on to power but his days as FIFA president are almost certainly over (Image: Getty Images)

When Gianni Infantino became president of FIFA in February, 2016, the previous incumbent sent a message. “I congratulate Gianni Infantino sincerely and warmly on his election as the new president,” wrote Sepp Blatter. "With his experience, expertise, strategic and diplomatic skills, he has all the qualities to continue my work.”

‌



You were not wrong, Sepp. He has continued your rotten work … and then some. Thankfully, Infantino’s work is now done.

‌



There is surely no scenario imaginable in which he can continue in his role. It is now just a question of how and when he goes. And it then becomes a question of who succeeds Infantino, the man whose rise to the role was greeted with widespread positivity over a decade ago.

‌



Gianni Infantino was set to earn huge salary from World Cup plan as staggering figure revealed READ MORE :

English FA follow Wales in withdrawing Gianni Infantino support after botched World Cup plot READ MORE :

“He is not a politician and he is not an ego,” said Greg Dyke, the chairman of the Football Association at the time. “FIFA has been dominated by egos for a very long time. He is the type of person who will just get on with the job.”

Don’t worry, Greg, you were not alone in being spectacularly wrong. The problem was that everyone in football was in ABB mode. Anyone But Blatter.

The same will probably be true when candidates line up to follow Infantino. The favourite for the job is Victor Montagliani, the 60-year-old Canadian who is currently the president of CONCACAF.

‌



Mattias Granstrom, FIFA’s Swedish general secretary, is very well-respected in the organisation while Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim Al Khalifa, the Asian Confederation’s president since 2013, was the candidate narrowly beaten by Infantino in 2016. These potential successors are all highly thought of in football governance circles but then so was Infantino when he took over.

View 3 Images Luis Figo once stood to be FIFA president before pulling out of the race in 2015 (Image: Getty Images)

And do not forget, Infantino still had overwhelming support from member associations right up to his scarcely believable World Cup sell-off scheme. Which surely invites doubt about whether FIFA should be run by one autocratic, football administrator. It should not.

‌



One of the positive things Infantino did was promote the FIFA Legends scheme. For a lot of the time, you felt he only did it so he could play football with famous ex-players - and sit next to them at matches - but, all the same, it is always nice to see greats of the game involved in its promotion.

Greats of the game have been involved in its administration down the years - with mixed results, it has to be said. Most notably, Michel Platini’s presidency of UEFA ended in scandal.

But the world game does not need an autocrat, an executive whose political acumen can force through unwelcome changes. The world game needs a figurehead.

‌



It needs someone who does not need the extra fame. Or the extra money, even. The organisation can be done by committee, of which FIFA has many.

View 3 Images CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani is one of the leading contenders to replace Gianni Infantino (Image: Elizabeth Ruiz Ruiz/Getty Images)

It needs a leader who is emblematic of the sport, rather than a schmoozer, a mover and shaker who wants to court the rich, powerful and famous. It does need a lawyer or a PR man or woman.

‌



When Blatter was elected for a fifth term in May, 2015, Luis Figo had originally planned to stand. He withdrew late in the contest but, for a while, he was an interesting candidate.

And he still would be, along with a whole raft of ex-players - both male and female - with a global standing. Perhaps Sir David Beckham might want to put his hand up.

But seriously, Infantino needs to go and the role needs to change. World football does not need an administrator who can become intoxicated by power - it needs a figurehead who represents everything good about the game.

Sports.title: Maguire handed Solheim Cup return as Europe's captain's picks revealed
Sports.content:
Leona Maguire has been included among Team Europe's captain's picks for next month's Solheim Cup, with Anna Nordqvist adding three more rookies to her line-up.

Maguire has featured in the last three Solheim Cups, top-scoring as an unbeaten rookie in Europe's away win over Team USA in 2021 before making further appearances in 2023 and 2024.

The 31-year-old was the highest-ranked European player in the Rolex Women's World Golf Rankings not to qualify automatically, having posted three top-10 finishes on the LPGA Tour this season but missed the cut in four of the five majors.

Image: Leona Maguire has won 8.5 points for Team Europe from 12 matches during her three previous appearances

Maguire was the only player with past Solheim Cup experience named among Nordqvist's picks, announced live on Sky Sports, with Spain's Julia Lopez Ramirez, France's Nastasia Nadaud and England's Mimi Rhodes the other selections.

Image: Team Europe's confirmed 12-player line-up for this year's Solheim Cup

"I'm really excited to be part of Team Europe again in September," Maguire said. "I love the Solheim Cup, it brings the best out of my game and I love being part of the team."

It leaves Team Europe with four debutants in their line-up to face Angela Stanford's Team USA at Bernardus Golf in the Netherlands from September 11-13, where the hosts look to regain the trophy after their 2024 loss.

Former world amateur No 1 Lopez Ramirez and Nadaud were the next two available players in the world rankings, while Rhodes claimed her pick having won three times on the Ladies European Tour last season.

"It's always been a dream and goal of mine to play in the Solheim Cup," Rhodes said. "To now be selected for the 2026 Solheim Cup is beyond anything I imagined. I'm so proud to represent Team Europe so early in my professional career."

"I think we have a good mixture of experience and we have four rookies - the most we have had in a couple of years - but the rookies are not playing like rookies. They will bring a great attitude and positivity.

"We knew coming into the year that it was going to be a little different, but different can also be good.

"The way these girls play, they are so fearless and they show up and they are ready."

Who else features for Team Europe?

Team Europe's qualification campaign ended after the AIG Women's Open on Sunday, where the top two players on the Ladies European Tour Solheim Cup points list and the next available six via the world rankings secured their spots.

Image: The eight automatic qualifiers were confirmed after the AIG Women's Open

Charley Hull topped the LET Solheim Cup points list to secure her an eighth consecutive Solheim Cup appearance, while Esther Henseleit pipped Chiara Tamburlini to second by 0.9 points after her runner-up finish at the final women's major of the year.

"I'm really happy to be part of the European Solheim Cup team again," Henseleit said. "It was a great experience last time out in the United States but I'm very excited to be in the team on European soil. With it being so close to Germany, I hope a lot of fans come out and watch."

Sweden's Maja Stark and Linn Grant return for their third consecutive Solheim Cups, with France's Celine Boutier, Spain's Carlota Ciganda and Denmark's Nanna Koerstz Madsen the others to qualify automatically.

Team USA's qualification campaign ends after the CPKC Women's Open from August 20-23, with the top seven in the Solheim Cup points list and the next two in the world rankings qualifying, before Stanford names three captain's picks later this month.
