Sports.title: Jordan Henderson's move to Chelsea confirmed: England midfielder, 36, joins Blues after ripping up Brentford contract
Sports.content:
Chelsea have confirmed their signing of Jordan Henderson on a free transfer, after Brentford allowed the 36-year-old to terminate his contract a year earlier than expected.

It comes two days after they secured the signature of Danny Welbeck, 35, from Brighton.

Between them, Henderson and Welbeck will add 863 Premier League games’ worth of experience to a changing room now overseen by new manager Xabi Alonso, 44.

Henderson said: 'Given the size of the club, the manager, who I have great admiration for, and the quality of the players, this was a huge opportunity I couldn’t turn down.

‘I was also so impressed with how much the ownership want Chelsea to be successful and move in the right direction.

‘For me, it's about giving everything every single day, both on and off the field, to help the players around me and the team as much as possible. I'm very excited to get going.’

Jordan Henderson's move to Chelsea has been confirmed after he ripped up his Brentford deal

The midfielder was all smiles as he spent the day at Chelsea's Cobham training ground

Henderson, 36, said he was ready to 'give everything every single day, on and off the field'

Alonso identified during his talks to take over Chelsea that their squad was in need of greater balance among the players. The Blues had broken Premier League records for fielding the youngest sides over the previous two seasons, but they had been criticised by fans on occasion for appearing to lack maturity on and off the pitch.

Chelsea previously targeted Granit Xhaka, the 33-year-old Sunderland captain who had worked with Alonso at Bayer Leverkusen, but were unable to get him out of the Stadium of Light. They likewise showed interest in John Stones, who has now joined Inter Milan at 32.

Yet they have now secured Henderson for free, while the fee for Welbeck is being described as ‘undisclosed’, though his cost is by no means substantial, if indeed there even is one.

Welbeck has already travelled to Hong Kong to join his new team-mates. Daily Mail Sport reported last week how Brentford were ready to sanction Henderson’s exit rather than seek a fee from Chelsea. He is still recovering from the broken arm he suffered with England at the World Cup.

These signings are concrete confirmation that Chelsea have adjusted their transfer strategy by now aiming to add experienced leaders to their squad. Previously, there had been a focus on finding younger players of potential.

Maxence Lacroix, 26 and from Crystal Palace, has already been confirmed by Chelsea for £52million. Morgan Rogers has also arrived for £117m from Aston Villa.

Sports.title: Three Premier League clubs, including a newly-promoted side, enquire over Mykhailo Mudryk after £89m Chelsea winger's doping case is resolved
Sports.content:
Chelsea have received multiple approaches about Mykhailo Mudryk from clubs following the news of his return to football – including three from the Premier League.

Coventry City, managed by Frank Lampard, who worked with Mudryk at Stamford Bridge in 2023, are believed to be among those to have enquired, sources have told Daily Mail Sport.

All options are open between Mudryk and Chelsea this summer, including whether to send him out on loan after his sudden comeback from a doping suspension.

The current plan is for the 25-year-old Ukrainian to be assessed by Xabi Alonso, having travelled to Hong Kong to join his team-mates on their pre-season tour.

Chelsea want to see where their player’s performance levels are now at, with the Ukraine international having not been involved in competitive football since November 2024. That was via his last appearance in a Conference League win away at Heidenheim in which he scored and then disappeared following his failed test.

Another option this summer would be to send Mudryk on loan to Strasbourg, their sister side in France’s Ligue 1. That would allow him to stay under the BlueCo umbrella.

Chelsea posted this picture of Myhailo Mudryk with team-mates in Hong Kong today

Coventry City, managed by Frank Lampard, who worked with Mudryk at Stamford Bridge in 2023, are believed to be among those to have enquired, sources have told Daily Mail Sport

Wingers are in-demand in this window, which may explain why so many sides are intrigued by Mudryk’s comeback, despite nobody knowing his current fitness levels. His potential was once considered so highly that Chelsea paid £89million to sign him from Shakhtar Donetsk.

Mudryk is effectively a bonus arrival for Chelsea, with Alonso having told reporters after their pre-season loss to Tottenham in Sydney how the news came as a pleasant surprise. He is set to train under Alonso and with the Chelsea squad in Hong Kong, where the club will be facing Juventus in a friendly.

They also have games in Indonesia and Malaysia which will follow, and will be hosting Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge after returning home to London.

If Mudryk was deemed ready to appear in that match, it would represent his first appearance at the Bridge since facing Arsenal in the Premier League there in November 2024. Chelsea beat Mikel Arteta’s club to secure his signature in January 2023.

Mudryk’s return to football was made possible because of a change in the way the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) measures meldonium – the substance for which he tested positive.

WADA increased the threshold by which a player is deemed to have passed the minimum reporting level, from 120 to 150 per cent. In other words, were Mudryk’s sample analysed today, he would not have been deemed to have violated the anti-doping rules.

Mudryk has now managed to come to a resolution with WADA and the Football Association, in which it has essentially been deemed he has served his time for his violation.

He has spent his suspension – described as long and lonely by sources – training almost daily in the hope of returning. That includes renting the pitch at the stadium of non-League side Uxbridge to stage sessions with a private trainer. Chelsea have been highly sympathetic to Mudryk’s situation, having believed his consistent claims of innocence ever since he tested positive.

It was believed to have occurred while he was away with the Ukraine national team in September 2024, and it was after facing Heidenheim in November 2024 that he was informed of his failed test.

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes back with Manchester United after World Cup - as Benjamin Sesko aims for return from shin injury
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes back with Manchester United after World Cup - as Benjamin Sesko aims for return from shin injury

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes is among the latest World Cup contingent to report back to the club’s Carrington headquarters for pre-season training as Michael Carrick’s squad nears full strength.

Fernandes has returned along with his Portugal team-mate Diogo Dalot and Brazil’s Matheus Cunha after reaching the last 16, while Noussair Mazraoui is also back after making it to the quarter-finals with Morocco.

The four players will have individual testing and fitness assessment in the first couple of days, and could be in the travelling squad for United’s next pre-season friendly against Paris Saint-Germain in Gothenburg on Saturday. There, Belgian duo Senne Lammens and new £35million signing Youri Tielemans may also feature after returning to training last week.

It’s unclear if Benjamin Sesko will be able to play after missing United’s first three pre-season games against Wrexham, Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid with an ongoing shin problem, although there could be an update on the Slovenia striker later on Monday.

The last group back will be England duo Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford, plus Lisandro Martinez of Argentina, who are expected to join up with the club’s training camp in Ireland where United will also play Leeds in Dublin.

The club are not expecting any issues with the thigh injury Martinez suffered before half-time in Argentina’s defeat to Spain in the World Cup final, or the back complaint that kept Mainoo out of England’s win over France in the bronze medal match, but are waiting to assess both players once they return.

BrunO Fernandes has returned to training with Manchester United after his summer break

Speaking before United beat Atletico 2-1 in Stockholm on Saturday, Carrick said: ‘We’ve got five or six coming back on Monday, and then more a week after that. The further you get in the World Cup, the less time you have off. We had a bit of a joke about that with the players before they left, that's just how it is.’

Meanwhile, Manuel Ugarte has been undergoing rehab since returning to Carrington in mid-July following surgery on the knee ligament injury he suffered in Uruguay’s group defeat to Spain.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino begs Trump for help as he fights to save his job: 'Isolated' FIFA president 'set for White House talks' after failed bid to sell World Cup
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino begs Trump for help as he fights to save his job: 'Isolated' FIFA president 'set for White House talks' after failed bid to sell World Cup

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Embattled FIFA president Gianni Infantino is reportedly set for crunch talks with the White House on Monday morning as he battles to save his job in the wake of his failed bid to sell off the World Cup to private investors.

Infantino sparked an open revolt when The Times first revealed his bombshell plans to sell a $4.2 billion (£3.1bn) stake in FIFA's flagship tournament to a private equity firm led by Joshua Kushner.

The proposals have since been scrapped after opposition from UEFA, the North, Central America and Caribbean confederation (CONCACAF) and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC).

And as Infantino battles to save his job, the New York Post has claimed that Infantino is now turning to his biggest ally - Donald Trump - to help him survive.

The paper reported that Infantino will hold a call with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio at 9am EST (2pm BST), as pressure rises on the FIFA president to resign from his role.

An insider told the Post: 'He wanted to get online with the secretary and talk about how soccer can be a form of soft power for America. But we all know that it is about job protection. It is not about anything else at this point.'

FIFA boss Gianni Infantino is in a fight to save his job after his failed bid to sell the World Cup

Infantino will reportedly hold a call with Marco Rubio (C) on Monday to ask for support

A second source described Infantino as feeling 'isolated' by the 'avalanche' of negativity surrounding his now-doomed plans. 'He is looking for allies of note to publicly support him,' they said.

The Daily Mail has reached out to FIFA and the White House for comment, while on X the Assistant Secretary of State for Global Public Affairs, Dylan Johnson, denied that a call is taking place.

He posted: 'There are no plans for [Marco Rubio] to speak with Infantino and there is no call this morning. [The New York Post] should check their sources or they could have just asked us.'

Infantino's alleged last-ditch attempt to save his presidency comes just days after Trump brutally denied all knowledge of Infantino's bold sell-off plan.

When asked 'did Mr Infantino speak to you about his proposal to sell a stake in the World Cup?' Trump brutally first replied: 'Who?'

After the question was repeated, the president then added: 'No, I didn't speak to him.'

Trump's reaction to Infantino in that Oval Office media session was a far cry from previous comments before and during the World Cup, in which he often gave a glowing review of the FIFA boss.

The Post also reports that Infantino has repeatedly tried to call Trump in the past few days, only to be met with a wall of silence from the president.

Trump brutally responded 'who?' when asked if Infantino had consulted him about his plan

Earlier on Monday, Infantino's battle to survive as FIFA president took another big hit as more nations withdrew their support for his re-election bid.

England, Wales and Finland are the latest countries to explicitly stand against Infantino's re-election, with more UEFA nations expected to follow.

Prior to his controversial sell-off plans, Infantino had reportedly been endorsed by almost all of FIFA's 211 member associations for re-election. Candidates must be put forward by November 18 and the vote will take place at FIFA's congress in March.

Infantino has been FIFA president since 2016 after replacing Sepp Blatter and is targeting a fourth term in charge.

But the events of recent days - and the controversies that blighted him before and during the World Cup - have rocked his authority.

His plans have been widely lambasted and two of his closest allies have resigned. Firstly, his senior adviser Carlos Cordeiro - who acted as FIFA's link to the White House during the tournament - stepped down, before chief operating officer Kevin Lamour lambasted the proposals.

UEFA and CONCACAF have called on Infantino to quit but their ploy to depose the Swiss football administrator hit a roadblock after Kuwait, Qatar, Sri Lanka and Lebanon reiterated their confidence in his leadership.

Joshua Kushner - brother of Jared, Donald Trump's son-in-law - was at the heart of the plans

A lot has changed since Trump and Infantino handed Spain the World Cup trophy on July 19

UEFA and CONCACAF make up 90 of FIFA's 211 member associations. Although that is above the 20 per cent threshold to trigger a vote of no confidence, it falls short of the majority needed to topple Infantino.

With Infantino retaining support from Africa while South America are expected to take the same position, AFC members would be required to oust the FIFA president.

New Zealand could join Europe and CONCACAF's resistance, but it is doubtful that the remaining 10 members of the Oceania Football Confederation would follow suit.

Infantino wrote to all FIFA nations claiming they would receive $41m (£30m) if they backed his plan to sell off stakes in FIFA's major competitions.

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino finally agrees huge new contract to STAY as USA head coach until 2030... despite World Cup disaster on home soil
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino finally agrees huge new contract to STAY as USA head coach until 2030... despite World Cup disaster on home soil

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Mauricio Pochettino has officially signed a new contract with the USMNT that will keep him in charge until 2030 – despite their disappointing World Cup campaign.

The 54-year-old's initial contract expired at the end of the tournament, where the USMNT suffered a dispiriting 4-1 thrashing at the hands of Belgium in the round of 16.

The nature of their World Cup exit drew questions over Pochettino's future with the side – until reports last week revealed that talks were ongoing over a new deal.

On Monday, it was officially confirmed that the former Chelsea, Tottenham and Paris Saint-Germain head coach had put pen to paper on a new contract with the USMNT.

In a statement, Pochettino said: 'Working together with U.S. Soccer over the past two years, it has become clear to us that there is tremendous potential to make the Men's National Team program even stronger.

'The passion we experienced from the fans throughout the World Cup only strengthened our belief in what is possible here.

Mauricio Pochettino has signed a new contract with the USMNT that will run until 2030

His initial contract expired after the World Cup - where the USA crashed out in the round of 16

Here to create a culture.



Here to stay for the USA. pic.twitter.com/wxfg0MNNWT — U.S. Soccer Men's National Team (@USMNT) August 3, 2026

'We are excited by the opportunity to bring all our experience and knowledge to even more areas of U.S. Soccer while helping strengthen the pathways for players, coaches and teams across the Federation.

'We want to try to have a lasting impact on the sport in the country that has welcomed us so warmly and for that impact to extend beyond results on the field.'

The Daily Mail understands that Pochettino's appointment has been funded in part by Kenneth C Griffin, Founder and CEO of Citadel and Scott Goodwin, Co-Founder and Managing Partner of Diameter.

A statement by US Soccer insisted that Pochettino 'will have the opportunity to test and strengthen the player pool through numerous official competitions'.

The Argentine's new deal means that he will oversee the USA throughout the 2027 Concacaf Nations League, the 2027 Concacaf Gold Cup, the 2029 Concacaf Nations League and the 2029 Concacaf Gold Cup.

He will also lead the USA into the 20230 World Cup – jointly hosted by Morocco, Portugal and Spain – should they qualify for the competition.

Meanwhile, US Soccer CEO and Secretary General JT Batson said: 'Mauricio and his staff believe in the future of soccer in the United States and our new project allows us to build on progress of the USMNT and the momentum of U.S. Soccer.

'We know we have a lot of work to do to achieve our clear ambitions, including competing to win Men's World Cups and having soccer become the most played sport in every community.

The new deal means Pochettino will lead the USA through 2030 World Cup qualification

A statement by US Soccer insisted that Pochettino 'will have the opportunity to test and strengthen the player pool through numerous official competitions'

'I couldn't be more excited that Mauricio and team are committed to partnering with all of us to do the hard work to bring those ambitions to life.'

Batson had confirmed last week that active discussions were underway regarding the future of the program's coaching staff.

Meanwhile, despite a disappointing end to their World Cup campaign, Pochettino and the USMNT still made history with their performances earlier on in the competition.

For just the third time in history, the USA won their group outright, before going on to defeat Bosnia and Herzegovina 2-0 in the round of 32 – before their loss to Belgium.

Pochettino's coaching staff, Jesus Perez, Miguel D'Agostino, Toni Jimenez, Sebastiano Pochettino and Silvia Tuya, are expected to remain with the Argentine.

Sports.title: Revealed: The stumbling block in Vinicius Jr's talks with Real Madrid... as Arsenal wait to pounce
Sports.content:
Vinicius Junior is poised to hold contract talks with Real Madrid this week amid ongoing interest from Arsenal.

The Brazilian star has only one year remaining on his deal at the Bernabeu and the Premier League champions are weighing a stunning move before the start of the new campaign.

All avenues are currently open ahead of the discussions between Vinicius’ advisors and Madrid president Florentino Perez. Daily Mail Sport understands that while the salary on offer is acceptable to Vinicius, the parties have yet to reach an agreement on a potential signing-on fee.

If Vinicius were to switch to the Premier League, the competition would have another global superstar.

Though the Premier League is comfortably the richest of Europe’s top five leagues, the world’s best attackers like Lamine Yamal, Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe and Ousmane Dembele play elsewhere.

‘We expect to have movements in the next few weeks, obviously,’ said Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta after his side’s pre-season match against Girona.

Vinicius Junior is set to hold contract talks with Real Madrid amid interest from Arsenal

The Brazilian striker returned to Real Madrid's pre-season set-up this week after his post-World Cup break

‘We want to get better like anybody else, and you can see the transfer market and our opponents... We won't sit still and we are very ambitious with what we are doing.

‘The margins are very small. Because we want to get better and the level is going to increase.

'We need to increase the competition internally. We need to make sure we identify the things that we don't have in the team.’

Arsenal are working on a deal to sign midfielder Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle and have already paid £34million for Club Brugge winger Christos Tzolis.

Arteta had insisted last week that Arsenal are hoping to make signings that give the club a ‘different dimension’.

His pledge to fans came after the Gunners ended their 22-year wait to be Premier League champions last season, while they also finished as runners-up in the Champions League.

Arteta said: ‘A lot is happening. From ownership to the board, the sporting director and myself, we know that we want to take this club to a different level.

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta has stressed the club are looking to sign players to take the club to a different level

‘That is going to require a better squad, better individuals. We have identified where we have opportunities to grow and to improve and to evolve our game and what is going to be needed to achieve that.

‘Hopefully very soon we can start to put things in a very concrete way.

‘Excellence has to be our standard and this has to drive to attack the future. The way we behave daily with more and more determination and ambition because we've shown that we've got it.

‘Now we have to show that we belong to this level and we want to increase and take this football club to a different dimension.’

Sports.title: Emma Raducanu practises in an orthopedic boot as injury-stricken British No 1 unwinds in the Swiss Alps with less than a month to go until US Open
Sports.content:
Emma Raducanu practises in an orthopedic boot as injury-stricken British No 1 unwinds in the Swiss Alps with less than a month to go until US Open

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Emma Raducanu heralded the 'best reset ever' after a holiday in the Swiss Alps, but raised concern among her fans as she continued to practise in an orthopedic boot with less than a month to go until the US Open.

The British No1's season has been one of promising peaks but speckled with injury, after a post-viral illness torpedoed her clay season.

Returning to her stronger grass surface, Raducanu reached the final at Queen's Club before her narrow defeat to Donna Vekic.

The 23-year-old was unable to build on this however, after picking up a grade-four stress fracture in the aftermath of the final which kept her out of Wimbledon.

Raducanu was pictured sporting the protective boot as her WTA peers played their opening rounds in SW19, and shared on social media that she continues to wear it for practising her serve.

The former US Open champion chose the picturesque backdrop of St Moritz's Grand Hotel Suvretta House, a five-star hotel in the heart of the upscale Swiss resort.

Emma Raducanu has been unwinding at the five-star Grand Hotel Suvretta House in St Moritz

The British No 1 continued to practice in an orthopedic boot after sustaining a grade four stress fracture (pictured right in July)

Billed as a 'luxury fitness retreat', the hotel - where a Junior Suite can be booked for £1,038 a-night (1,130 CHF) - boasts tennis courts, a spa and close proximity to alpine walking trails and Lake Sils.

But with less than a month until her potential run-out in Flushing Meadows, evidence of her practising wearing the boot, on the hotel's clay rather than hard court, might have been cold comfort to those keen to see her back full to fitness.

Raducanu previously shared a video on social media of herself wearing the boot while she practised her serve perched on top of a rubbish bin.

'Not in the bin but on the bin,' she captioned the image with a wink.

Raducanu's withdrawal on the eve of her home Grand Slam saw the player experience a drop in her ranking as she lost the points gained by reaching last year's third round.

In 2025, Raducanu then chased her grass season with a competitive hard-court build-up ahead of New York, reaching the semi-final in Washington, the third round in Montreal, and the second in Cincinnati.

With all those points set to be lost, Raducanu - who is currently ranked 49th in the world - will likely drop out of the top 50 and could possibly lose her standing as British No1 to Katie Boulter, who is currently 20 points behind her compatriot.

Raducanu will also have to prepare for the possibility of a tricky first round at the US Open with no chance of securing a seeded berth.

As she continues to recover from her own injury, she may be watching the travails of her fellow injury-stricken countryman Jack Draper, who was handed a wildcard to play this week's Canada Open in Montreal.

Raducanu described the break at the luxury fitness resort as the 'best reset ever' on Instagram

In a round-up she shared the stunning vistas from the property, which overlooks Lake Sils

Meanwhile with the hard court swing started in earnest, her compatriot Jack Draper is looking to return to competitive action after a similarly injury-stricken 2026

The 24-year-old, who played last year's US Open as the world No5, has seen his early summer injury comeback hampered by continuing issues, forcing his own withdrawal from Wimbledon ahead of the first round and a late withdrawal from last week's Mubadala DC Open in Washington.

Draper, who is coached by tennis legend Andy Murray, has since called for patience and time as he seeks to climb higher than his current No147 ranking.

'It's important for people to recognise that the injury I have is very complex, it's very complicated and everyone around me is doing everything we can to help this keep moving along,' he told Sky Sports on Sunday. 'It's not as simple as "rest and heal up and you'll come back and you'll be fine."

'Everything outside of tennis I'm doing amazingly well, everything on the court I'm managing really well too, so I'm at a point now where I'm happy that I will come through this period.

'It's just going to take some time, but I'm doing all the right things, and the people around me are really supporting me.'

Sports.title: Saffie Osborne to captain Ryan Moore and Dylan Browne McMonagle in Shergar Cup at Ascot
Sports.content:
Saffie Osborne to captain Ryan Moore and Dylan Browne McMonagle in Shergar Cup at Ascot

The Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup at Ascot on Saturday has been boosted by the news that Ryan Moore and Dylan Browne McMonagle will be in action

View 2 Images Saffie Osborne (centre) will lead a team featuring Dylan Browne McMonagle (left) and Ryan Moore (Image: PA)

Ryan Moore will make only his second appearance in the Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup at Ascot on Saturday, with the event further strengthened by confirmation that rising star Dylan Browne McMonagle will compete.

‌



Moore, who secured the Silver Saddle award for leading rider in the team competition during his only previous participation in 2006, has been freed up with no Flat racing scheduled in Ireland that afternoon.

‌



Moore and McMonagel will represent the Great Britain and Ireland team which will be captained by Saffie Osborne at the event which will also feature teams from Hong Kong, Europe and the Rest Of The World.

‌



The Hong Kong Jockey Club will field a team, led by Vincent Ho, who claimed Shergar Cup glory in 2019 as part of the victorious Rest of the World squad. He will be accompanied by Jerry Chau and Luke Ferraris.

Christophe Lemaire will skipper Europe, alongside Marie Velon and Frida Valle Skar, while Jamie Melham (nee Kah) will return to spearhead the Rest of the World. She will be partnered by Japan's Yutake Take and Suraj Narredu, who steered team Asia to victory last year.

‌



Ascot's head of corporate and industry affairs Will Aitkenhead said: "It's absolutely fantastic to have Ryan and Dylan on board. Both had very strong Royal Ascots, with Ryan the leading jockey, and both had very good weeks at Goodwood.

View 2 Images Jamie Kah: Melbourne Cup winner will ride at Shergar Cup (Image: Getty Images)

"It's really helpful the Phoenix Stakes has moved from the Saturday to the Sunday at the Curragh this year which frees them up and it's great to have them board.

Article continues below

"We'd been in discussions with Oisin (Murphy) and Billy (Loughnane) earlier in the year and they were keen, but they just don't know where they'll be. Obviously Hollie Doyle would have been here, but she's sadly injured.

"In previous years we've lined them up early which helps with the marketing and everything, but this year we were keen to get the strongest teams that we could so waiting until this week made sense."

On the subject of overseas riders, Aitkenhead commented: "Jamie Melham returns as a Melbourne Cup winner, she's huge in Australia and Yutake Take is the biggest name in Japan. We've got Christophe Lemaire and the Hong Kong team led by Vincent Ho as well so we've got some really strong teams."

Sports.title: Jockey allegedly headbutted official and told another ‘if you keep filming, I am going to slap you’
Sports.content:
Jockey allegedly headbutted official and told another ‘if you keep filming, I am going to slap you’

Jerome Claudic became aggressive and insulting after staff tried to stop him entering an area reserved for corporate guests at ParisLongchamp

View 3 Images Jerome Claudic (second right) was banned for one month (Image: Icon Sport via Getty Images)

A jockey allegedly headbutted an official and told another ‘if you keep filming, I am going to slap you’, according to a disciplinary inquiry.

‌



Jerome Claudic, a jockey with nearly 20 years experience, has ridden 27 winners in France this year and over 500 during the course of his career.

‌



He was reported to the France Galop stewards following an incident after racing at Paris Longchamp in July in a corporate hospitality where a garden furniture design business was entertaining guests. The disciplinary panel was told that Claudic, who appeared "heavily intoxicated", had attempted to enter the area with two female friends insisting he was entitled to be there.

‌



When challenged he unleashed “a torrent of insults” at France Galop and described the guests and partners as “buffoons”.

During a six minute outburst, which included racist comments, he was filmed by the company's head of digital who he ordered to put away her phone, telling her, "If you keep filming, I’m going to slap you". He then delivered a “completely unprovoked headbutt” to a member of France Galop staff, the hearing was told.

Claudic was escorted to the exit by a France Galop staff member but as he left uttered “death threats, threats of physical violence, and racist remarks—shouting, in particular, 'You two are dead men walking'.

‌



View 3 Images The incident occurred after racing at Longchamp (Image: Getty)

Claudic explained when interviewed that he had been looking for somewhere to watch the football. He admitted losing his temper when he saw someone filming him but denied headbutting anyone. He said he had been under the influence of alcohol after drinking a "small glass," but that he was mainly tired and annoyed by the video taken without his knowledge.

He explained that jockeys undergo gruelling work schedules, including in intense heat on that day, and he felt worn out.

‌



The panel was told: “He intends to go straight home after races from now on; he and his colleagues feel unwelcome at this racecourse—which provides no designated space for professionals—and since this has caused problems before, he will never set foot there again.”

He apologised and said he had never behaved in that way before and on that evening it was simply a case of having "had enough".

View 3 Images Claudic said jockeys don't feel welcome at Longchamp (Image: Getty Images)

‌



The France Galop stewards said Claudic had “displayed behavior that was absolutely intolerable and unacceptable. This conduct cannot be justified by the explanations he provided; while the apologies he offered must be taken into account, they do not absolve him of responsibility.”

The panel added his behaviour damaged “the image and reputation of the racing institution and the sport itself”.

It said it was also clear Claudic had not learned the lessons of previous disciplinary actions having previously been suspended for six months in 2021, following a test that revealed the presence of a narcotic substance.

Article continues below

Claudic was referred to the France Galop Medical Department for potential psychological, medical, and addiction-related follow-up. He was suspended from riding for one month with another three months suspended for five years.

Sports.title: Glasgow hailed as 'blueprint for future of Commonwealth Games' after major success
Sports.content:
Glasgow hailed as 'blueprint for future of Commonwealth Games' after major success

A new format using exisiting facilities proved to be a "Games changer". The event sold more than 430,000 tickets to show that it was a real Box Office success.

The King and The Queen's entrance to the Opening Ceremony of Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games

Glasgow 2026 was today hailed as a 'blueprint' for future Commonwealth Games.

‌



The event ended with a message to the rest of the world - the new format using exisiting facilities is a "Games changer". It sold more than 430,000 tickets to show that it was a real Box Office success.

‌



And Phil Batty, chief executive of Glasgow 2026, said: "We have created a Games that will inspire more nations to host. Probably more importantly, it is one that every nation feels it could host at some point in the next 100 years.

‌



"The future of the Commonwealth Games was in jeopardy. Glasgow saved the Commonwealth Games but it also reinvented the Commonwealth Games."

Jim Kerr and Simple Minds brought down the curtain on the event at the closing ceremony. The Games' projected cost was £162.6m compared with £543m for Glasgow 2014 and £680m for Birmingham 2022.

View 3 Images Jim Kerr of Simple Minds at the closing ceremony of Glasgow 2026 (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Prince Edward shares sweet moment with Prince Louis at Commonwealth Games READ MORE :

The public backed the Games as netball proved to be the most popular sport selling more than 100,000 tickets. English powerlifter Mark Swan won the first gold medal of the 215 that were on offer.

The rising star from Seaham, Co Durham, said it had provided an 'unforgettable experience'. The more compact 23rd edition featured 215 medal events compared to 261 when the city last staged the Games in 2014. It also saw a record 47 para-sports events, which included the symbolic first gold medal.

View 3 Images Jim Kerr of Simple Minds on stage at the closing ceremony of Glasgow 2026 (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Australia dominated the medal table by amassing 171 followed by England with 110. The host nation finished fifth, with 39 medals, behind Canada and India.

It was a performance described by First Minister John Swinney as "truly historic". Welsh star Emma Finucane created history by becoming the first sprint cyclist to win four track gold medals at the same Games.

Louise Hoskins became the oldest Commonwealth Games gold medallist, winning the para-bowls women's pairs title for Australia at the age of 76 years and 173 days. And legendary South African swimmer Chad le Clos became the most decorated athlete in the 96-year history of the event with 21 medals.

Article continues below

View 3 Images Fireworks closed Glasgow 2026 (Image: Jane Barlow/PA Wire)

Prince William and Princess Kate were among those who took in the action with their children. Mile world record holder Josh Kerr produced another thrilling triumph in the mile, which last featured at the Games in 1966.

The star repaid fans by taking 45 minutes to pose for selfies and autographs after his emotional medal ceremony.

Sports.title: Glasgow saved Commonwealth Games - but don't expect them back on UK soil anytime soon
Sports.content:
Glasgow saved Commonwealth Games - but don't expect them back on UK soil anytime soon

Four of the last seven editions have been staged in Great Britain, and it's clear that Commonwealth Sport realises it needs to cut ties to the mother country for its future relevance

View Image The Prince And Princess of Wales attended the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games (Image: Getty)

Glasgow might have saved the Commonwealth Games, but don't expect to see them back on these shores for a generation.

‌



Four of the last seven editions have been staged in Great Britain, and it's clear that Commonwealth Sport realises it needs to cut ties to the mother country for its future relevance. Scotland gets its eternal thanks for stepping in at late notice when Australia said it couldn't afford to host.

‌



Australian taxpayers ended up paying this city £100 million in compensation to stage the Games on their behalf and were duly thanked by topping the medal table with 70 golds.

‌



"Glasgow has acted as a bridge to the future of the Commonwealth Games movement," said Commonwealth Sport president Dr Donald Rukare. "Every host writes its own chapter, and Glasgow's has been one of bravery, courage, friendship and, above all, outstanding innovation."

India will host the centenary Games in 2030, and there are four private expressions of interest for 2034. Nigeria has made no secret of its desire to become the first African host, while New Zealand believes a lower-cost approach to hosting finally gives it a chance to welcome the Commonwealth for the first time since 1990. Canada hasn't hosted since 1994 either.

‌



Insiders admit there is more chance of the Olympics coming back to the UK – with a bid mooted for the 2040s – before another Commonwealth Games. For years, officials presented hosts with a long list of demands and requirements. Glasgow has changed all that.

"It's a much more collaborative process," said Commonwealth Sport chief executive Katie Sadlier. "We're not telling hosts, 'This is what you must do.' Instead, we're asking, 'What are you trying to achieve?' and then working with them to make that happen.

"We've set a guideline of around 15 to 17 sports, but if a future host comes to us with a proposal they believe works for them, we'll sit down and work through it together. We're not imposing rigid targets. We don't want countries building facilities they don't actually need just to host the Games. If a nation genuinely wants to build a stadium because it fits its long-term plans, that's fine, but it shouldn't automatically become part of the Games budget.

Article continues below

"We don't want hosts spending huge amounts of money on things we don't think are necessary any more. Glasgow is using existing venues, stakeholders have accepted reduced service levels, there aren't fleets of VIP cars, and people are travelling by bus. Everyone has embraced that because they wanted the Commonwealth Games to happen."

Thanks to National Lottery players, more than £33m is raised every week for good causes. It’s because of you that sport, arts, heritage and community projects, as well as our athletes competing at the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games, are supported across the UK .

Sports.title: Emma Finucane roars into history books by completing incredible Commonwealth Games clean sweep
Sports.content:
Emma Finucane roars into history books by completing incredible Commonwealth Games clean sweep

The Welsh wonder crowned a stunning week by adding keirin gold to her time trial, sprint and team sprint titles to cement her status as Britain's undisputed sprint queen

View 2 Images Emma Finucane of Team Wales after her keirin gold at Glasgow 2026 (Photo by Quinn Rooney/Getty Images) (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

Four golds. One queen. Emma Finucane roared into the history books by becoming the first sprinter in 96 years to complete a sensational Commonwealth Games clean sweep.

‌



The Welsh wonder crowned a stunning week by adding keirin gold to her time trial, sprint and team sprint titles to cement her status as Britain's undisputed sprint queen. And she barely broke a sweat.

‌



The 23-year-old felt the pressure of becoming the rider everyone wanted to beat after Olympic glory. But in Glasgow, her rivals could only watch her disappear into the distance. She muscled her way to the front with two laps remaining and never looked back, cruising home to claim Wales' 31st medal of the Games.

‌



“I don’t think I’ll ever fully believe I’ve made history here,” the Carmarthen rider said. "It’s surreal. Little me would be absolutely screaming right now. Ten-year-old me would never have imagined this.

“I just hope I’ve inspired people back home to get on a bike or into a velodrome. I’m so glad I found this sport—or maybe it found me. I absolutely love what I do. It feels incredible to have those gold medals. There was definitely a lot of pressure coming in, but I think throughout the week I just focused on riding my own race and letting things unfold naturally.”

The keirin is usually cycling's answer to a pressure cooker – six riders scrapping for every inch behind a pacing bike before the lid blows off in a frantic final lap. But Finucane blew her rivals away long before the final dash. Her decision to hit the front with two laps to go was a huge gamble, handing her rivals the advantage of her slipstream. Yet none could even get close enough to challenge. And this was no easy ride to glory.

‌



While some critics questioned the strength of the Commonwealth Games field, Finucane's rivals included Olympic champion Ellesse Andrews, who took silver while defending her title. Katy Marchant – her Olympic team sprint partner – finished fifth, while fellow Paris gold medallist Sophie Capewell failed to reach the final.

View 2 Images Emma Finucane won a historic four golds at Glasgow 2026 (Photo by Molly Darlington/Getty Images) (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

This was no cakewalk. But Finucane served up another golden masterpiece, insisting she has learned as an athlete since her Paris experience.

‌



“After Paris, everything was a huge learning curve for me emotionally,” she said. "That week was really tough, and what I came away with was hard to process.

“But going into these Games, I’ve learned how to handle pressure better and regulate my emotions more. I definitely felt like I had a target on my back, but I’ve learned to embrace that. I’ve learned how to deal with it better and just focus on improving every day.

“I’m always thinking about the next thing, but I really want to stay in the moment now. That’s something I haven’t always been good at, but I’m trying to change that. Next up, I’m actually going on holiday with my sister. I’ll take a bit of time to reset, then focus on the World Championships. I’ll soak everything in first, because I don’t think it will fully sink in for a while.”

Article continues below

Finucane’s win was the sixth gold medal for Wales on the track and she added she loved singing the anthem.

"I wish I could have stood on the top step in Paris and sung the anthem louder,” she said. "Here, I got to do that, and that means everything to me. I sang every anthem like it was my last. My family being here meant the world."

Sports.title: Josh Kerr outlines next steps after Commonwealth Games glory
Sports.content:
Josh Kerr outlines next steps after Commonwealth Games glory

Kerr has already erased Hicham El Guerrouj's mile world record and the Moroccan's 28-year-old best in the 1500m is next in his sights

View 2 Images Josh Kerr of Scotland with spectators at the Scotstoun Stadium during day nine of the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. (Image: Martin Rickett/PA Wire)

Josh Kerr knows he's running with a target on his back - and insists he wouldn't have it any other way.

‌



World record holder, Commonwealth champion, it was a whirlwind 24 hours for the new 'King of the Mile'. But Kerr is not the sort to stand still, though he admitted he hadn't had much sleep since his gold medal success at Scotstoun.

‌



"Glasgow on the weekend is always bouncing," he joked.

‌



This was the event he'd had circled in his calendar for some time, but the 28-year-old has new targets in his sights. First, there's regaining the world 1500m title in Beijing next year, then upgrading his Olympic silver from Paris to gold in LA, but top of the list is another world best.

He's already erased Hicham El Guerrouj's mile world record. Perhaps next is the Moroccan's 28-year-old best in the 1500m - the longest-standing running record on the books. Seb Coe, Steve Ovett, and Steve Cram are all former British world record holders in middle-distance running's blue riband event. Kerr makes no secret of the fact he is racing for his legacy too.

In middle-distance running, it's not unknown for in-form athletes to quickly collect records. During a historic 41-day summer stretch in 1979, Coe broke the world records for the 800m, mile and 1500m. Kerr won't compete over 1500m at the European Championships in Birmingham, which perhaps opens up another world record tilt, maybe in Lausanne or Zurich later this summer

‌



“I think the 1,500-world record is within my grasp,” he said. "I'm going to keep going after these records. Unfortunately, I'm the sort of person who gets something and always wants more. We need to keep pushing our sport into the 21st century.

"I don't want to get greedy. Greedy athletes make mistakes, like I did last year at the World Championships. I want to play through all the variables and not push through the red line.

View 2 Images Josh Kerr of Team Scotland celebrates as he crosses the line to win the Men's One Mile Final during the Athletics on day nine of the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"I'm a body of work built by everyone else around me and I'm incredibly lucky to have the team of people I have supporting me. You don't know how many times you'll get the chance to make history."

Kerr has never hidden his ambitions. He vowed to smash a 27-year-old record and win Commonwealth gold this summer – and no he's delivered on both. Admitting there was relief at backing up his bold talk with action, the Scot insisted he had loved every minute of the pressure.

Sir Chris Hoy, Sir Andy Murray... more of this and it'll surely be "Arise, Sir Josh".

Article continues below

"Chris Hoy went to my school and I was in school assemblies listening to his stories and being inspired," he added. "To be mentioned even in the same sentence as two absolute legends like him and Andy doesn't seem real.

"This job is not easy if you don't have role models and those guys were mine. But I've got a lot of work to do to keep up with them, and I'll try."

Sports.title: Leandro Paredes sparks uproar for unsportsmanlike act weeks after World Cup final ‘punch’
Sports.content:
Leandro Paredes sparks uproar for unsportsmanlike act weeks after World Cup final ‘punch’

The Argentine midfielder has again been at the centre of controversy while in action for Boca Juniors.

View 3 Images Leandro Paredes was at the centre of another incident for Boca Juniors. (Image: ESPN Sports Center)

Argentina international Leandro Paredes has again caused an uproar after appearing to kick the ball at an opponent. The midfielder was at the centre of controversy in a hostile end to the World Cup final vs Spain.

‌



After the full-time whistle of Spain’s 1-0 extra-time win over Argentina, Paredes was involved in an incident in which he confronted opposition players. TV footage appears to show him throwing punches towards Gavi and throwing him to the ground.

‌



It was claimed at the time that the 32-year-old was shown a red card for the incident, but that has not appeared on FIFA’s website. It has, however, been confirmed that he has been charged by the governing body for the unsavoury scenes and faces a potential ban.

‌



Non-league footballer shown red card after climbing into stands and confronting fan READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino was set to earn huge salary from World Cup plan as staggering figure revealed READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Parades is now back with his club Boco Juniors, with the Argentine league season at the mid-point. He played 14 minutes of the league game vs Central Cordoba on Sunday, despite the short amount of time, he was still involved in controversy.

A clip shared on social media appears to show Paredes kicking the ball straight at an opponent just as he got to his feet after a foul. There is some argument as to whether it was deliberate or just the midfielder trying to clear the ball.

‌



The incident caused a stir on social media, with some fans clear. “This guy should be sanctioned by @FIFAcom He is a cancer in football,” one said. “He kills the game as we know it. Remove this man.”

View 3 Images Leandro Paredes clears the ball onto his opponent (Image: ESPN Sports Center)

A second added: “He needs to be banned from football for a couple of months. Disgusting player.”

‌



“Genuinely top 2 most dislikable footballers all time lmao and then Argentinians play victim to people hating them when it’s fully deserved,” a third said. A fourth added: “Proper thug this guy. Needs banning.”

A second clip from the game emerged that showed Paraedes reacting towards the referee when not given a foul. “He doesn't like it when the same thing is done to him, so he can see how many players he's done the same to, and he doesn't like a taste of his own medicine,” another fan said.

There were, however, some supporters defending him for the first incident.

‌



“The ref hadn't blown the whistle yet. The ball was in play he cleared the ball,” one said. “The player went down and came back up immediately. This is being blown out of proportion imo.”

A second added: “If you watch the video with audio, it’s clear that he cleared the ball before the whistle was blown.”

Paredes has not yet addressed the melee after the World Cup final. Instead, in the days after the game, he took to social media to send a message .

‌



View 3 Images Leandro Paredes has been charged by FIFA due to the incident after the World Cup final. (Image: Marvin Ibo Guengoer - GES Sportfoto/Getty Images)

"Thank you, Argentina! I love you today and always. Today, I write with a heavy heart, having been unable to bring our country the joy it so richly deserves,” he wrote.

"But with a chest full of pride for having given everything we had and for flying our flag at the very top once again! Thank you to everyone who was part of this national team.

Article continues below

"To this group of players who gave their all to represent this jersey, fighting for it until the very last second of every match! It was an honour to be part of the best Argentine national team in history."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
