For everything else, follow official updates rather than forwarded messages, which tend to recycle photos and closure reports from previous storms.

Alert levels can change during the day as rivers respond to rainfall upstream, so a canton that is green this morning may not stay that way. Check the current status before committing to a route through any of the affected areas.

World.title: CONCACAF Calls for Reckoning With Infantino’s FIFA Leadership
World.content:
North and Central American football’s governing body CONCACAF yesterday called for a “comprehensive reckoning with” Gianni Infantino’s leadership of FIFA after his aborted plan to allow private investment in the World Cup. “This recent unilateral and egregious act of poor governance and leadership follows a pattern of missteps and similar behavior,” CONCACAF said in a statement.

“A comprehensive reckoning with this presidency is imperative.” Last week, world governing body FIFA had announced plans to create a commercial subsidiary which would run its biggest events, including the World Cup and Club World Cup. This body would be open to minority private investment, under a plan which Infantino said would “turbocharge the development of the game globally” by raising up to $4.2 billion.

On Friday, facing a fierce global backlash, Infantino pulled the plug on the plan. CONCACAF, which includes all three co-hosts of the recently concluded 2026 World Cup — the United States, Canada and Mexico — as well as Caribbean associations, yesterday welcomed the decision to scrap the divisive proposal.

It joined European organization UEFA in criticizing Infantino’s actions and expressing doubt over his suitability to continue in the role. “This concern is not CONCACAF’s alone. It is shared across many confederations, Member Associations and those who serve and love the game,” said the statement.

In defending his initial proposal, Infantino had said that it could provide each of FIFA’s 211 member associations with a one-off payment of $20 million in early 2027 and increase their funding allocation for the 2027-2030 cycle from $8 million to $20 million. But the CONCACAF statement noted that FIFA already has “vast reserves,” and said that its members would push for those finances to be disbursed “for football development across our region, without compromising our shared future.”

Infantino’s plan had “advanced outside every established governance framework, without transparency, consultation or due process,” it said. “A proposal of this magnitude does not reach that stage by accident. It is a symptom of leadership that has stopped putting football first.”

World.title: Beach, rainforest or culture? In Belize the answer is yes
World.content:
Beach, rainforest or culture? In Belize the answer is yes

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Every vacation begins with the same argument. The beach people want salt and sun. The adventure people want jungle and adrenaline. The culture people want food, music, and history you can touch. In most of the world, somebody loses that argument. In Belize, nobody does, because this small country delivers all three, often in the same week, sometimes in the same day.

Start with the beach, because the Caribbean here makes an unanswerable opening statement. The Belize Barrier Reef, second largest on Earth, runs the length of the coast, turning the sea into a living aquarium for snorkelers, divers, and fly-fishers. On the Placencia Peninsula, the beach vacation reaches its finest form at Chabil Mar Villas, the award-winning, guest-exclusive resort where the water begins where the veranda ends, and the hardest decision of the day is hammock or pool.

Then turn inland, where the second Belize waits under the canopy. The west is rainforest country, rivers, caves, waterfalls, and the ancient Maya sites that crown it all. Base yourself at Villa Massis Resort on the banks of the Mopan River near San Ignacio, and the jungle chapter organizes itself: Xunantunich and its towering El Castillo one day, Cahal Pech the next, the legendary ATM Cave for the brave, and the river itself for the lazy golden afternoons in between. Good food, good vibes, and howler monkeys for an alarm clock.

And through it all runs the third Belize, the one that lives in people rather than places. This is a nation of cultures side by side: Garifuna drumming and hudut on the southern coast, Maya villages where chocolate is still made from bean to bar, Mestizo towns fragrant with escabeche and corn, Creole rice and beans perfected in every kitchen, and market mornings in San Ignacio where the whole tapestry shops together. Cultural immersion here is not a scheduled excursion. It is simply what happens when you talk to people.

The practicalities seal the case. Belize speaks English, pegs its dollar two to one to the US dollar, and has never been easier to reach, with a record 1.4 million visitors, new nonstop routes connecting five more American cities this winter, and Canadian service growing from three cities. The world is discovering what a single small country can hold.

The only real challenge is logistics, stitching reef, rainforest, and culture into one seamless trip, and that is a solved problem too: Barefoot Services in Placencia, local travel experts who live the destination daily, build the whole route, transfers, tours, and hidden gems included.

So bring the beach people, the adventure people, and the culture people on the same plane. Belize ends the argument the only way worth ending it: everybody wins.

World.title: ‘Kimmy Boo’, in this trimester of pregnancy, found dead in advanced state of decomposition
World.content:
‘Kimmy Boo’, in this trimester of pregnancy, found dead in advanced state of decomposition

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police are investigating the sudden death of 22-year-old Kimane Rosita Ashanti Garbutt, a pregnant woman also publicly known as “Kimmy Boo,” whose body was discovered inside an upstairs room in Belize City on Sunday morning.

Police were called to a building at the corner of Vernon Street and Amandala Drive at about 9:30 a.m. on August 2. Upon arriving, officers met a 44-year-old man, who escorted them to a room on the upper floor.

Inside, police found Garbutt’s motionless body in a seated position in a corner of the room. Her body was reportedly already in an advanced state of decomposition.

Moore told investigators that he went to check on Garbutt at about 9:00 that morning but found the door to the upstairs room locked. He forced the door open, found her motionless and immediately contacted police.

According to the police report, Garbutt had suffered from epileptic seizures for several years. She was also in the third trimester of pregnancy and had reportedly been experiencing complications. She had visited the Karl Heusner Memorial Hospital for a prenatal check-up approximately two weeks before her death.

Garbutt was last seen alive at about 7:00 a.m. on Saturday, August 1. At the time, she told him that she was not feeling well.

Garbutt had previously received public attention under the name “Kimmy Boo” through several Magistrate’s Court appearances. In October 2025, she pleaded guilty to a theft charge and was fined, and in December 2025, she was fined after pleading guilty to common assault.

Her body was transported to the National Forensic Science Service laboratory, where it awaits a post-mortem examination. The cause of death has not yet been determined, and police investigations continue.

World.title: Pregnant young woman found dead in Belize City room
World.content:
Pregnant young woman found dead in Belize City room

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): A death investigation is underway in Belize City after a 21-year-old woman, in the third trimester of pregnancy, was found lifeless in an upstairs room, with a post mortem examination expected to determine how she died.

According to the Belize Police Department, information of a sudden death was received at about 9:30 a.m. on Sunday, August 2, 2026, directing police to a location at the corner of Vernon Street and Amandala Drive.

On arrival, officers met a 44-year-old man who escorted them to a room on the upper floor of a building, where they observed the motionless body of a young woman seated at a corner of the room. She appeared to have passed some time before she was found. The deceased was identified as a 21-year-old domestic of the area.

The man reported that at about 9:00 a.m. that morning, he went to check on the young woman and found the door to the upstairs room locked. He forced the door open to gain entry, and upon seeing her motionless, immediately called the police.

The circumstances of her health add layers of sorrow to the investigation. The young woman had been suffering from epileptic seizures for several years, and was in the third trimester of pregnancy with complications, having last been seen by medical personnel at the Karl Heusner Memorial Hospital about two weeks earlier for a prenatal checkup.

She was last seen alive at about 7:00 a.m. on Saturday, August 1, when she informed the man that she was not feeling well.

Her body has been transported to the National Forensic Science Service laboratory, where it awaits a post mortem examination. Police have given no indication of foul play, and the matter remains under investigation, with the examination expected to establish the cause of death.

World.title: Sunny week opens for Belize while the south catches showers
World.content:
Sunny week opens for Belize while the south catches showers

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): The new work week begins under mostly sunny skies for Belize, with the familiar August heat reaching 95 degrees inland, though the south stands as the exception, catching a few more shower and thunderstorm outbreaks through the morning and again late at night.

According to the National Meteorological Service, a light to moderate easterly airflow prevails. Skies will be sunny today with a few cloudy spells, turning partly cloudy tonight and becoming cloudy at times, especially over the south. Showers or thunderstorms will be isolated, except for the south, where a few more outbreaks can be expected during the morning hours and late at night.

Temperatures along the coast will reach a high of 89 degrees Fahrenheit (32 Celsius) and a low of 82 (28 Celsius). Inland areas will be the hottest, climbing to 95 degrees Fahrenheit (35 Celsius) before dropping to 74 (23 Celsius). In the hills, expect a high of 83 degrees Fahrenheit (28 Celsius) and a low of 68 (20 Celsius). With the mercury holding at 95 inland, hydration and shade breaks remain the order of the working day.

At sea, conditions stay gentle, with easterly winds of 10 to 15 knots, a light chop, and waves of 2 to 4 feet.

On the tropical front, the calm continues. Tropical cyclone formation is not expected in the region over the next 48 hours.

Looking ahead to Tuesday and Tuesday night, skies will be partly cloudy to cloudy at times, with showers and thunderstorms staying isolated, except over the south, where a few more can be expected.

Today’s low tides are at 7:08 AM and 7:17 PM, with a high tide at 1:02 PM and another high at 1:18 AM tomorrow. The sun rose at 5:32 AM and will set at 6:24 PM. The forecast was issued by forecaster Catherine Cumberbatch.

World.title: ‘War With Me And The Mother-In-Law’: Man charged with trying to light mother-in-law’s house on fire with her in it
World.content:
‘War With Me And The Mother-In-Law’: Man charged with trying to light mother-in-law’s house on fire with her in it

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A 22-year-old construction worker accused of deliberately setting fires inside his former mother-in-law’s Belize City home has pleaded not guilty to two counts of arson in the High Court.

Sir Hugh Anthony Andrewin appeared unrepresented before Justice Nigel Pilgrim this week, where he was formally indicted on the two charges.

Justice Pilgrim strongly advised Andrewin to obtain an attorney, telling him that the allegations against him were “very serious offences.” The judge gave him approximately three months to seek legal representation and adjourned the matter until November 13, 2026.

Andrewin was further remanded to the Belize Central Prison, as he also has other pending matters before the Belize City Magistrate’s Court for which he remains on remand.

The charges arise from two alleged incidents at a home on Flamboyant Street on June 11 and June 12, 2025.

Police allege that at about 10:00 p.m. on June 11, Andrewin arrived at the residence of his now former mother-in-law, pulled out a blue lighter and set fire to a sheet covering a grey loveseat valued at $400. The woman reportedly extinguished the fire before it could spread further.

Several hours later, at about 4:00 a.m. on June 12, the woman and her daughter were reportedly awakened by smoke and found a curtain and a green loveseat valued at $750 engulfed in flames. The fire also damaged aluminium louvre windows valued at $495.

The prosecution alleges that the second fire was set with the intention of endangering both women. Andrewin initially faced one arson charge in the Magistrate’s Court but was indicted on two counts when the matter reached the High Court.

World.title: Village man sent to jail after police bust him riding up-stop in Belize City
World.content:
Village man sent to jail after police bust him riding up-stop in Belize City

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A Lords Bank construction worker was sent to prison for two weeks after his arrest for riding a bicycle against the flow of traffic led the court to uncover several unpaid fines for previous bicycle offences.

Ashton Keiron Garbutt appeared in the Belize City Magistrate’s Court and pleaded guilty to causing a bicycle to proceed along a one-way street in the wrong direction.

Police alleged that at about 1:30 a.m. on Sunday, July 26, 2026, cops saw Garbutt riding against traffic on Vernon Street.

According to the officers, Garbutt jumped from the bicycle and hid behind a vehicle after noticing the police. He was searched, but nothing illegal was found.

When informed of the traffic offence, Garbutt reportedly told the officers, “Boss man, I nuh know this dah one way because I dah nuh from here; I dah from village.”

During his arraignment, Garbutt told the court that it was his first traffic conviction. However, a check of his court record showed that he had five previous traffic convictions, including offences for riding bicycles without bells or lights in 2020 and 2021. The magistrate reprimanded him for being untruthful.

Garbutt was fined $30, along with $5 in court costs, for the latest offence. He was given until August 10, 2026, to pay or serve one month in prison.

However, the court also discovered that Garbutt owed $105 in fines from five previous traffic convictions. When he was unable to pay the outstanding amount immediately, a warrant was issued and he was escorted to the Belize Central Prison to serve two weeks.

All of Garbutt’s previous bicycle-related convictions reportedly arose from incidents within Belize City.

World.title: Belize City man fined $360 for assaulting ex-girlfriend and throwing her phone in the drain but must compensate ex $200; Relationship advice from the Judge: ‘Let it go’
World.content:
Belize City man fined $360 for assaulting ex-girlfriend and throwing her phone in the drain but must compensate ex $200; Relationship advice from the Judge: ‘Let it go’

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A Belize City man was fined and ordered to compensate his former girlfriend after admitting that he assaulted her and threw her cellphone into a drain during a domestic dispute.

Francis Staine, 30, appeared unrepresented in the Belize City Magistrate’s Court, where he pleaded guilty to common assault and damage to property.

Police alleged that on Monday, July 27, 2026, Staine assaulted the woman and damaged her cellphone by throwing it into a drain. The dispute reportedly arose after Staine accused her of being unfaithful.

While the complainant described Staine as her ex-boyfriend, he told the court that they had still been in a relationship up until the incident. He also said their child was with the woman at the time.

In mitigation, Staine became emotional and described himself as a hardworking person.

“I can give her back the phone, and I promise I will leave her alone,” he told the court.

The court advised Staine to accept that the relationship had ended and “let it go.” Staine acknowledged that he needed to move on and leave the woman alone.

He was fined a total of $360 for the two offences and ordered to pay the complainant $200 in compensation for the damaged cellphone by September 30, 2026. Failure to pay the compensation could result in distress proceedings against him.

World.title: Belize City messenger fined $155 for possession of crack pipe
World.content:
Belize City messenger fined $155 for possession of crack pipe

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A Belize City messenger received his first drug-related conviction after pleading guilty to possession of a crack pipe.

Alexander Rodolfo Chan, 37, of Antelope Street, appeared unrepresented in the Belize City Magistrate’s Court this week, where he admitted to possession of a pipe.

Police alleged that Chan was found with a metal pipe on June 24, 2026. The object had reportedly been used or adapted for smoking crack cocaine.

In mitigation, Chan asked the court to impose a fine rather than a custodial sentence. The court considered that he was a first-time offender with no previous drug-related convictions.

Chan was fined $150, along with $5 in court costs. He was given until August 31, 2026, to pay the total amount or serve two weeks in prison.

World.title: Stronger than ganja!
World.content:
Consultant child and adolescent psychiatrist Dr Ganesh Shetty says child guidance clinics are now seeing more children addicted to digital devices than to marijuana. He has sounded an alarm over what he describes as a pattern of “disconnection and misconnection, alienation and addiction” amongst Jamaican youngsters.

“These algorithms are created by behavioural specialists, and they drag you into something more interesting, something more wonderful, so that it will suck you in to addiction. I have more tablet addicts coming to my child guidance clinics than weed addicts nowadays,” Dr Shetty disclosed as he warned minors of the danger courted daily.

There are 23 of these clinics in hospitals and health centres throughout Jamaica, providing mental health and counselling services for clients up to 18 years old. Key services include behavioural assessments, emotional support, and treatment for conditions such as attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and depression.

It is unclear if the troubling trend has emerged at all of them.

Dr Shetty, who is also acting director, adolescent mental health, in the Ministry of Health, made the disclosure on digital device addiction during last week’s press conference to present findings of the National Study on Social Media Use and the Protection of Children.

He outlined the toll addiction takes.

“We have teenagers who are so disconnected [from] everybody and everything. And this is what happens when you’re disconnected, and misconnected, and addicted: You don’t sleep; you don’t eat; you’re miserable. Next day, nobody can talk to you, including your mom. And sometimes, when you see a lot of shooting and fighting and cutting off head and cutting off fingers on your screen, you get disconnected [from] that human suffering. So somebody gets hit in school [and you are more] interested in taking a video of it and putting it online so it can go viral — not going and assisting that person,” he pointed out.

Dr Shetty noted that the attraction to screens has its genesis in seemingly harmless choices made by parents and guardians during their children’s early years. He cited the example of a mother who gives her two-year-old an iPad when out in public to prevent the child from “running up and down”. The woman is proud of her baby who appears well-behaved and does not cause “discomfort to others and mother”.

The mental health professional then described a scenario in which the mother has two more children at home, absent fathers, and she uses digital devices to fill the gap as she does household chores such as cooking.

“So she has to have the older two watch some TV and the younger one to deal with the tablet. What happens? The child gets disconnected from the human beings around her/him, and gets connected with the machine and, even at this age, can get addicted to the machine,” Dr Shetty outlined.

He said a child’s affinity for his electronic device only grows, becoming a competitor for the time spent on every other aspect of life.

“It can affect you, affect your energy, affect your focus, affect your memory, affect your school grades, affect what you want to become. You can’t become [a success] because you don’t have grades to go to college, but you have just grades enough to go to supermarket and push cart,” he warned.

Dr Shetty is heartened that there is recognition that a holistic approach is needed to tackle the areas of concern outlined in the study, which is said to be “one of the most comprehensive national assessments ever undertaken” on social media use by minors in Jamaica.

“I’m glad that most folks you interviewed think it has to be done together. Government cannot do it alone. Community cannot do it alone. Family cannot do it alone. Young persons have to be involved in it. It is a family and community effort,” he said.

According to the study, nine out of every 10 respondents, or 90.2 per cent, support government regulation of minors’ social media use, while 2.9 per cent expressed opposition. Nearly 84 per cent believe Jamaica should establish a clear national policy framework governing minors’ use of social media.

World.title: Catherine Hall is back!
World.content:
President of the Montego Bay Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Jason Russell, on his way to winning the Celebrity Cook Off at Saturday’s staging of Montego Bay Jerk and Food Festival.

MONTEGO BAY, St James — Local stakeholders are thrilled with the return of activities to Catherine Hall Entertainment Centre, with Saturday’s staging of Montego Bay Jerk and Food Festival, an annual event whose fate was in question after the venue was damaged by last October’s Hurricane Melissa.

“The feeling of being in this Catherine Hall Entertainment Centre is one of triumph,” president of the Montego Bay Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Jason Russell, told the Jamaica Observer on the sidelines of the celebrity chef cook-off competition which he later won.

“To see the park back and opened, separate and apart from Jerk Fest, to see the Government fix back the park, it looks good. The grass looks good, the walls are up, the fences are up. It gives me a real warm feeling and MoBay is really back,” he added.

Catherine Hall was among the hardest-hit sections of the city when the Category 5 storm struck and the popular entertainment venue was not spared. A section of its perimeter wall was washed away and although it has since been repaired, the venue remained unused for months. Its marquee event, Reggae Sumfest, went to St Ann on July 18 for a one-day event, scaling down the show from the usual seven days.

“They didn’t think that the park would be ready in time and being here we realise that some good work was done,” Russell stated.

Also in attendance at Saturday’s event was Mayor of Montego Bay Richard Vernon, who was equally pleased with the venue’s return.

“It’s good to know that the centre can be used for events. I was always of the view that it could be used ever since the hurricane, just needed to do a little work to get it back in order to ensure we can host events of this size. Today is testament to that thought process back then and we intend for the regular activities in this area to return,” he said.

The facility is owned and operated by the Urban Development Corporation (UDC), which the mayor said had been working diligently to restore the venue. He also commended organisers of Saturday’s event for successfully taking on the challenge of hosting a major event after the hurricane.

Promoter John Lindo admitted there had been significant concerns when organisers first assessed the venue which on Saturday was still being powered by generators. They decided to go ahead with the show, he said, as they did not want to disappoint regular patrons and they know how important the event is to the city.

“Montego Bay Jerk Festival is the people’s show. For 17 years we have been doing it and we must be doing something good. It is a clean, nice show. We do things straight and we do things right and so I guess that is why… the sponsors… are always coming back on board,” he said.

Several sponsors, he added, have thrown their support behind the usual plan to give back to the community by helping individuals connected to the festival and are Hurricane Melissa victims.

Lindo said once arrangements are finalised, organisers will identify the beneficiaries and determine the level of assistance to be provided.

For Mayor Vernon, however, the benefits of the festival were already evident Saturday, particularly for vendors operating both in and outside the venue.

“Events like these they provide spin-offs to other businesses and that is why they are so important. We work closely with promoters to give them as much support as possible to have these types of events,” he asserted.

“Some of them have houses damaged, they’re still fixing and at the same time, you have to send children back to school so they have to deal with that, so I am happy for this opportunity for them and I am happy for this opportunity for the city of Montego Bay,” he stated.

The festival attracted thousands of patrons despite an earlier threat of rain. Attendees enjoyed a wide variety of food, drinks and activities that culminated in a stage show featuring performances by songbird Alliance and several other artistes.

World.title: Pick up a book
World.content:
Kinloss Primary and Infant School teacher Shernette Brooks packing away books she received from Blue World Travel’s Festival at Sea delegation at the Falmouth Port last Wednesday.Horace Hines

FALMOUTH, Trelawny — Regional director at the Jamaica Tourist Board (JTB) Odette Dyer is urging Jamaican children to spend less time on tablets and rediscover the joy of reading, describing books as one of the greatest investments that can be made in a child’s future.

“Please put away the tablets a little bit. That’s not your only avenue for learning and understanding the world. Open your minds to reading a book because when you read, it prepares you for learning, achieving and doing your schoolwork that much better,” Dyer urged students attending a ceremony where 1,000 children’s books were among items donated to 15 schools across Trelawny, St James, and St Elizabeth.

School supplies were also presented to the institutions through a partnership involving Blue World Travel — one of America’s leading travel companies for African American travellers — JTB, and local charity Sarah’s Children. The handover was done at the historic Falmouth Port during the arrival of Celebrity Cruise Lines’

Reflection, which was carrying a delegation from Blue World Travel’s annual Festival at Sea.

Dyer described every donated book as “an opportunity to spark imagination, encourage learning and inspire the dreams of a young Jamaican”. Recalling her childhood, the tourism player said books introduced her to the world long before she had the opportunity to travel.

“I am a testament to reading and loving books. Back then we didn’t have technology, and books sparked my curiosity to explore different cultures. Later, I experienced the world first-hand and was not disappointed,” she said.

Welcoming the visitors, Dyer thanked Blue World Travel President Patricia Nicholson Yarbrough and the team for once again selecting Jamaica as the beneficiary of the annual book drive.

“Tourism is at its best when it creates meaningful connections between people,” Dyer said, noting that initiatives such as the donation demonstrate tourism’s ability to enrich communities long after visitors have returned home. She also commended Festival at Sea passengers who packed books and school supplies before boarding the cruise.

Blue World Travel, a San Francisco-based agency that created Festival at Sea, America’s original African-American cultural cruise, has incorporated children’s book drives into the annual programme for more than three decades.

Yarbrough said the 34th Festival at Sea continued a tradition that began during the cruise’s second year.

“Our passengers are the ones who actually bought all of these books for the schools and libraries. We wanted to give something back to the islands that host us,” she said.

Former Los Angeles School District administrator Peggy Taylor Presley said about 85 per cent of the donated books feature Afro-centric characters, giving students the opportunity to see themselves reflected in the stories they read.

“You can be anything you want to be,” Presley told the students.

Sarah’s Charity Founder Janet Silvera said the donation was particularly meaningful in the aftermath of Hurricane Melissa, which damaged schools and learning resources across western Jamaica.

“For some institutions, rebuilding a library has become just as important as rebuilding a classroom,” she said, adding that every book has the potential to unlock imagination, build confidence and change a child’s future.

Among the beneficiaries was Kinloss Primary and Infant School in Trelawny.

Teacher Shernette Brooks said the donation would help establish a reading corner for the infant department while expanding the school’s library.

“The child-friendly books will support our younger learners, while the remaining books will benefit the wider student population,” she told the Jamaica Observer.

Meanwhile, Dyer thanked the visitors for their generosity, friendship and belief in the potential of Jamaica’s children and encouraged them to experience Jamaica beyond the cruise port.

“Go out, explore the destination and engage with a Jamaican,” she urged.

World.title: From viral buzz to bigger ambitions
World.content:
Tielo Lanez.

When Tielo Lanez released Greedy, the song quickly found a home on social media, introducing the emerging dancehall artiste to a growing audience and earning him early recognition in the genre. Now, almost two years after making his debut on the musical landscape with TikTok trending songs Muk Truck and Bless, dancehall artiste Tielo Lanez has released his debut EP titled The Rebellion.

According to the 21-year-old, The Rebellion represents his musical direction.

“The EP is called The Rebellion because it’s a representation of what I need to become to achieve what I want,” Tielo Lanez told the Jamaica Observer recently.

“I somewhat write as if I’m creating an album each time I create a record,” he explained. “I believe it was only a matter of time before I dropped a project. I don’t think I was getting the singles out fast enough, and so this is a way to get all the songs out without it becoming overwhelming.”

The EP features StairDiWay produced Undecided, and the DJ Mac-assisted Blow and Code Up by Extended Play Records.

The track Shootah Dem (remix) features Kkrytical, while Worship is a collaboration with Ayetian.

Other producers who contributed their talent include MXSSIVH, Alva Music, Kutti Music, Temple Boss, Slyngerz Music, Prod 14, and Doneknowkello.

The project took two months to complete.

The artiste noted that he wrote every song himself and remained fully involved throughout the production.

“The song on this project I believe will surprise people the most is Bad Bunch. It’s my newest sound, created on accident. The instrumental is also a skeleton, which is something very new to me as well.”

The project’s emotional centre, however, is the title track, Rebellion, which the artiste recommends listeners hear first.

“Rebellion is about finding yourself, being yourself and living your truth,” he said, explaining that the song carries a message of honesty and self-discovery that he believes many people will relate to.

Originally from St Thomas, Tielo Lanez (real name Jevaughn Smith) attended Morant Bay High School and later Signal Hill Secondary in the parish.

He shared that music has been his calling since his high school days.

“I’ve been doing music professionally for less than two years and the journey has been challenging. However, the lesson learnt along the journey is to be yourself and to live your truth,” he disclosed.

Putting the EP together also gave the entertainer a clearer understanding of his own creative instincts.

“A lesson that stood out to me while putting this EP together is I’m a jack of all trades when it comes to creating different types of music.”

The artiste experiments with multiple sounds on the project, hoping to better understand both himself as an artiste and the audience discovering his music.

“What I want the audience to understand about Tielo Lanez is that he is more than capable of dominating different styles of music and is ready to make a name for himself,” he said, outlining that his willingness to experiment became one of the defining characteristics of the project.

Rather than chasing trends, Tielo believes the project’s greatest strength lies in its authenticity.

“This project distinguishes itself and me with its sound and energy behind each record. No trends were followed — just music for the soul and pure creativity,” said the artiste.

As he braces himself for fan reactions to the project, the entertainer also sets his sights on finding that one breakthrough record he hopes will elevate his career to the next level.

Tielo Lanez made his debut in the United Kingdom in May, when he performed before at City Splash, which reportedly saw more than 20,000 patrons in attendance. Also sharing that bill were Beres Hammond, Aidonia, and Elephant Man.

World.title: No quarrel with the courts
World.content:
Prime Minister Dr Andrew Holness (second left) and president of the Jamaican Bar Association (Jambar) Tenneshia Watkins (second right) celebrate Jamaica’s first female Director of Public Prosecutions Paula Llewellyn (left) and former Jambar President Ian Wilkinson, both King’s Counsel, who were honoured Friday night during the association’s annual banquet.Joseph Wellington

Prime Minister Dr Andrew Holness, whose legal team on Friday lost an appeal to block the disclosure of certain files in his battle with the Integrity Commission (IC), later that evening reaffirmed the importance of an independent judiciary. While speaking broadly about his Administration and not directly referencing his legal issues, Holness stressed that he has no quarrel with the application of the law — even at times when it “constrains the actions of the executive”.

On the contrary, he stressed that “a strong and independent legal profession is indispensable to the rule of law”.

“It provides citizens with representation, assists the court in administering justice, scrutinises public authority, and helps ensure that rights are protected and obligations enforced. Jamaica has a constitutional order built deliberately on the separation of powers, and that separation will, from time to time, produce tension between the branches of the State. I say that as I see others smiling. I do not regard such tension as a defect in our democracy. I regard it as evidence that our democracy is working,” the prime minister declared.

He was speaking to an audience of leaders and other members of the justice system during the 2026 Jamaican Bar Association’s (Jambar) Annual Banquet.

It is essential, the prime minister said, for the judiciary to provide checks and balances.

“When the courts constrain the actions of the executive, they do not obstruct the work of the Government; they discharge the very duty the constitution assigns them. An executive that is never checked is an executive that has forgotten the source of its authority. And let me say that this executive has never forgotten the source of its authority,” added Holness.

He spoke of the importance of a judiciary that is impartial, and displays “principled application of the law” for all Jamaicans, not just some.

“We also expect this for all our citizens who seek access to the courts. That is what secures the confidence of our citizens in our Government and institutions, and this is what keeps us free as we pursue major reforms and investment in security, infrastructure, and the economy,” the prime minister said.

Critics have frowned upon Holness’s decision to take the IC to court. However, his proponents have consistently argued that it is his right — as it is for any other Jamaican — to seek legal redress.

The prime minister was granted leave by the Supreme Court in 2024 to apply for judicial review of the IC’s report on his statutory declarations, challenging processes engaged by the IC and its Director of Investigations Kevon Stephenson.

Holness has maintained that he has not broken the law since the tabling of the report that contained recommendations that the Financial Investigations Division (FID) and Tax Administration Jamaica (TAJ) examine his financial dealings.

He sought a declaration that the commission acted unfairly and unlawfully in its conduct of an investigation into his statutory declarations, with his lawyers arguing that the issues were of critical importance to the overall fairness of the proceedings. It was revealed, Friday, that their bid was unsuccessful.

Hours after, the prime minister spoke of the importance of a system of justice that is beyond reproach, framing his comments within a national context.

“Confidence in our legal system is essential. Investors and citizens must trust our laws, contracts, and institutions,” he told the audience of legal professionals from bench and bar.

During the banquet, Jamaica’s first female Director of Public Prosecutions Paula Llewellyn, and former Jambar President Ian Wilkinson, both King’s Counsel, were honoured. Wilkinson is also president of the Jamaica Chess Federation. The prime minister paid tribute to them both.

“They have demonstrated that excellence at the Bar requires much more than technical knowledge. It demands discipline, preparation, courage, integrity, and an abiding respect for institutions,” said Holness.

He also acknowledged a select group of legal stalwarts who were being honoured for individually giving five decades of service to the profession.

“Fifty years of advocacy, 50 years of counsel, 50 years of mentorship — most important — but 50 years of service! You have trained generations, preserved our traditions, and helped shape our institutions we rely on today. Jamaica owes you a debt of gratitude,” Holness said.

Reflecting on her journey from a young child to the peak of her profession as a public servant, Llewellyn was adamant that she would have it no other way.

“I learned from very early that when you have positions in life and you have to serve the people, do not levitate up into the clouds. Stay on the ground, serve the people, they will always know when you are sincere,” she urged young professionals present.

Wilkinson, for his part, emphasised the importance of hard work and mentorship to the craft while urging young professionals to aim for maximising their contributions to the legal arena and country, rather than seeking to line their pockets.

World.title: PRIDE & JOY
World.content:
In this August 6, 2022 file photo, Jamaica’s Sunshine Girls celebrate the semi-final netball win over New Zealand during the Commonwealth Games in Birmingham, England. The Sunshine Girls lost to New Zealand in the 2026 Commonwealth Games final in Glasgow, Scotland, on Sunday .Photo: Naphtali Junior

DESPITE coming up short in consecutive Commonwealth Games netball finals, Jamaica’s Latanya Wilson says they are proud they got into position to challenge for the gold medal.

The Sunshine Girls battled gamely but were defeated 48-56 by world number two-ranked New Zealand Silver Ferns at Hydro arena in Glasgow, Scotland, on Sunday.

The Jamaicans had also lost to the Silver Ferns in the preliminary stage, going down 48-53 last week.

But they entered the final high on confidence after pulling off an emotional, nail-biting 46-45 win over 2022 champions Australia in the semi-finals on Saturday.

“I’m very proud that we put ourselves in this privileged position to be out here to actually play the finals,” Wilson said after the match. “I’m a bit disappointed in the loss, but I’m still proud of the girls.”

Wilson, who played wing defence for the full 60 minutes of the game, said she thought they did not get off to a fast start like they did in the semi-final.

“I think it’s a number of things [for falling short]. I feel we started really slow, and I felt like in that second quarter we came back into it but I feel we just kind of let the momentum swing a bit for them. But yeah, I’m still proud. It was a good match. New Zealand is a top team, and we knew that they were going to come out here and put on a strong performance,” the Jamaican netballer said.

Wilson said Coach Sasher-Gaye Henry Wright had urged them to dig deeper during a talk at half-time, at which point they had been trailing by three goals.

“[We had to] just try and get something. We weren’t winning any balls, so it was very important for us to try something different and just give it a prop. Because at [that time] we were done, so we needed to give it a try,” she said.

Jamaica were off to a sluggish start, and despite tying up the scores twice in the third quarter, New Zealand always appeared in control. The Silver Ferns were led by a magnificent shooting performance from goal shooter Grace Nweke who had 48 goals from 54 attempts.

New Zealand led by 16-13 after the first quarter and held on for 28-25 margin at half-time, before increasing the advantage to 41-36 at the end of the third quarter. They led by as many as 10 goals in the fourth quarter before coming out winners by eight goals.

Romelda Aiken-George, who was oftentimes defended by two players when she got the ball, led Jamaica with 32 goals from 36 attempts, while Shanice Beckford scored 16 goals from 18 tries.

Despite the loss, Wilson said she was satisfied they had done their best and that their fans appreciated their effort.

“I think they’re super proud of us, whether we win or lose. I feel like they would be proud of us, and I know that all our fans in Jamaica would be cheering us on, and even here, like it’s amazing. It’s a privilege to be in this position. I know Australia would love to be in this position, so to be able to get this privilege and to be here, it’s good job to us,” she reasoned.

The second-place finish on Sunday earned Jamaica a fifth medal in netball at the Commonwealth Games, as the country finished with 19 medals (10 gold, four silver, five bronze) overall in Glasgow. The other 18 medals came from track and field competitions which ended on Saturday.

In the bronze-medal game that preceded the final on Sunday, four-time champions Australia defeated England 68-50. It was the first time Australia were not contesting the gold-medal game in the history of the Commonwealth Games.

World.title: Drought busters
World.content:
This youngster seems fascinated by this impressive head of cattle on display at Denbigh Agricultural Show on Sunday. Garfield Robinson

DENBIGH, Clarendon —With the country bracing for drought, the National Irrigation Commission (NIC) has given an assurance that it is adequately prepared to provide water to farmers in need should the current dry period persist.

“We are seeing where the water levels are falling, especially in the surface systems [rivers]. But we are monitoring it and we are working closely with the Water Resources Authority, which is the regulator, to ensure that we stay within the guidelines to be able to manage what we do,” said NIC director of engineering and technical services Rohan Stewart.

He was speaking with the

Jamaica Observer, Saturday, on the margins of Denbigh Agricultural, Industrial and Food Show held at the Denbigh Showground in May Pen, Clarendon.

The Meteorological Service of Jamaica is projecting prolonged dry conditions stretching into this October. Last Thursday, Water, Environment and Climate Change Minister Matthew Samuda put the country on alert for full prohibition orders for water usage, which he says will take effect on August 10 if the forecast remains unchanged or worsens.

The water minister said those orders will be targeted at “irrigation and watering of gardens, lawns, grounds, and farms, filling or supplying of pools, and other things for domestic services”.

On Saturday, Stewart assured commercial farmers that the NIC has measures in place to ensure that their thirst for water is met. Outside of irrigation, he explained that NIC has trucks that are used predominantly in the St Elizabeth and Trelawny areas to supply farmers with water.

“That service is in significant demand now, but there are a few weeks’ backlog because the demand is so great in that area; but we are working on it,” he assured.

In addition, he said, there is also a water filling service where individuals may purchase water and truck it to their farms.

“If the drought intensifies, we will have rotation where farmers would get water at different times. Currently, farmers can get water on demand, but if the dry period progresses into a drought where we will have to do some restrictions, then farmers will be notified and they will be given water on a scheduled basis,” Stewart explained.

“With the best plans, sometimes things go awry but we are agile. We are seeing an increase in persons coming for water. Some people would have been dormant or not utilising all of their lands, so some of those persons are coming on to the system. Also, with the new Essex Valley and Parnassus irrigation systems, we are also seeing persons coming on for connection and we are prepared to supply those areas,” he added.

However, Stewart urged farmers to put their own contingency plans in place to weather conditions that are expected to pose a challenge for an extended period.

“Despite where we are now in the dry period, it is not too late for farmers to start planning and implementing those plans. Farmers are encouraged to use water efficiently and we are also saying, ensure you utilise crop cover which will reduce your evaporation and water loss. Also, do mulching and look into planting drought-tolerant crops to achieve the objective of efficiency for the system, success for you as the entrepreneur, and food security for Jamaica,” he urged.

World.title: Superwoman doesn’t exist
World.content:
SOMEWHERE along the way, many women bought into the myth that being ‘superwoman’ meant doing everything, for everyone, all the time.



We wear multiple hats with pride. We are wife, mother, entrepreneur, ministry leader, caregiver, employee, mentor, volunteer, daughter and friend. We answer emails before sunrise, push hard during the day, prepare meals after dark, encourage everyone else, and somehow convince ourselves that asking for help is a sign of weakness.

I’ve been there and I’m still trying to shake some of these practices.

Over the years, I’ve coached women who looked successful on the outside but were quietly exhausted on the inside. Their calendars were full, but their souls were empty. They had mastered the art of showing up for everyone else while disappearing from themselves.

Many women wear the title ‘superwoman’ like a badge of honour. But here’s the truth: superwoman doesn’t exist. Behind the polished social media photos and professional success are many women like yourself, who are overwhelmed, exhausted, emotionally depleted, and quietly wondering how much longer they can keep going.

As a life coach, I’ve worked with high-achieving women. Many appeared successful by every outward measure, yet privately admitted they were exhausted – exhausted trying to be everything to everyone. They weren’t failing but they were burning out because they never gave themselves permission to slow down.

Success should never come at the expense of your well-being and can I tell you that the body is going to respond negatively if you refuse to slow down?

Here are five habits every driven woman should embrace to protect her peace, her health, and her future.

1) Stop wearing “busy” as a badge of honour. Being constantly busy doesn’t necessarily mean you’re living a meaningful life. Many women fill every moment of every day because they’ve become uncomfortable with slowing down. I know because I’ve been right there.

Others say yes to every request because they don’t want to disappoint anyone. But busyness can become a distraction from what truly matters. Peace of mind came for me the day I stopped saying yes to every request.

Take a step back and ask yourself: Is everything on my schedule necessary? Or have I confused being busy with being valuable? The most fulfilled women aren’t necessarily the busiest. They’re often the ones who have learned to focus on what matters most.

2) Rest before your body forces you to. Burnout rarely happens overnight. It builds slowly, through skipped meals, late nights, chronic stress, emotional overload, and the constant pressure to keep performing.

Unfortunately, many women don’t stop until their bodies make the decision for them. But rest isn’t something you earn after you’ve done everything. Rest is part of staying healthy enough to keep doing what you love.

Fit these things into your schedule now – a quiet afternoon, a weekend away, a walk, a hobby, or simply switching off your phone for a while. It’s maintenance. Your body and mind deserve the same care you so freely give everyone else. (I’m speaking to myself here too)

3) Learn that “no” is a healthy sentence. One of the hardest lessons many women ever learn is that saying no doesn’t make you selfish. It makes you wise. Not every invitation requires your presence.

Not every favour requires your agreement. Not every problem is yours to solve. Not even Jesus did that when he was on earth. Every unnecessary “yes” usually comes at the expense of something important. Maybe your family, your health, your peace, or your time. Healthy boundaries don’t push people away. They protect you.

4) Take care of yourself with the same commitment you show everyone else. Women are natural caregivers. We encourage. We nurture. We solve problems. We show up.

But too often we become experts at caring for everyone except ourselves. My son said to me recently, “mom you give so much, sometimes you need to slow down”. I stopped answering every phone call. I stopped praying on cue, the moment someone called me. It takes a lot from the body to be available to minister, give advice and pray for people 24/7. Your emotional health matters. Your mental health matters. Your physical health matters.

So slow down and read books that inspire you. Exercise regularly. Laugh often. Eat well. Spend time with people who energise rather than exhaust you. Invest in hobbies that bring you joy. You can’t keep giving your best to the world if you never give anything back to yourself. Self-care isn’t selfish. It’s essential.

5) Stop trying to carry everything alone. One of the greatest myths successful women believe is that asking for help means they’ve failed. It doesn’t. Strong women ask questions. Strong women delegate.

Strong women lean on trusted friends, family members, mentors, and professionals when life becomes overwhelming. Strong women understand that they need to think like a project manager. You don’t have to do it all. Just find people who has strengths in areas you need help and let them handle things.

You don’t have to prove your strength by carrying every responsibility on your own. Sometimes the strongest thing you can do is simply admit, “I need help”. There is tremendous freedom in releasing the pressure to be everything for everyone.

The world often applauds women who never stop. But true success isn’t about how exhausted you become chasing achievement. It’s about building a life where your success and your well-being can thrive together. Your career matters. Your family matters. Your dreams matter. But so does your health and peace of mind.

Give yourself permission to slow down. Protect your peace. Create healthy boundaries. Celebrate progress instead of perfection. Because at the end of the day, no one wins an award for burnout. The goal isn’t to become superwoman. The goal is to become a healthy, fulfilled, resilient woman who has the energy to enjoy the life she’s worked so hard to build.

Marie Berbick-Bailey is a certified master life coach, women’s transformational coach, ordained minister, author, motivational speaker, wife, mother and big sister dedicated to empowering women to heal, thrive, and walk in purpose. Connect with her at www.marieberbick.com, www.marieberbickcoach.com, or e-mail marieberbick@gmail.com.

World.title: Farage needs the border to be the battle of the summer
World.content:
Under its proposals, an “integrated surveillance command” to track boats using drones, space satellites and infrared feeds would be established using the Royal Navy, Royal Air Force, Royal Marines and British Army.

Small boats would be intercepted at sea with their occupants detained, medically-assessed and given food and water before being returned on military inflatable boats to the country they came from, most likely France.

“I am entirely confident that under a Reform government, within a fortnight, there would be no more boats,” Farage — who took questions at a press conference for the first time since early May — told reporters.

“If the Royal Navy is not there to protect this country from invasion, then, frankly, I can’t see what its purpose is,” he added.

Seizing the agenda

The Reform announcement comes as the ruling Labour Party enjoys a modest bounce in opinion polls two weeks after swapping out Keir Starmer as prime minister for former Greater Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham.

Burnham has seized the agenda, announcing a flurry of spending commitments in his first fortnight in charge, and struck a more optimistic tone than his predecessor.

World.title: Zelenskyy appoints chief negotiator as head of foreign intelligence
World.content:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has appointed Kyiv’s chief negotiator and former Defense Minister Rustem Umerov as head of the country’s Foreign Intelligence Service, according to a decree published by the presidential office on Monday.

Umerov’s current position as secretary of the National Security and Defense Council will be taken over by Ihor Klymenko, who was serving as minister of internal affairs, as announced in a separate presidential decree. Klymenko had been considered by lawmakers the leading candidate to replace ousted Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov.

Umerov’s appointment comes as part of a broader reshuffle of Ukraine’s security leadership that Zelenskyy announced in July. The overhaul included the dismissals of Fedorov, Commander-in-Chief Gen. Oleksandr Syrskyi and others. Ukraine needed “more strength” in its wartime leadership, said Zelenskyy.

Umerov will now be in charge of a broader portfolio including “diplomacy, defense, negotiations with the U.S. and other designated partners, as well as talks on ending the war,” according to Zelenskyy’s announcement. A key participant in Ukraine-Russia negotiations, Umerov will also continue overseeing work on the EU–Ukraine Drone Deal.

World.title: Paris court rejects pro-Kremlin TV star’s appeal against expulsion
World.content:
A Paris court on Monday rejected Russian television star Xenia Fedorova’s appeal against a ruling that she must leave the country, a week after French authorities accused her of acting as “a conduit for disinformation campaigns” orchestrated by Moscow to “destabilize public order.”

The former head of Kremlin-backed RT France, who has been under house arrest in Paris since Wednesday, challenged three government measures: the expulsion order, a requirement that she remain in Paris and report to police daily, and a six-month asset freeze. But an administrative court ruled she had failed to demonstrate any of these measures caused her immediate and serious harm.

The former RT France chief was a regular commentator on media platforms owned by conservative French billionaire Vincent Bolloré — including CNews and Europe 1 — where her Russia-friendly views on Ukraine, NATO and European security had come under growing scrutiny ahead of the country’s 2027 presidential election.

World.title: Von der Leyen rallies to support Spain after Ceuta crisis
World.content:
Around 50,000 people crossed into Ceuta from Morocco last week, with dozens dying in the attempt. Almost all those who entered have since returned to Morocco.

Von der Leyen on Monday praised the “swift handling” of returns by Spanish and Moroccan authorities, saying they had “successfully prevent[ed] illegal movement onwards to mainland Spain and Europe.”

The exchange followed a joint letter from 22 EU leaders at the weekend calling for an emergency meeting of interior ministers and a tougher, coordinated response to the crisis. That meeting will take place on Tuesday, with EU ambassadors discussing the situation on Monday afternoon.

The intervention by EU leaders opened a new political fight over Spain’s migration policy, including Madrid’s plan to regularize more than 1 million undocumented migrants. Some governments argued that the measure created a “pull factor” by encouraging people to believe that irregular entry could eventually lead to legal residency.

Sánchez rejected that criticism in his letter, accusing some EU countries of responding in a “selfish,” “polarizing” and unlawful manner. He argued that Spain needed European solidarity rather than blame after the deaths and the strain placed on Ceuta’s authorities. The Spanish government refused to comment for this article.

Von der Leyen’s letter offered that solidarity while making clear that the crisis would also have to prompt stronger EU action.

World.title: Spain’s politicians point finger at Morocco over Ceuta crisis
World.content:
That led many to suspect that such a large flow of people could hardly be masterminded without the acquiescence of Morocco, which claims the Spanish cities of Ceuta and Melilla as occupied territories.

Diplomatic speculation has also centered on whether Rabat could be flexing its muscles over Spain’s recent rapprochement with Algeria, which supports self-determination in Western Sahara — a territory claimed by Morocco.

“Let’s call things by their name: Morocco is using human beings to attack our sovereignty,” said Eduardo Rubiño, lawmaker with the Sánchez-allied, left-wing Más Madrid party.

Ceuta Mayor Juan Jesús Vivas from the conservative People’s Party on Monday said the situation could not be characterized as “a migration crisis” because “people have the perception that this, if not orchestrated, was encouraged or permitted” by Moroccan authorities.

Vivas conceded that Madrid had to do its utmost to continue working with Rabat, but also told Spanish newspaper El País that “Morocco has shown us that it is not reliable.”

Since the outset of the crisis, Spain’s Socialist-led government has prioritized smooth relations with Morocco, which will prove critical to resolving the crisis, rather than pinning the blame on Rabat.

World.title: France bolsters checks on ‘sensitive’ foreign investments
World.content:
Earlier this year, Lecornu asked three parliamentarians from his center-right coalition to report on France’s economic security. Obtained by POLITICO, the document called for a “radical change in posture” and urged the government to take “a holistic approach” to protecting strategic assets, securing critical supply chains, reducing dependencies and strengthening technological sovereignty.

In a press release on the threshold change, Lecornu’s office said the government would give its response on any proposed foreign investments within 10 days of notification to “avoid placing an undue burden on companies’ ability to raise capital in financial markets.”

The move is intended to “guard against opportunistic acquisitions by non-EU investors in French companies listed outside the EU that could pose risks to national security,” the statement noted.

France had previously set up a screening process for planned acquisitions of over 10 percent of shares in French companies listed on European markets during Covid-19, with the stated aim of “protecting strategic companies” in a time of crisis. The measure was later made permanent and is now being extended to French companies listed outside the EU.

The new rules will come into effect in the coming days.

Other EU countries, such as Germany and Spain, have similar foreign investment screening regimes that apply a 10 percent threshold to acquisitions in certain strategic sectors.

Paul de Villepin contributed to this report.

World.title: Iran signals no immediate U.S. talks after Trump says negotiations to resume
World.content:
U.S. President Donald Trump said negotiations with Iran would resume Monday, after scrapping a planned military strike over the weekend. Speaking on Sunday, the American leader also refused to set a deadline for reaching a broader deal with Tehran.

“They knew the extent of the attack because they saw it forming. Now what we’re doing is we’re talking to them in the form of a negotiation. It begins tomorrow afternoon, and we’ll see,” said Trump, talking to reporters aboard Air Force One.

Asked whether he had imposed a deadline, the U.S. president responded: “Would I rather make a deal? I’m not looking to kill people because people die, a lot of people die, and we don’t want that.”

Trump’s remarks came on the heels of his early Sunday announcement on Truth Social that the U.S. was shelving a “massive attack,” after Iran and several Middle Eastern countries asked Washington to pause military action while negotiators worked toward an agreement. He said the framework under discussion included the “Immediate, Complete, and Total OPENING OF THE HORMUZ STRAIT” and an end to Iran’s nuclear threat, adding that Israel had also agreed to pause strikes.

Baghaei stated there would be “no significant change” in the situation in the Strait of Hormuz as long as Iran remained under what he described as U.S. military pressure.

World.title: UEFA threatens Infantino, Joshua Kushner with legal action
World.content:
Gianni Infantino looks on during the 2026 World Cup quarter final match between Norway and England at Miami Stadium in the U.S. on July 11, 2026. | Image Photo Agency/Getty Images

The FIFA chief’s plan to privatize part of the World Cup’s commercial operations sparked a major backlash in Brussels.

The governing body of European football, UEFA, has threatened legal action against FIFA President Gianni Infantino, venture capitalist Joshua Kushner — brother of U.S. President Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner — and other individuals involved in the controversial plan to privatize a share of the World Cup’s commercial operations.

UEFA is “actively considering legal action, arbitration, and/or regulatory complaints” against Infantino, reads a letter sent to Infantino, seen by the Telegraph.

The move follows Infantino’s proposal to transfer FIFA’s commercial rights and tournament operations to a private entity firm — in partnership with Thrive Capital, Kushner’s venture capital company — allowing private investors to acquire a 20 percent stake.

World.title: Zelenskyy’s military shake‑up continues – but Fedorov remains out
World.content:
Rustem Umerov, former secretary of Ukraine’s National Security and Defence Council has been appointed as head of Ukraine's Foreign Intelligence Service on 3 August.

 

Umerov has also been a key member of Kyiv’s negotiating team in the US-led peace process and he will carry on with this task, according to Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

Ukraine’s president explained as well that Umerov will also continue coordinating the Drone Deal initiative with foreign partners, including in the Middle East.

"He has greater capacity to deal with these issues simultaneously — diplomacy, defence, and the negotiations process with the US and some other partners," Zelenskyy said during an event with diplomats on Monday.

Former Interior Minister Ihor Klymenko will replace Umerov as secretary of the National Security and Defence Council.

The appointments come as part of Zelenskyy’s war-time government reshuffle launched in July, which triggered a self-inflicted political and military crisis.

FILE - Secretary of State Marco Rubio, left, and Secretary of the National Security of Ukraine Rustem Umerov shake hands, Nov. 30, 2025 AP Photo

Pro-Fedorov protests continue in Kyiv

Ukraine’s Foreign Intelligence Service has been without a permanent chief since winter, a situation that has drawn far less attention than turmoil at another key institution - the defence ministry, which has now gone more than two weeks without a full‑time minister.

Ukrainians are still demanding that Zelenskyy reinstates former Mykhailo Fedorov after his dismissal triggered nationwide street protests.

On 31 July Kyiv saw what the organisers claimed was the “the largest protest since the Revolution of Dignity” in 2014.

Activists shout slogans during a thousands-strong rally to denounce Volodymyr Zelenskyy's decision to dismiss Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov, Kyiv, Ukraine July 31, 2026. AP Photo

Ukrainian war veteran Dmytro Koziatynskyi, one of the protest movement's public leaders, called on Zelenskyy to “give Mykhailo (Fedorov) a year to carry out the reforms, and then make decisions based on the results."

Koziatynskyi said even “during the air raid alert in Kyiv, the protesters refused to disperse and chanted: "We stand and we will keep standing.”

“Frustration and anger are building up in society, and it's currently completely unclear how such a disoriented state will enter the promised harsh winter.”

“You must end the protests by bringing Fedorov back to the Ministry of Defence,” he said calling on Zelenskyy to fulfil the last one of the protesters' original demands.

Earlier Ukraine’s president already dismissed Oleksandr Syrskyi as commander in chief and replaced him with Mykhailo Drapatyi, a widely respected commander.

But as the protesters vow to continue demonstrating, Zelenskyy has given no indication that he intends to return Fedorov.

World.title: Hungary's nuclear crisis tests new PM Magyar's leadership
World.content:
Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar is facing the biggest test of his government yet, as an energy crisis triggered by the partial shutdown of the Paks Nuclear Power Plant threatens to disrupt supply during peak summer demand.

 

All but one reactor has been taken offline because of record-low water levels in the Danube, which the plant relies on for cooling. Should water levels fall further, the plant could be forced to shut down entirely for the first time since it opened 42 years ago – raising the prospect of blackouts and electricity restrictions during the high season.

For Magyar, who won April's election and took office in May, managing the crisis marks his first major political test.

"The current situation can turn out to be either a threat to the reputation of the new Hungarian government or, in fact, an opportunity to strengthen the perception of an efficient crisis manager in Hungarian society," said Dániel Hegedűs, deputy director of the Institut für Europäische Politik.

According to the latest opinion poll from the Republikon Institute, Magyar's Tisza Party held a commanding lead in July, with 58% support. The opposition Fidesz Party, led by former prime minister Viktor Orbán, trailed on 20%.

Fidesz seizes on the crisis

Fidesz, which governed Hungary for 16 years before its electoral defeat and has seen its support fall sharply since, is already using the crisis to portray Magyar's government as incompetent.

"The government is not in control of the situation. It is only thanks to the sacrifices of the Hungarian people, the self-restraint of companies, and the development achievements of the past 16 years that there is no bigger problem. The Tisza government cannot handle the energy crisis," Fidesz parliamentary group leader János Bóka wrote on social media.

Government response

Paks typically supplies around 40% of Hungary's electricity, but demand has risen sharply amid a heatwave. Magyar said Hungary would weather the crisis by boosting output from other power plants, increasing electricity imports, and asking industry and households to voluntarily cut consumption.

"The Hungarian government has already done what was possible under the given circumstances for successful crisis management — both in terms of strategic communication to Hungarian society and mobilising domestic power plant capacity, as well as ensuring that imports from European electricity markets can proceed smoothly to cover Hungarian consumption," Hegedűs said.

The government also has a contingency plan in place to limit industrial consumption on a rotational basis, if required.

"The unprecedented situation calls for solutions that have never been used before," Magyar said. "In these extraordinary circumstances, coordinated action and an exceptional level of cooperation will be essential."

Magyar's Party blames the previous government

Márton Hajdu, a Tisza Party lawmaker, told Euronews the current government could not be blamed for the lack of investment in infrastructure at Paks that would have allowed the plant to keep operating during periods of extreme drought.

"The government is getting on with the job," Hajdu said. "At the same time, Hungarians are witnessing the true legacy of the previous government. Every day, it becomes clearer how much essential infrastructure was never built — projects the country desperately needed. While squandering and siphoning off vast sums of public money, they were also prepared to let billions in EU funding slip away. Our job is to minimise the price the Hungarian people have to pay for the previous government's irresponsibility."

Crisis could be an opportunity, if handled well

Another official close to Magyar's government, speaking to Euronews on condition of anonymity due to the sensitivity of the matter, said the crisis could become an opportunity for the government — provided it avoids major missteps.

"This is an opportunity to prove ourselves, demonstrate that we are competent, and help reunite the nation. It is also a chance to explain how Fidesz betrayed the country, while allowing our ministers to prove themselves," the official said.

"There is one condition: we have to get through this crisis without major mistakes or unnecessary distractions."

"So far, we have not had to choose between impossible options, because the Hungarian people and businesses have shown remarkable maturity in managing the demand side, and Prime Minister Péter Magyar has been showing strong leadership. I don't think this will be a major test for us; that will come later."

Risks ahead

Magyar said the coming days would be crucial for the energy network. Expert Dániel Hegedűs warned that shortages could still benefit the opposition.

"If anything goes wrong and there will be blackouts in the coming days, then of course it will open up an opportunity for the opposition party Fidesz to attack the government with the argument that they failed to manage the situation," Hegedűs said, adding that the political fallout for Magyar could be limited, as he could place the blame on Orbán's government for its lack of investment.

"Péter Magyar can use the counterargument that the current situation is a consequence of the negligence of the Fidesz governments, and particularly the delayed investment and construction of new pipelines at the Paks nuclear power plant, which would have allowed operations to continue even at a lower water mark on the Danube."

World.title: Revealed: New York and Paris top global tourism city attractiveness index
World.content:
Is there a science behind what makes a city attractive to travellers? According to the latest research, the answer is a resounding yes. A new global ranking has not just looked at where people are travelling to, but which cities are capturing their attention and leaving the strongest emotional impressions.

 

The Global Tourism City Attractiveness Index for 2026 issued by Yanolja Research, in collaboration with Purdue University and Kyung Hee University, took a deep dive into social media conversations across 14 languages to rank 200 destinations.

Rather than focusing on usual tourism indicators, such as visitor numbers or hotel occupancy, the index measured two pillars: the “cognitive awareness” of destinations, which measured how visible, recognisable and “top of mind” destinations were within global travel discussions, and “affective attractiveness”, which assessed how memorable and enjoyable destinations were, as well as how keen travellers were to recommend them to others.

Researchers also analysed 419 travel-related words and phrases – such as mountain, hotel, street food and art gallery – which either fell into the urban aesthetics and natural scenery category, or culture and history, experiential tourism content or hospitality categories.

"The 2026 index shows that the most competitive tourism cities are no longer simply the most visited or most heavily promoted places,” said Dr. SooCheong (Shawn) Jang, Professor at Purdue University and Director of Yanolja Research. “They are cities that successfully convert global awareness into emotionally meaningful visitor experiences.”

Which cities ranked highest?

The 2026 Global Tourism City Attractiveness Index was divided into three ranking categories: overall, awareness, and attractiveness.

Overall ranking

1. New York, USA

2. Paris, France

3. Osaka, Japan

4. Kyoto, Japan

5. Seoul, South Korea

6. London, UK

7. Rome, Italy

8. Bangkok, Thailand

9. Okinawa, Japan

10. Chicago, US

Awareness ranking

1. New York, USA

2. Paris, France

3. London, UK

4. Rome, Italy

5. Bangkok, Thailand

6. Seoul, South Korea

7. Washington, DC, USA

8. Osaka, Japan

9. Los Angeles, USA

10. Kyoto Japan

Attractiveness ranking

1. Osaka, Japan

2. Kyoto, Japan

3. New York, USA

4. Seoul, South Korea

5. Paris, France

6. London, UK

7. Rome, Italy

8. Okinawa, Japan

9. Bangkok, Thailand

10. Dubai, UAE

American and Asian heavyweights take the lead

New York claimed the highest spot in both the overall and awareness rankings, only moving down a notch in the attractiveness poll – coming in third place.

The study attributed its top overall ranking to its “rare combination” of global visibility and being favourable within visitor sentiment. Other American destinations, including Chicago, Washington D.C. and Los Angeles, had a broad appeal, making it to the top 10 of the overall and awareness rankings.

In total, 16 US cities feature in the global top 50. According to researchers, this presence points to a portfolio that has a diverse ecosystem of cultural, business, entertainment, leisure and lifestyle destinations offerings.

Meanwhile, France’s capital Paris ranked highest among the European cities – second in the overall and awareness rankings, and fifth for attractiveness.

“New York's No.1 ranking demonstrates the power of combining unmatched global recognition with strong experiential appeal,” Dr. Jang said. “At the same time, the rise of Asian destinations such as Osaka, Kyoto, Seoul and Okinawa shows that emotional attractiveness is becoming a decisive source of tourism competitiveness."

The research highlights Asian destinations being dominant for attractiveness, with 60% of destinations within the attractiveness ranking being in Asia.

According to the researchers, there is a shift in what’s peaking global tourism interest. Gone are the days when iconic landmarks or infrastructure defined a city, now, the destinations that stand out are the ones adept at combining their global awareness with distinctive visitor experiences that are shareable and emotionally satisfying.

World.title: Record low Danube levels prompt central European governments to take emergency action
World.content:
A drought gripping central Europe has seen record-low water levels in the Danube River, forcing governments across the region to take drastic action to prevent a looming energy crisis.

 

In Romania, where the Danube's water flow has reportedly dropped to 1,500 cubic meters per second, the country's navy has carried out a controlled explosion to clear rock near the river's Bala Canal in an effort to maintain the required water flow for the safe operation of Romania's Cernavodă nuclear power plant.

The drastic action came after authorities had already shut down one reactor unit at Cernavodă.

Romania's energy sector has been under a state of alert since Friday, when acting Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan called on residents to voluntarily lower their electricity usage during peak evening hours and warned that the low level of the Danube could lead to the shutdown of the second reactor at the Cernavodă power station.

The MVM Paks Nuclear Power Plant in Paks, Hungary, Wednesday July 29, 2026. MTVA - Media Service Support and Asset Management Fund

In Serbia, the government has made moves to reduce energy production from some of the country's hydroelectric plants.

The two biggest, Djerdap I and Djerdap II - which provide around 18% of Serbia's electricity generation - have reduced output to 20% and 30% of their respective capacities, Serbian Energy Minister Dubravka Đedović told local media.

Hungary is also facing energy-production challenges.

On Sunday, Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar announced that the nation's only nuclear power station was expected to shut down amid soaring temperatures across the region.

"Due to the further drop in the Danube's water level, one of the last two generating units at the Paks Nuclear Power Plant will be shut down at 1:30 a.m," Magyar wrote in a post on X shortly after midnight on Sunday.

"As a result, the plant's output will fall to just 240 megawatts, and tomorrow it will be completely shut down for the first time in 44 years," he added.

On Monday, the PM offered a slightly more upbeat update, saying "water management forecasts" for the next few days had "become slightly more optimistic."

"The Danube’s water level has remained stable since this morning at both Paks and Budapest," he said, adding: "The last turbine at Paks continues to generate power."

World.title: Second-hand home prices in Spain rise 16.2% in a year
World.content:
The resale housing market is showing no sign of easing. The average price in Spain stood in July at 3,154 euros per square metre, 0.7% higher than the previous month and 16.2% above a year ago, according to the Fotocasa Property Index. Converted into a standard 80-square-metre flat, the figure has jumped from 217,214 to 252,308 euros in just twelve months: 35,094 euros more for the same home.
