"The price of an average home in Spain has now exceeded 250,000 euros for the first time," sums up María Matos, head of research at Fotocasa, who attributes the rise to an insufficient supply in the face of demand that remains robust despite the mortgage strain households are already bearing. Matos herself expects the market to enter over the coming months a phase of "gradual normalisation", as more buyers hit the limit of their financial capacity.

Prices rise in every region

All 17 autonomous communities saw second-hand homes become more expensive in July compared with 2025. Fourteen of them recorded increases of more than 10%: Murcia tops the table with 26.2%, followed by Cantabria (20.1%), the Valencian Community (18.1%), Navarre (17%) and La Rioja (16.5%). At the other end of the scale, the Balearic Islands (6.5%) and Extremadura (7.4%) posted the most moderate rises.

In absolute price terms, Madrid remains the most expensive region, just short of 5,500 euros per square metre (5,455 €/m²), ahead of the Balearic Islands (5,401 €/m²) and the Basque Country (3,970 €/m²). Extremadura (1,359 €/m²), Castilla-La Mancha (1,426 €/m²) and Castilla y León (1,806 €/m²) bring up the rear.

Ávila and León, the biggest provincial surges

At provincial level, the increase is virtually across the board: 48 of the 50 provinces analysed saw prices rise, and in 29 of them the increase exceeded 10%. Alongside Murcia (26.2%), two inland provinces that rarely make the property headlines stand out: Ávila, with 25.3%, and León, with 25.2%. Only Teruel (-8.4%) and Huelva (-2.3%) recorded falls.

Madrid (5,455 €/m²) and the Balearic Islands (5,401 €/m²) again rank as the most expensive provinces, followed by Gipuzkoa (4,758 €/m²) and Málaga (4,651 €/m²). Jaén, at 1,117 euros per square metre, remains the cheapest province in the country.

Donostia, the most expensive provincial capital; Jaén, the most affordable

Among provincial capitals, 46 of the 47 analysed became more expensive, with the city of León leading the way (25.6%), ahead of Ávila and Ciudad Real, both up 19.8%. The only capital where prices fell was Santa Cruz de Tenerife, with a slight -1.3%.

Donostia-San Sebastián has cemented its position as Spain's most expensive provincial capital, at 7,120 euros per square metre, ahead of Madrid (6,624 €/m²), Barcelona (5,304 €/m²) and Palma de Mallorca (5,200 €/m²).

Zooming in on municipalities, 93% of the 404 analysed by Fotocasa posted year-on-year price increases, and in twenty of them the rise exceeded 30%. Catral (Alicante) tops the list with a 129.7% jump, followed by Bigastro (92.9%) and Narón (62.5%). The most expensive municipalities in Spain remain concentrated in the Balearic Islands: Santa Eulària des Riu, at 8,494 €/m², and Sant Antoni de Portmany, at 8,266 €/m², while Bailén, Mengíbar and Torredonjimeno, in Jaén, are the cheapest, all below 800 euros per square metre.

Madrid and Barcelona, moving at different speeds

Spain's two largest cities are on very different trajectories. In the city of Madrid, an 80-square-metre flat has gone from 485,075 to 529,900 euros in a year, up 9.2%, meaning buyers are paying 44,825 euros more for the same home. In Barcelona, the increase is much more contained: 3% year on year, from 412,086 to 424,280 euros, 12,194 euros more.

By district, Madrid is experiencing its own boom in the south of the city: Villaverde is up 29.8% and Villa de Vallecas 25.5%, well ahead of already consolidated areas such as the Barrio de Salamanca (2.6%), which remains the most expensive district, at 10,682 euros per square metre. In Barcelona, Gràcia (11.6%) and Nou Barris (11.5%) lead the rises, while Ciutat Vella is the only district where prices are falling, down -2.7%.

World.title: Inside Europe’s EV boom: Are we prepared for more than a million batteries to reach end-of-life?
World.content:
More than a million electric vehicle (EV) batteries could reach end-of-life by 2030, becoming one of the world’s “fastest-growing waste streams”.

 

Global EV sales have surged in recent years, surpassing 20 million units and now accounting for around 25 per cent of all new cars sold worldwide. The EV boom has also been bolstered by the war on Iran, which continues to send oil and gas prices soaring.

In fact, more than 1.24 million fully electric cars were sold in Europe during the first half of 2026 – marking a 33.7 per cent increase compared to the same period last year.

Are EVs greener than petrol cars?

EVs often start with what is known as a higher “carbon debt” compared to petrol and diesel cars as they require significantly more energy to manufacture.

Much of this is due to battery production, which requires huge amounts of electricity to produce heat needed during manufacturing. While this electricity can be produced through renewables, many countries still rely on burning polluting fossil fuels.

Minerals such as lithium, cobalt and nickel, which are required in EV batteries, also pose environmental and social concerns.

A 2023 report from Amnesty International found that the mining of critical minerals has led to a slew of human rights abuses, including forced evictions and physical assault.

While modern mining remains controversial, research has shown that the environmental benefits of an EV do outweigh their energy-intensive production.

A 2020 report by Transport & Environment (T&E) found that EVs outperform diesel and petrol cars in all scenarios, even on carbon-intensive grids such as Poland, where they are about 30 per cent cleaner than conventional cars.

In the best case scenario, where an EV runs on clean electricity with a battery produced with clean electricity, EVs are already about five times cleaner than conventional equivalents.

“Crucially, the evidence shows that EVs powered with the average electricity repay their ‘carbon debt’ from the production of the battery after slightly more than a year and save more than 27 tonnes of CO₂ over their lifetime compared to a conventional equivalent,” the report says.

“EVs that do high mileage (e.g. shared vehicles, taxis or Uber-like services) save up to 77 tonnes over their lifetime (compared to diesel).”

Why EV battery waste is a growing concern

Most EVs are powered by lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) – the same kind found in many everyday electronics such as smartphones, laptops and games consoles.

But according to the International Energy Agency (IEA), the number of lithium-ion and similar batteries reaching their end-of-life is expected to rise sharply from the mid-2030s onwards. This is when the battery can no longer store or deliver energy effectively because it has degraded over time.

It means that around 1.2 million EV batteries could end up as waste in the next four years. By 2040, this number is expected to reach a staggering 14 million.

At the same time, demand for LIBs is rising, increasing the pressure to mine for critical minerals and risking a future shortage of lithium.

While EV batteries can be recycled, it is notoriously difficult and costly to do so. Before a battery can even start the recycling process, it must undergo a time-consuming preparation phase that involves discharging, dismantling and separating its components.

There are also safety risks associated with chemical reactions used to recycle batteries, which can release toxic substances such as hydrofluoric acid. These compounds pose serious risks to worker health and safety, and can even damage recycling plant equipment.

It’s why experts are calling for a “significant expansion” of recycling infrastructure that will manage future waste volumes and recover valuable materials needed for new battery production safely.

“EVs are a critical part of the transition to a lower-carbon economy, but their long-term success depends on how effectively we manage the waste stream that follows while also strengthening the supply of critical minerals,” says James Skifmore of environmental consultancy firm Valpak.

“Expanding the capacity and efficiency of circular infrastructure will be essential to recover valuable materials, strengthen supply chains, reduce reliance on virgin resource extraction and maximise the long-term sustainability of the EV transition.”

Across Europe, companies are racing to achieve exactly this.

Can EV batteries be recycled more efficiently?

The ReLiB project, which is being spearheaded by the University of Birmingham in the UK, is developing recycling technologies that it says will put the country at the “cutting edge” of research and development.

Researchers are aiming to develop and scale-up technologies that will raise material recovery rates from recycled batteries from around 50 per cent to 90 per cent by targeting faster and more efficient dismantling and separation processes.

The EU has also funded a four-year project, coordinated by the Technological Centre LEITAT in Spain, which aims to replace slow, manual dismantling with semi-automated systems that can safely disassemble batteries while recovering around 95 per cent of the components.

EU-funded project BATRAW will also work on giving batteries a second life, as some EV batteries may no longer have enough capacity to power a car, but could be used for less demanding energy storage jobs – instead of being recycled straight away.

The project is developing better ways to transport old batteries safely and exploring how new batteries can be designed so they’re easier to repair and recycle.

World.title: Italy to propose Albania-like migrant centres at the EU level
World.content:
Italy is aiming to extend at European level the model of migrant centres set up in Albania, proposing the creation of expulsion hubs of foreign nationals arriving on EU turf unlawfully to safe third countries while their asylum and immigration files are examined.

 

The proposal, revealed by leading Italian media outlets and confirmed by government officials, will be presented by Interior Minister Matteo Piantedosi at the extraordinary Council of European Union interior ministers convened for Tuesday.

The meeting was organised after the migration emergency that erupted in Ceuta, the Spanish enclave on Moroccan territory, where over the course of the last few days, as many as 70,000 migrants forced their way into the autonomous Spanish territory.

Among the potential host countries are several African states, with Uganda cited as one of the most concrete options. The question of the resources needed to fund the project, however, remains open.

"We need to build a common strategy on immigration. The Italian government requested this meeting, together with Denmark’s social democratic government, so that the Pact on Migration and Asylum is implemented in the EU. In other words, returns are activated," said Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani to local media outlets ahead of Tuesday's meeting.

Tajani also floated the "possibility of creating new Albania-model centres in various African countries" and "more generally in the countries of origin and transit".

Madrid accused of 'ideological manipulation'

The crisis in Ceuta has laid the groundwork for a new flashpoint between Italy and Spain over the management of migrants.

Tajani defended the position of Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's government, describing it as "rigorous and moderate", while criticising the strategy of the Spanish government led by Pedro Sánchez, accused of pursuing an overly submissive approach to migration.

"Madrid’s approach runs counter to the Italian one, which almost all the other countries support," the top Italian diplomat said.

"The ‘everyone come to Europe’ policy is wrong, because Europe is not able to take in everyone indiscriminately. And it is a good sign that the European Commission has backed Italy’s position and not Spain’s," Tajani added.

The Italian foreign minister denounced the "ideological manipulation" he says the Spanish government has created around the question of migrantion, explaining that the cooperation plan could lead to "policies that are needed", far removed from "slogans and false promises".

What is Italy proposing?

The government’s goal is to create a network of centres outside the European Union dedicated to the management and return of irregular migrants, based on cooperation with countries of origin and transit.

The idea was first put forward by the Italian premier at the end of June, after gaining approval of the new EU regulation on returns. Rome now intends to formalise the plan and present it to the other 26 member states.

The new hubs, under the Italian proposal, would be financed through the bloc.

An initial list includes several African states and some countries located outside the traditional migration routes. Potential candidates include Ghana, Senegal, Tunisia, Libya, Mauritania, Egypt, Uganda, Ethiopia, Uzbekistan, Armenia and Montenegro.

Uganda is among the options considered most concrete. Germany, Austria and the Netherlands are reported to have already expressed interest in possible projects in the African country.

Montenegro could also be brought into the European strategy, although discussions remain at a preliminary stage. One of the key issues still to be settled concerns the financial coverage of the plan, including contributions of both the EU and at the national level.

The GSP+ programme

Rome will also call for a stricter application of the Generalised Scheme of Preferences programme, known as the GSP+, which was approved earlier this year and is set to enter into force from 1 January 2027.

The system links trade benefits and tariff reductions granted to developing countries to their cooperation in readmitting citizens who are attempting to enter or stay in Europe illegally.

The aim is to strengthen the tools available to facilitate and support returns of migrants and asylum seekers, and increase cooperation with countries of origin of those migrants.

In parallel, the government is seeking to make fully operational by the end of the year the Italian-run centre in Gjader, in Albania.

Interior Minister Matteo Piantedosi explained that the goal is "to bring it back into full operation at the height of its capacity by the end of the year, or even earlier if the problems and legal proceedings are resolved".

The facility is set either to resume its original function or to be used in line with the new EU regulations, once the necessary judicial steps have been completed.

The initial plan envisaged a much broader use of the Albanian centres, with a capacity estimated at up to 3,000 people a month and a possible total of 36,000 migrants a year.

The aim was to apply fast-track border procedures to examine asylum applications. Since April last year, however, the site has operated exclusively as a detention centre for returns. Only a few hundred people have passed through it since then, and the number of returns has remained limited.

The Gjader complex includes three facilities with different functions. The largest centre, for asylum seekers, has 880 beds. There is also an Italian-run repatriation holding unit (CPR) with capacity for 144 people and a small 20-person holding prison.

In the port of Schengjin an initial reception hotspot has been built to take in migrants intercepted in the central Mediterranean and transferred on-board an Italian naval vessel.

Detention orders issued at the facility, however, have not been validated by judges, slowing down the implementation of the project.

World.title: Madrid breaks tourism record, tops €10 billion in international spending in six months
World.content:
With its blend of major museums, history-filled streets, renowned gastronomy and a vibrant cultural life, Madrid is becoming ever more attractive to travellers from around the world. The Spanish capital closed the first half of 2026 with record figures: international tourism generated €10.007 billion in spending, 11.4% more than in the same period a year earlier.

 

For the City Council, these figures underline Madrid's ability to attract visitors, talent and investment. The head of tourism, Almudena Maíllo, has pointed out that the sector's growth has an impact that goes beyond the economic data, breathing new life into neighbourhoods, creating jobs and strengthening the city's services.

Madrid is not only drawing in more travellers, it is also seeing a growing share of international visitors. Between January and June 2026, the capital welcomed 5.66 million tourists, 4.1% more than a year earlier, with foreign markets as the main driver: they now account for 59% of arrivals and generated two out of every three hotel nights. In total, overnight stays were just shy of 12 million, with an average stay of 2.38 nights among international visitors.

The capital strengthens its global appeal with more visitors from the US, Brazil and Europe

Madrid continues to widen its international appeal, with the United States as its leading source market. In the first half of 2026, American travellers exceeded 567,000, with more than 1.3 million overnight stays, while Italy and the United Kingdom rounded out the top three foreign visitor markets.

The biggest leap came from Brazil, which became the fastest-growing market, with a 30% increase in visitors and a 24% rise in overnight stays. Portugal also gained ground, strengthening Madrid's links with European and Latin American markets.

Madrid's tourism boom is also evident in its hotel offering and employment figures. The capital ended the first half of 2026 with 920 establishments, almost 48,600 rooms and more than 96,000 beds, numbers that confirm the expansion of its tourism infrastructure. The sector also reached 15,249 workers, 5.4% more than the previous year, driven by business confidence in the city's appeal.

World.title: Growing impact of extreme heat on informal workers in Asia's cities
World.content:
When temperatures soar across Asia's cities, informal workers face a choice: risk their health or lose their income. For many, the effects don't end when the workday is over.

Brijpal Singh spends long hours working construction under the blazing sun in Noida, a sprawling industrial satellite city in India's National Capital Region. Even as temperatures soar past 45 degrees Celsius (113 Fahrenheit), work on the building site rarely stops.

By the end of each shift, the 51-year-old says his heart is pounding, and he's usually dizzy, dehydrated and physically drained from hours in the heat. Yet taking a day off is a luxury he cannot afford.

Missing work would mean losing his daily wage of 500 to 600 rupees ($6 to $7). The money supports his wife and three children living in a village in Uttar Pradesh, a two-day journey away .

"There are days when I don't feel like working," said Singh. "But if I miss a day, who will take care of my children and pay for their expenses?"

After a day in relentless heat on a construction site, Singh tries to find relief in front of a fan Image: Danish Pandit/DW

Some 5 million people work in the Delhi region's informal economy, accounting for roughly 80% of the total workforce. And as climate change drives up temperatures, many paid by the day like Singh are faced with an impossible trade-off between providing for their families and protecting their health.

Extreme heat harms health, productivity and earnings

The past decade has been India's warmest on record, bringing more frequent, intense, and prolonged heat waves. At the same time, heat is reducing productivity and increasing illnesses, with one study finding rising temperatures could be costing informal workers the equivalent of 2% of their country's GDP annually. That's nearly $80 billion (€69 billion).

"Wage losses are only going to worsen as temperatures continue to rise," said Ameena Kidwai, lead researcher at People's Courage International, a nonprofit aiming to strengthen informal workers' rights. "Workers are now putting in many more hours than they did before to complete the same amount of work."

The US-based organization surveyed informal workers in five Asian cities. Kidwai said some of those surveyed reported that tasks once completed in eight hours now take 10 to 12 hours during the hottest months, as they slow down to cope with dangerous conditions.

With heat becoming a major occupational hazard, workers described the harm to their health, ranging from respiratory and gastrointestinal illnesses to stroke and kidney disease.

"As a result, workers also have to spend more on over-the-counter medicines and visits to clinics or hospitals," Kidwai said.

Out of the work frying pan and into the home furnace

A lack of ability to recover is a defining feature of urban heat for informal workers — from construction laborers and street vendors to delivery riders — say researchers.

Like Singh, many are migrants who leave their families behind to earn a living in fast-growing cities, said Patricia Samantha Narvaez, a program manager at the Philippine development organization IDEALS.

"You would expect home to be a place of relief," said Narvaez. "But many live in densely packed neighborhoods with poor ventilation, little green space and heat-absorbing concrete."

That's the case for Singh, who returns to a single room with poor ventilation after work. During the hot months from April to June, it becomes a furnace, and frequent power cuts make it difficult to cool down before the next day's shift.

"During the hot days, I can't eat well," Singh said. "I often drink oral rehydration solution and go to bed without eating."

Narvaez surveyed informal workers in Quezon City for a report on the impacts of extreme heat. The city is just northeast of Manila, the capital of the Philippines, a country in which some 42% of the employed population are informal workers.

"Some participants described Quezon City as a 'concrete jungle' because even at night it remains unbearably hot," said Narvaez.

Fifty-year-old Aida Tano has experienced such conditions firsthand. Tano worked in a garment factory in Quezon City for nearly two decades, where soaring temperatures, heat-generating machinery and poor ventilaton turned the production floor into an oven. With no air conditioning, four workers shared one electric fan.

Aida Tano, like many informal workers, bears the brunt of extreme heat both at her job and at home Image: People's Courage International

"There was no escape from the heat," Tano said. "We complained, but management told us that if we couldn't endure it, we could leave."

Narvaez says it's not unusual for factory owners to restrict measures that help workers cope with the heat even for trivial reasons such as not wanting fans to break down. At Tano's workplace, she had to pay for her own drinking water, and even climbing stairs to leave on her break became too exhausting in the heat.

The factory has since closed, but after a long day in extreme heat, Tano, who now does odd jobs like sewing and cleaning, would come back to a house with no AC. She still relies on electric fans and keeping windows covered to block the sun, both of which do little to cool her home.

Working women bear the brunt of extreme heat

The economic impacts of climate change hit women hardest, largely because they account for a majority of the world's poor, according to the United Nations.

Women in the informal economy also shoulder a disproportionately large burden because they combine paid work with unpaid caregiving responsibilities, said Ameena Kidwai of People's Courage International.

"They're managing their jobs while also running their households," Kidwai said. "When children or older family members fall sick during a heat wave, the caregiving duties falls largely on women."

Shanti Devi, a 36-year-old daily wage laborer in Noida, has been her family's sole breadwinner since her husband was injured in a workplace accident several years ago.

"Now I have to manage the house, care for my children and also try to earn a living," said Devi.

During heat waves, school closures and a shift to online classes often force Devi to stay home with her four children instead of going to work. Each day of lost wages adds to the already struggling family's financial strain.

"I took the day off because it is too hot to work, and my children are home because their school is closed for the summer," Devi said. "I have to cook for them. When school is open, they eat their meals there."

If Shanti Devi misses work to care for her children, she loses out on a much-needed pay check Image: People's Courage International

Frequent power outages and overheated homes, also leave many women up through the night caring for family members in the heat before returning to work the next day. Disrupted sleep and lack of rest come with increased health risks, such as heart disease and diabetes, meaning women are often more vulnerable than men in heat waves.

Researchers say these overlapping pressures expose a gap in many cities' efforts to adapt to a heating planet. While India has introduced heat action plans, and Quezon City is developing its own measures, protections for informal workers remain limited and unevenly enforced.

As temperatures rise because of human-caused climate change, experts say measures focus largely on short-term responses and often overlook the realities of informal workers' lives.

"Climate change will only deepen existing inequalities because those with the fewest resources are often the most exposed to extreme heat," Narvaez said. "Ultimately, resilient cities cannot be built on exhausted and unprotected workers."

Edited by: Jennifer Collins

World.title: Russia says civilians killed in strike on Black Sea resort
World.content:
Moscow has accued Kyiv of stepping up attacks on civilian targets in recent weeks. Meanwhile, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy put Ukraine's chief peace negotiator in charge of foreign intelligence.

At least seven people, including three children, were killed in a Ukrainian strike on a Black Sea resort village of Arkhipo-Osipovka, authorities in Russia's Krasnodar region said on Monday.

Local governor Veniamin Kondratyev stated that falling drone debris injured at least 40 others, and accused Kyiv of attacking civilian targets far away from military installations.

Meanwhile, Sergey Aksyonov, the Moscow-installed governor of Crimea, said in a Telegram post that four people were killed in a Ukrainian strike on the Russia-annexed region.

Sergey Aksyonov, the Moscow-installed governor of Crimea, said in a Telegram post that four people were killed in a Ukrainian strike on the Russia-annexed region.

Russian military officials said they have intercepted a further 131 Ukrainian drones overnight.

Kyiv did not confirm the strikes, but analysts said it was in line with the size of a recent spate of Ukrainian counter-attacks to Russian aggression.

At the same time, Ukraine said that an attack on a gas station in the Dnipropetrovsk had killed three people, in keeping with a recent pattern of Russian attacks on fuel depots.

Ukraine's negotiator to head foreign intelligence service

In the latest move in an ongoing shakeup in Kyiv, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy appointed Rustem Umerov, Ukraine's chief peace negotiator, to lead foreign intelligence.

Zelenskyy said Umerov would remain in charge of peace talks after being moved from his previous job as head of the Security Council advisory body. Zelenskiy tasked Umerov with continuing to seek a diplomatic end to the war with Russia.

Ihor Klymenko, the former Interior Minister, will take over as head of the Security Council.

Since the sudden cabinet reshuffle last month, which included replacing Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov, Zelenskyy has been shuffling senior officials among top posts. He has also replaced the top military commander, Oleksandr Syrskyi.

World.title: Binging on cringe: It's as addictive as 'eating junk food'
World.content:
Flexing achievements? Cringe. Expressing genuine emotions? Cringe. You want to look away, but you can’t. Cringe. It's so addictive, people have built social media careers by monetizing other people's worst moments.

I feel it. You probably do, too. Someone posts a crying selfie, proposes at a wedding, or confidently sings off-key at karaoke and we cringe.

We cringe when we see something so awkward, embarrassing, or painfully lacking in self-awareness that it makes us recoil.

But we're attracted to it at the same time because — perhaps — we've experienced similar situations ourselves or we know and care about people who have embarrassed themselves and we felt empathy.

And that's why cringe is also known in psychology as secondhand or vicarious embarrassment. We feel it on behalf of other people as well as their feeling it themselves. And sometimes we just enjoy watching other people suffer in a socially awkward situation.

Cringe has an online community: There are cringe compilations, reaction channels on cringe, comedy and other formats built on people's most cringeworthy moments. And people appear to be hooked.

Stefan Hofmann, a clinical psychologist specializing in social anxiety disorder at Marburg University, Germany, says cringe videos are as addictive as junk food: "If you eat junk food, you want more of it [or] even more outrageous stuff," Hofmann said.

Why we can't we look away from cringe moments

Embarrassment is subjective. A bad grade won't embarrass a person who doesn't care about school, but it can trigger real embarrassment in a person for whom academic success is central to their sense of self, their identity.

"If you see a complete stranger misbehaving in public, you might get angry," said Frieder Paulus, a psychologist and neuroscientist at the University of Lübeck, Germany.

"But if your kid is doing the same stuff, you might feel embarrassed, not only for the kid, but also for yourself," said Paulus, "because [you feel] the behavior of the kid reflects [on] you."

Virtual people: Why you can't always trust what you see To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Embarrassment belongs to a class of emotions called emotional barometers. Emotional barometers include shame, pride, and guilt. They signal a social norm has been broken.

For people to feel embarrassment, they have to be aware of the social norms, the context of the situation, and be aware there is an audience watching them.

Our reactions to embarrassing situations are visible on a brain scan.

"We see failure ... the arousal region [lights] up because something is not okay," said Paulus.

Why cringe is a useful reaction

Matthew Feinberg, a social psychologist at the University of Toronto in Canada, has found that people understand displays of embarrassment as a signal of prosocial behavior.

And that prosocial behavior creates a feeling of trust in the observer — they see that the person who is embarrassed knows they have done something socially awkward or wrong.

The message is: "I did something silly and I want to signal that it wasn't intentional and that I am a good member of society," said Feinberg.

On whether the same logic applies to the person observing someone else's mishap, Feinberg said witnessing embarrassment "triggers a natural response. My mind tells me to respond to that person with sympathy."

Feinberg said vicarious embarrassment may even be a stronger trust signal than being embarrassed yourself: "Possibly … because you're experiencing it even though you didn't do anything. It's an interesting research question that as far as I know hasn't been explored."

Millions followed her — then fake nudes appeared To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Exclusion: The cost of too much cringe

Embarrassment is also an expression of our fear that we may be excluded from a group when we do something embarrassing. For a social species such as that of humans and other animals, that can be dangerous.

"Fear of exclusion and fear of negative evaluation by others is painful psychologically as well as physically," said Hofmann. "It is certainly not the same quality of pain [as physical pain], but it's pain nonetheless."

In Hofmann's clinical work, he has tested so-called "social mishap exposures" in which patients embarrass themselves in an intentional and engineered way in an attempt to disprove the beliefs driving their fear or anxiety.

But cringe isn't something we can simply stop feeling. The emotion, researchers suggest, is involuntary and develops from an early age. And that also goes for associated emotions, such as empathy and trust, but also schadenfreude — not all of our addiction to cringe can be explained as an expression of positive emotion.

Hofmann says some people do experience pleasure when they see other people in embarrassing situations. And this distinction between empathy and schadenfreude also matters. If the pull toward cringe content was only about empathy, watching more of it would make us feel worse over time. But people keep watching cringe videos online.

Edited by: Zulfikar Abbany

World.title: Can PM Modi reconnect with India's Gen Z?
World.content:
Student protests exposed a growing disconnect between PM Narendra Modi's BJP and young Indians. Experts say Instagram reels alone won't close it.

As students filled India's streets to demand accountability from the government, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi seemed to have realized that he needed to connect more effectively with the country's youth.

Modi posted on Instagram a rare selfie video in which he said he was pained by their suffering and promised remedial steps. But it was not enough to satisfy the protesters' concerns, and five Gen Z-style reels later, that gap seems as wide as ever.

"We ain't friends," one comment under the first reel read. It echoed thousands of others reacting to a midnight video drop from the PM.

In one of Modi's lesser-produced videos, he addressed the youth as "friends" before finally speaking about the exam at the center of the protests.

It was the prime minister’s response to the biggest political crisis he has faced in his third term so far, over a cancelled high-stakes medical entrance exam which affected millions of aspirants.

Since the first video, he's improved camera angles and lighting, tried varied backgrounds, and even started and ended the videos himself like a one-man content creator. The response remains tepid.

For Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), the protests came at the peak of its power, but the unrest has dimmed that shine, and the disconnect with the youth is substantial, experts told DW.

Young voices sidelined

In 2024, the average age of MPs elected to India's Parliament reached a record 56 years, which is a problem, said Shipra Baduni, CEO of Young Leaders for Active Citizenship, because there is not much youth representation in the legislature.

The second shift is in the nation's youth politics.

India has traditionally had vibrant youth participation at the university level, where student parties have long been affiliated with national and regional parties.

"Student politics has not only given a pulse check, or given a platform for young people to be able to express frustration, or anger, or dissent," said Baduni. "It's also given some of these parties and leaders today."

"We've seen systematically over the last one decade that it has been cut down," she added. "There is a very evident push to say that students should only study, and there is no need for students to engage in politics."

"Where is the space for a young person to express their frustration? If you go on social media to criticize the government, there is a crackdown. Offices are screening your social media."

But Baduni believes the responsibility to connect with the youth doesn't lie with the central government alone: "It's the job of my ward councillor or my local elected leader to come out and say, 'let me talk to the young people in my locality, what are your concerns?'."

DW reached out to BJP's youth leader for New Delhi and the party's national spokesperson, but did not receive a response from either.

Decoding the Gen Z vibe

Memes and music formed the backbone of reels posted on social media, while some young adults politely made their demands and others used expletives in sing-song slogans.

When the government responded, that response itself became fodder for a new wave of memes and content.

"The BJP does not understand expression of anger through ironic humor/memes, because their strategy was focused on the WhatsApp generation," political scientist and author Amit Julka told DW.

"Even now, let's say the BJP's PR department were to say we are now going to crack the Gen Z code, the result will be fundamentally inorganic."

Over a week after the protests were called off following the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, the national conversation has shifted — not to education reform and preventing paper leaks, but to "misguided youths."

Delhi police crack down on student protests To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Several BJP members and supporters posted messages saying the abuses were against Indian moral codes and had deeply unsettled them. They were referring to a viral video where a teenage girl used abusive language against the Prime Minister and his late mother.

In a reel posted over the weekend, Modi addressed the teenager's words.

"I can fully understand the outrage within society. It comes as a cultural shock to see our daughters using such language," Modi said, adding that he wanted to "forgive them" rather than see them dragged through court proceedings.

Modi's senior ministerial colleague Rajnath Singh said last weekend that the government's "top priority remains to understand our students' genuine concerns, ​address them promptly, and ensure that they know their voices are being heard."

Julka pointed to this episode as one way the BJP can delegitimize dissenters going forward. "There doesn't necessarily need to be an application of coercion. Sometimes even a veiled allusion is enough," he said, adding that Gen Zs were ultimately "vulnerable" youth.

What can bridge the political gap?

Working at the cross-section of youth and policy, Baduni believes the BJP still has non-coercive ways to bridge the gap. First, by staying on topic.

"The agenda of the protest is the systematic failure of the education system in India that has failed so many people. Why are you, even today, not talking about that?" she asked.

Baduni suggested that the BJP government needs to speak with the youth at various civic levels and make constructive changes while refraining from further crackdowns.

"I'm not sure how much of it is going to reverse the dent that has already been made," she said, adding that it could give the BJP a better sense of the issues that matter to young people and help the party begin addressing them.

"If you tell them that they will only be heard if they're disruptive, then there is no incentive for them to not be disruptive," Baduni noted.

Education minister concedes to 'Cockroach' demands, resigns To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Since the protests against the education minister ended, several smaller demonstrations have been reported across India.

In Uttar Pradesh's Fatehpur, hundreds of students staged a peaceful walkout to bring the district's attention to infrastructure gaps. In a government school in western India, students protested to demand more teachers. In Jaipur, three student leaders began an indefinite hunger strike, demanding restoration of student union elections.

As for Modi's series of reels, both Baduni and Julka said the one-sided interaction wasn't a real solution.

"That will just give Gen Z a lot more content on what's wrong with this government," said Baduni.

Edited by: Keith Walker

World.title: Indian court acquits ex-wrestling chief of harassment
World.content:
While the court ruled in lawmaker Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh's favor, female athletes say their legal battle is not over. The case sparked months of protests by India's leading female wrestlers.

An Indian court on Monday acquitted the former head of the country's wrestling federation of sexual harassment and stalking charges brought by female athletes.

Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, a former lawmaker from Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), had denied allegations that he groped wrestlers and demanded sexual favors.

What was the reaction to Singh's acquittal?

Singh's lawyer Rajiv Mohan said the New Delhi court found "inconsistencies" in witness statements and "contradictions on major issues."

"I had complete faith that justice would be done," Singh told reporters after the verdict. "I never considered myself a criminal at all."

Supporters celebrated outside the court by setting off firecrackers, showering Singh with flower petals and offering him sweets.

Leading female wrestler Vinesh Phogat said the women would challenge the ruling in a higher court and continue their legal fight.

India: Khomlainai wrestling unites hostile communities To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

"It took a great deal of courage for us to take to the streets and get a complaint registered against a powerful leader of the ruling party," she wrote on X.

What is the significance of the case?

The allegations triggered months of protests in New Delhi in 2023, led by prominent athletes including Phogat, Olympic bronze medalist Sakshi Malik and Olympic medalist Bajrang Punia.

Hundreds joined sit-in demonstrations accusing authorities of failing to act against Singh.

Malik later retired from wrestling in protest, while Punia returned one of India's highest civilian honors.

Delhi police charged Singh in 2023 after sustained pressure from the protesting wrestlers.

A court formally brought charges against him in 2024 over allegations involving five women.

Singh completed his parliamentary term that year and was not selected to run again. The BJP instead fielded his son from the same constituency, which he won.

World.title: What happens next for Infantino and FIFA?
World.content:
FIFA President Gianni Infantino is under pressure after the failure of his plan to create a commercial subsidiary for the World Cup. But will he be ousted? And what is needed for that to happen?

Now that Gianno Infantino has shelved his plans to create a commercial subsidiary for the World Cup and other FIFA events, UEFA's boycott of FIFA events is over and matches now appear less in danger. Nevertheless, the European governing body says it is now "rebuilding trust" with FIFA — and the story continues to develop rapidly.

As a result, increased focus will be put on women's football when the U20 World Cup starts on September 5 in Poland, and when the U17 World Cup starts in October in Morocco. There are also matches around the world that will decide the qualifiers for next summer's World Cup in Brazil in the same month. Despite there being scant mention in FIFA's subsidiary proposal of the women's game, it will be the first test of life after it.

While a boycott is now off the table, the games will be harder to navigate given the current chaos around the sport's governing body. This is far from ideal for the teams competing, particularly given the tournament's importance.

FIFA revolt: Can Infantino's Trump connection save him? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Football associations have pull support for Infantino

With UEFA, Europe's football governors, forming a united front, it is assumed that most, if not all, football associations on the continent will withdraw their support in the coming days.

The first nation to publicly drop their support for Gianni Infantino was Finland, last week. Wales followed on Monday, saying in a statement that "failing to put the best interests of football first is a failure we cannot accept," before England followed suit later in the day.

Germany's FA (DFB) is the biggest sports association in the world, but has yet to officially withdraw its support. It is expected to though, especially when considering the recent words of DFB Director Andreas Rettig. The 63-year-old recently told Stern magazine in an interview that Infantino's recent actions have led to "an irreparable loss of trust" and that football needs to "hit the reset button. We need a different culture. Because trust is the hardest currency."

"From my perspective, Mr. Infantino has invested a great deal of time, money, and energy into maintaining his power structure. Clearly, many decisions served primarily to consolidate his own position," added Retting.

FIFA presidential election next year

The election for Infantino's post is on March 18, 2027, at the 77th FIFA Congress in Rabat, Morocco.

He will run for re-election as president for a final four-year term, looking to gain 106 votes from FIFA's 211 member states (Uefa has 55 votes, Africa 54, Asia 46, Concacaf 35, Oceania 11 and Conmebol 10) to win. Each state gets a vote and voting is done in a secret ballot, which takes time.

However, it seems as though Infantino is increasingly under pressure, and if 19 of the 37 members of the FIFA Council, the organization's main executive body, call for an emergency meeting in the next two weeks, he could be asked to resign. Several members of the council, including Germany's Bernd Neuendorf, have publicly crititcized Infantino for failing to consult them about his latest plans.

There might also be an Extraordinary FIFA Congress if 43 associations formally request it. Given that UEFA has 55 members, it holds the power to request it at any time. For Infantino to be voted out through a vote of no confidence, 106 votes would be required.

Before his venture to sell stakes in FIFA competitions to private investors ended in chaos after widespread condemnation, Infantino looked almost certain to win re-election. The reported revenues from this summer's World Cup were $15 billion (€13 billion), a significantly higher number than expected and one that would have strengthened his position in the organization, given that much of it would be redistibuted among the member organizations.

No clear candidates to succeed Infantino

There has been a lot of speculation about who might succeed Infantino since his position has come under threat in the last week, but it is too soon to really know the legitimacy of any claims. In any case, any potential challengers must declare their candidacy by 18 November.

Nasser Al-Khelaifi, the Paris Saint-Germain chairman, had been touted as a potential candidate given his increasingly influential position in world football. However, the Qatari recently ruled himself out, with a representative for the executive reportedly saying via Politico: "Nasser has absolutely no ambition, no intention, no interest in the Fifa role." Qatar is one of the few federations to have publicly backed Infantino in recent days.

The most obvious candidate is the current UEFA President, Alexander Ceferin, but the Slovenian lawyer is reportedly also not interested in the role.

Concacaf (the confederation of North and Central America and the Caribbean) president Victor Montagliani is one of the few candidates who has expressed interest in the role in the past, but it is unclear whether the man who speaks English, French, Italian and Spanish is ready to challenge now.

Outspoken Norwegian FA President Lise Klaveness has supporters, and, after an initial failure, reached the UEFA Executive Committee in 2025. But the outspoken style that has won her admirers is thought not to have the broad appeal needed in a FIFA candidate. Some also believe her gender may count against her.

Finally, AFC chief, Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, who lost out to Infantino in the 2016 election, could be a contender if the AFC breaks ranks from FIFA in the way UEFA have. A member of Bahrain’s ruling House of Khalifa, the 60-year-old called Infantino's actions "totally unacceptable" and may be tempted to go against him again, though human rights questions contributed to his previous defeat.

Edited by: Matt Pearson

World.title: Russia: Bridge-building with North Korea
World.content:
In the far east, well away from world events, Russia and North Korea are building their first road connection. The project has set alarm bells ringing in Ukraine.

For years, Khasan was little more than a very remote place on the edge of Russia. Less than 500 people live in the village in the country's far east, more than 5,600 miles (9,012 kilometers) from Moscow. But it's here that Russia shares a mere 10.5-mile border with North Korea — and Khasan is the only Russian settlement along that short stretch. Since 1959, the so-called Korean-Russian Friendship Railway Bridge has crossed the Tumen River here, serving as the only land connection between the two countries.

But in recent years, Russia and North Korea have been building a parallel road bridge just a few hundred yards away. The bridge is now nearing completion ahead of schedule, raising concerns in Kyiv that Russia could use it to secretly bring North Korean troops to the front lines in Ukraine.

Since the start of Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Moscow and Pyongyang haveimproved their ties. Both countries face Western sanctions and are diplomatically largely isolated. In June 2024, Russian President Vladimir Putin and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un signed a strategic partnership deal which in part focused on expanding military cooperation. That meant large-scale weapons shipments as well as the deployment of North Korean soldiers to support Russia's war in Ukraine. At the same time, both governments agreed to build the new road bridge.

"The opening of the new bridge will boost bilateral trade, optimize logistics, strengthen cultural ties and transform border regions into dynamically growing economic centers," Russian Transport Minister Andrey Nikitin said at the time.

Not particularly attractive to tourists: until now, the only crossing over the border river was an old, single-lane "Railway Bridge of Friendship." Image: Yuri Smityuk/TASS/picture alliance

The Washington-based Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) has also pointed to the bridge's economic significance, noting that "the pace at which construction of the road bridge is progressing, and the continued high level of rail traffic at previously dormant rail yards, are clear indicators of the importance and expansion of trade between the two countries during Russia's ongoing war against Ukraine."

A project for trade and tourism?

But according to British newspaper The Guardian , there are major doubts that civilian economic goals are the project's true primary purpose.

Official data shows that trade between Russia and North Korea amounted to just $34 million in 2024. The bridge and its immediate infrastructure are thought to cost roughly $100 million. Satellite pictures of the site show warehouses, customs facilities, truck areas and a helicopter pad being built.

Cultivating a "strategic partnership": North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and Russian President Vladimir Putin. Image: Sergey Bobylev/Sputnik/REUTERS

Ukrainian human rights organization Truth Hounds, which has been monitoring the project , also doubts the bridge is for tourism. It is about 125 hours by car from Moscow and about four hours from Vladivostok.

"Tourism in North Korea is heavily restricted and, given the country's isolation, cannot expand rapidly," the organization said. If anyone from Russia would visit North Korea, they probably would go to the capital, Pyongyang, rather than the country's remote northeastern region. But Pyongyang is hundreds of miles from the border, and "few people would want to make that journey by car," the group argued.

Russia has spent years trying to get tourists to take heavily subsidized flights to visit Pyongyang. However, not many have taken up the opportunity. In 2025, fewer than 10,000 Russian citizens are thought to have traveled to North Korea.

Here, the boss makes the beds himself: Kim Jong Un inspects a tourist hotel. But demand from Russians for holidays in North Korea is rather low. Image: YONHAP NEWS AGENCY/picture alliance

Or a cover for military transport?

Truth Hounds instead concludes that the bridge's real purpose is to deepen military cooperation, particularly by facilitating the transfer of North Korean troops and weapons for the war in Ukraine.

According to unofficial information reported by South Korean, Ukrainian and US sources in the middle of last year, North Korea sent between 14,000 and 15,000 personnel to support Russia's war, with many reportedly deployed in Russia's Kursk region while parts of it were under Ukrainian control. North Korea has also supplied Russia with weapons.

Road transport, Truth Hounds suggests, is harder to monitor by satellite than rail transport. Trains are confined to fixed tracks, and loading and unloading can take place only at designated rail hubs. Trucks however, can load and unload almost anywhere and satellite surveillance is virtually impossible.

Ukrainian sources published this image in October 2024. It reportedly shows North Korean soldiers being issued Russian uniforms at a Siberian military training ground. Image: Ukraine Photo/Newscom/picture alliance

Just days ago, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned on X that Russia could deploy as many as 30,000 additional North Korean troops in the war against Ukraine.

Military know-how for North Korea

Zelenskyy also argued that North Korean leader Kim Jong Un from the improved military partnership. The new bridge could enable Russia to secretly move resources into North Korea.

"Russia," Zelenskyy wrote, "is helping North Korea learn how to wage modern war, improve its weapons and gain real combat experience in using them."

Observers also believe that North Korea might be receiving some Russian nuclear technology in exchange for helping Moscow in its war efforts.

Taken together, Zelenskyy warned in his X post, these developments pose "a threat to everyone in Asia who lives within range of North Korean missiles."

This article has been translated from German.

World.title: Germany news: Calls intensify to consider Meta Glasses ban
World.content:
08/03/2026 August 3, 2026 Southampton boss reveals threats after spying scandal

Southampton coach Tonda Eckert said he had not been prepared for such a strong backlash Image: Cody Froggatt/empics/picture alliance

The German manager of English football club Southampton, Tonda Eckert, has spoken about receiving threats serious enough for police involvement after a spying scandal broke.

The affair emerged in May after a Southampton employee was seen watching Middlesbrough train ahead of the two clubs' Championship playoff semifinal.

When news of the illicit surveillance came to light, the English second-tier club was thrown out of the playoffs that could have given it a chance to return to the Premier League. It was also docked four points for the upcoming season, leaving some of the club's fans outraged.

"You are not prepared for something like that," the 33-year-old told German sports magazine Kicker.

Eckert said he was barely active on social media, which helped, but people still found ways to reach him.

"I don't want to go into details, but I was advised not to drive myself anymore and instead sit in the back of the car. That was very difficult," he said.

Eckert took responsibility for the incident and is now under investigation by England's Football Association. Eckert said he had not realized that what he authorized was prohibited but accepted that he should have known the rules.

"Above all, there was a constant, racing stream of thoughts. As head coach, I'm responsible for a decision that we deeply regret," he said.

The club has continued to back the Berlin-born coach.

World.title: Ceuta calcula que tendrá que atender a más de mil menores migrantes y prepara dos grandes instalaciones
World.content:
El Gobierno de Ceuta, desbordado por la entrada masiva del pasado jueves, trata de ampliar su capacidad de acogida mediante la reorganización de sus instalaciones y el acondicionamiento de una construcción industrial y una nave. Con estos espacios busca dar cobijo a los 862 menores migrantes a los que atiende desde la llegada multitudinaria, aunque las autoridades creen que podría haber “algunos más en la calle”, una cifra que todavía no ha podido cuantificarse. El Ejecutivo ceutí da por hecho que el número de menores seguirá aumentando hasta rondar el millar y prevé solicitar al Gobierno central una mayor dotación económica para hacer frente a la emergencia. De momento, y hasta que esos lugares estén convenientemente acondicionados, algo que prevén que se consiga “en las próximas horas o en los próximos días”, los chicos se encuentran en las instalaciones de las que dispone la ciudad, algo apretados, según explica el consejero de Presidencia, Alberto Gaitán, responsable del área de Menores. Los menores que pasaron las primeras horas durmiendo en la puerta de una nave que la ciudad ha acondicionado cerca de la frontera de El Tarajal han sido asistidos y los están reubicando, asegura Gaitán.

En estos últimos días no ha habido traslados extraordinarios de menores a la península, que requieren una serie de trámites, aunque se solicitarán. Los servicios de la ciudad, habituados en los dos últimos años a la entrada de menores migrantes a nado, han multiplicado sus gestiones dando asistencia a los chicos con comida, ropa o alojamiento y reubicándolos. “Estamos preparando recursos para tenerlos en las condiciones más cómodas”, detalla Gaitán. Aunque todavía quedan algunos menores en las calles de la ciudad, asegura que se está peinando la ciudad para localizarlos. Los más pequeños, y sobre los que no hay duda de que son menores, han sido albergados en mejores condiciones, mientras que los mayores se han ubicado en lugares con características provisionales.

La atención a los menores tiene un gran peso en la ciudad fronteriza. Solo hay que ver que la plantilla dedicada a esta área, de unos 250 funcionarios, es muy similar a la de la Policía Local, formada por unos 290 agentes. Esto demuestra, según Gaitán, que es un área a la que dan “mucha importancia” y con unas necesidades de cobertura diferentes a otros municipios.

Es habitual que algunos niños se refugien durante un tiempo en casas de familiares y conocidos y luego acudan a los servicios de la ciudad, por lo que no se descarta que la cifra vaya aumentando. La expectativa de que finalmente tengan que asumir la tutela de entre 1.000 y 1.100 menores se ha calculado teniendo en cuenta la experiencia de 2021, cuando se produjo otra entrada masiva en la ciudad autónoma, en la que entraron irregularmente entre 10.000 y 12.000 personas.

Mediante el mecanismo del traslado de menores, que comenzaron a aplicar a finales de septiembre del año pasado, la ciudad ha derivado a la península a 655 chicos. “Llegamos a estar a mediados del mes de julio en 200 menores”, detalla Gaitán. Conforme pasaban los días, iban aumentando las entradas de niños y adolescentes que accedían a nado hasta llegar a los 862 que albergan este lunes. El Gobierno ceutí insiste en que ellos ya estaban dando la voz de alarma de que algo estaba ocurriendo, que había una “importante” entrada de menores a nado. “Alertamos de que la situación se estaba complicando y que algo podría pasar”, remacha su consejero.

En los próximos días comenzarán a tramitar traslados de menores al amparo del Real Decreto Ley 2/2025 sobre infancia y migración, con el que se modificó la ley orgánica, para derivar a los chicos cuanto antes. “Nosotros no tenemos cómo albergarlos”, insiste. “Es el mecanismo que tenemos y habrá que seguir usándolo para aliviar la situación en Ceuta”, añade.

Su capacidad ordinaria, fijada por el Ministerio de Juventud e Infancia en 29 plazas, se encuentra ampliamente desbordada, con una ocupación que roza el 3.000% de su cabida. “2.865, números redondos”, precisa. “Esta es una situación inasumible, desborda todas nuestras capacidades y exige una respuesta lo más rápidamente posible”, reclama.

Uno de los edificios que están acondicionando es una amplia nave industrial, como la que usan desde 2024, cuando también se produjeron numerosas entradas de menores, y que se encuentra en el Polígono de El Tarajal. Por aquel entonces, la ciudad ya advertía, como sigue haciendo ahora, que no podían asumir tal llegada de menores en solitario y reclamaba ayuda al Gobierno.

En la última conferencia sectorial de infancia y adolescencia, celebrada el pasado 16 de julio, se acordó el reparto de 5,5 millones de euros para que Ceuta pudiera atender a los menores migrantes del fondo de 35 millones aprobado para las comunidades autónomas. Ahora han reclamado que esa cifra suba de manera significativa.

Melilla acoge por su parte a 344 menores extranjeros no acompañados en sus centros de protección, algo más del doble de lo que tenía antes de declararse la crisis en Ceuta. En declaraciones recogidas por Efe, el presidente de la ciudad autónoma, Juan José Imbroda, ha recordado este lunes que sus instalaciones están concebidas para acoger a 84 personas y que el Gobierno debería hacerse cargo “de los que exceden” ese límite.

World.title: Cayetana Álvarez de Toledo: “Todavía no he entendido lo de Ayuso y el ático”
World.content:
El audio de esta noticia utiliza una voz sintética generada por Inteligencia Artificial y podría tener algunas inconsistencias.

La diputada del PP confiesa que no lee mucho los argumentarios del partido y que le gustaría ser ministra: “Estoy aquí para hacer gran política, no para ser una espectadora”

Cayetana Álvarez de Toledo (Madrid, 51 años) es historiadora, periodista y política; española, argentina y francesa; marquesa y diputada del PP. Plantó por carta a Mariano Rajoy, votó a Ciudadanos y ganó un duelo en diferido a Pablo Casado, que la destituyó como portavoz parlamentaria en 2020. De momento, aún confía en Alberto Núñez Feijóo, que la recuperó para agitar los debates en el Congreso. Tituló su primer libro Políticamente indeseable (2021). El segundo, A los españoles que quieren serlo, lo publica este otoño. La entrevista se realiza en el Hipódromo de La Zarzuela: “Crecí en Argentina, entre choripanes y caballos criollos. Este edificio, muy desconocido, es deslumbrante. Adoro la arquitectura racionalista, que une razón, belleza y verdad”.

Pregunta. Se define como “feminista amazónica”, de la escuela de Camille Paglia, la mujer que dijo que “no hay un Mozart femenino por la misma razón por la que no hay un Jack el Destripador femenino” y que describió a la cantante Taylor Swift como “barbie elitista nazi”. ¿Qué diferencia cree que hay entre lo políticamente correcto y lo correcto políticamente o lo correcto a secas?

Respuesta. Paglia es una mujer libérrima que cambió la concepción del feminismo, avanzando en la idea de una mujer valiente, no victimista, capaz de conquistar con sus armas de mujer cualquier meta. Lo políticamente correcto es una censura o autocensura, disfrazar la verdad por tabúes impuestos por la sociedad, y lo correcto o lo correcto políticamente es atreverse a decir la verdad en las circunstancias más difíciles. Yo reclamo mi derecho a ofender y a ser ofendida. La tolerancia es la base de una sociedad democrática.

P. ¿Quiénes son sus referentes femeninos? ¿A qué mujeres del pasado o del presente admira más?

R. A Camille Paglia y a María Corina Machado [opositora venezolana], una gran luchadora que entiende que no hay paz sin libertad, sin democracia.

P. Este año se cumplieron diez años del “No te lo perdonaré jamás, Carmena” a propósito de los disfraces de la cabalgata de Reyes de 2016. ¿Ha perdonado ya a Trump por presentar a María Corina Machado como una buena chica que no cae demasiado bien a los venezolanos?

R. No, sigo siendo muy exigente con el Gobierno de los Estados Unidos, en el que veo un sector negocios y un sector principios que compiten entre sí. Lo que queremos es que el sector principios se imponga, no que se sustituya un régimen cleptocrático por otro. Concebir Venezuela como un botín no es defender la democracia en Venezuela.

Otegi, Junqueras, Puigdemont... son tan españoles como yo y yo soy tan española como Lamine Yamal o como Santiago Abascal Cayetana Álvarez de Toledo

P. ¿Le da miedo al PP hablar de Trump?

R. A nadie debería darle miedo hablar de Trump. No debemos dejarnos llevar por el fanatismo, el sectarismo y la polarización. A las personas hay que juzgarlas por los hechos y conductas, no por sus teóricos alineamientos ideológicos. Lo peor de la polarización es que a veces te lleva a perdonar a los tuyos aquello que condenarías en los de enfrente. Y eso no lo podemos permitir.

P. ¿Eso ya ha pasado?

R. Pasa a diario en todos lados. Las democracias se ven completamente sacudidas por espirales de polarización y la polarización no es un accidente, sino una estrategia deliberada promovida desde el poder por un motivo: divide y vencerás. Cuando tu fin es el poder absoluto, tu medio es la polarización. Ese es el famoso muro que anunció Pedro Sánchez: demonizas la alternativa, la llamas fascista, ultra, franquista... para impedir que algunos de los tuyos se pasen al otro lado.

P. ¿Su lado no demoniza?

R. Hay una fosa en la democracia española: el acuerdo del Gobierno con un partido que no condena el asesinato político, una línea roja moral que nadie se había atrevido a cruzar. Si me preguntara con mi añorado Mario Vargas Llosa cuándo se jodió esta legislatura, diría que cuando el PSOE decidió pactar el Gobierno con quienes no condenan el asesinato.

P. Si EH Bildu no condenase la violencia, no estaría donde está porque incumpliría la Ley de partidos.

R. Es que incumplen la Ley partidos. Lo extraordinario de la democracia española es su inmensa generosidad con quienes buscan destruirla. La grandeza de España es que no exige adhesiones sentimentales para ser español. Otegi, Junqueras, Puigdemont... son tan españoles como yo y yo soy tan española como Lamine Yamal o como Santiago Abascal.

Álvarez de Toledo, el pasado jueves, en el hipódromo de La Zarzuela. INMA FLORES

P. Dice en Políticamente indeseable: “Conozco la muerte política y la desafío como Cyrano de Bergerac, espada en alto”. Quienes la critican dentro del PP suelen aludir a su independentismo, a que va por libre. ¿Cuándo fue, si la hubo, la última vez que hizo caso a un argumentario?

R. Nunca. Yo defiendo a capa y espada el espíritu crítico y la voz libre. Hemos ido hacia una partitocracia donde las cúpulas lo controlan absolutamente todo, los partidos quedan cada vez más jibarizados y la voz y el voto del diputado cada vez valen menos. Al tener menos libertad, tiene menos responsabilidad y se vuelve un perfecto irresponsable y, por tanto, perfectamente sustituible. Acepto que exista algo llamado disciplina de voto, porque esto no es una jaula de grillos o una asamblea universitaria, pero la disciplina tiene que ser compatible con mantener la capacidad de cuestionar las decisiones de la dirección. Confieso que los argumentarios los leo muy poquito. Sé que hay gente inteligente haciéndolos y que no es fácil sintetizar las noticias del día en tres o cuatro frases, pero, honestamente, no soy una persona de argumentarios.

P. ¿Llegó a pagar aquella multa por saltarse la disciplina de voto?

R. No. Soy una defensora a muerte de la independencia judicial y me oponía a cualquier reparto de cromos, en este caso en el Tribunal Constitucional. Todavía estaba Casado. Me abrieron un expediente, recurrí explicando que el programa del PP incluía la defensa de la independencia del Poder Judicial y lo que pasó fue que cayó la cúpula entera del PP. Aquel recurso lo gané por la vía de los hechos.

P. ¿Ha entendido lo de Isabel Díaz Ayuso y el ático?

R. No, todavía no.

P. ¿Quién cree que ha sido el mejor presidente del PP y por qué?

R. José María Aznar. Porque ha sido presidente del Gobierno y porque fue capaz de unir todo lo que estaba a la derecha de la izquierda, crear un proyecto político de mayorías. Ese tiene que ser nuestro objetivo. Hace falta una revolución de la decencia. Los españoles han pagado con sus impuestos a las prostitutas de ministros y eso ni siquiera es lo más grave que ha pasado. Hemos visto la constitución de una mafia pagada por el partido del Gobierno para destruir a jueces, fiscales y policías que luchan contra la corrupción.

P. Se refiere al caso Leire, que se está investigando, pero se acaba de juzgar el caso Kitchen.

R. Sí, pero montar una mafia para intentar destruir a jueces, fiscales y policías desde el poder no tiene precedentes. El viejo PSOE utilizó cloacas contra los enemigos del Estado: el GAL, lamentable. El nuevo PSOE las ha utilizado contra los servidores del Estado. La excelente noticia es que hay anticuerpos en España: fiscales, jueces, políticos y periodistas que hacen su trabajo y, sobre todo, hay y lo he visto con el Mundial, una nación esperando ser liderada, deseando iniciar una nueva etapa.

P. Le decepcionaron Mariano Rajoy y Pablo Casado. ¿Cree que le pasará con Alberto Núñez Feijóo? ¿Pone la mano en el fuego por él?

R. No estaría en política y no pediría el voto si no creyera que Fejóo va a ser todo aquello que está prometiendo, esencialmente, promover una gran refundación moral política.

P. ¿Lo puso en cuarentena cuando en 2024 se abrió a un indulto condicionado a Puigdemont o más recientemente, cuando abogó en Cataluña por “pasar página” del procés?

R. Él no abogó por dar indultos a Puigdemont, que decidió hacer presidente a Sánchez porque borró sus delitos de golpe de Estado a cambio del poder en una transacción corrupta sin precedentes. Feijóo ni lo hizo ni lo hará. Tengo una enorme esperanza respecto a lo que podemos hacer en Cataluña: presencia, prestigio, poder y presupuesto para quienes no son nacionalistas; establecer un sistema de incentivos de forma que ser constitucionalista o español en Cataluña tenga premio.

P. Ahora hay un presidente constitucionalista, Salvador Illa, del PSC.

R. Illa es un criptonacionalista: ni una mala palabra ni una buena acción. Es un híbrido entre Zapatero y Sánchez: Tiene el talante del primero y la mala política del segundo.

Soy bastante leal en mis amores, también en los políticos, y eso no quiere decir que no pueda sufrir decepciones Cayetana Álvarez de Toledo

P. Nicolás Sartorius opina que la Ley de amnistía beneficiará al PP porque permitirá restablecer los pactos más naturales entre derechas. ¿Cree que su partido volverá a pactar con Junts como hizo con sus predecesores de CiU? ¿Estaría dispuesta a hablar catalán en la intimidad, como Aznar en su momento?

R. Respeto muchas cosas que dice Sartorius, pero estoy en profundo desacuerdo con ese análisis. La Ley de amnistía lo que hace es desarmar al Estado y, por tanto, no puede beneficiar ni al PP ni al PSOE. Con esa ley Sánchez intentó amnistiarse a sí mismo, igual que con este último indulto a Laura Borràs, que es un escándalo: Sánchez llegó anunciando la regeneración contra la corrupción y acabó promoviendo una internacional cleptocrática que indulta a corruptos políticos.

P. La sentencia del Tribunal de Justicia europeo avala la ley de amnistía y comparte la tesis del Gobierno de que ha favorecido la reconciliación política y social. ¿La comparte usted? ¿Cómo encontró Cataluña la última vez que la visitó?

R. Lo que pacificó Cataluña fue lo que hicieron los policías heroicamente la noche del 1 de octubre [de 2017, durante el referéndum independentista]. El Mundo me envió a Sant Julià de Ramis a ver cómo votaba Puigdemont y vi a la Guardia Civil desarticular todo el operativo, quitar de los hombros de sus padres a niños que estaban siendo utilizados como escudos humanos por nacionalistas desalmados que utilizaban a sus hijos para votar. Los guardias civiles retiraban a los niños, los protegían, los dejaban al margen. Puigdemont no pudo votar. Le pregunté si estaba preparado para ir a la cárcel y no me contestó. Fue el Estado, la Guardia Civil, la Policía, el Tribunal Supremo y el Gobierno de Mariano Rajoy, del que yo discrepé tanto, pero que aplicó el artículo 155, lo que realmente pacificó Cataluña, no la ley de amnistía, que lo que hizo fue envalentonarles.

P. Pero el rechazo a la independencia aumentó en Cataluña después de la Ley de amnistía.

R. Ahora en Cataluña hay un nuevo factor, Aliança Catalana, un spin-off del proceso y una fuerza radicalmente separatista y xenófoba. Lo que pasa es que a muchos españoles incautos les acaba gustando porque el tema de la inmigración es enormemente sensible y polémico en toda Europa y muy particularmente en Cataluña. Mucha gente va a votar a Aliança Catalana pensando que vota a una opción firme contra la inmigración cuando están votando una opción firmemente xenófoba contra el resto de los españoles. El proceso separatista en Cataluña continúa. Y hay otra clave más, el concepto de plurinacionalidad, el nuevo eufemismo que se va a utilizar para la ruptura.

Álvarez de Toledo, en el hipódromo de La Zarzuela. INMA FLORES

P. Un concepto que ha pronunciado más de un dirigente del PP.

R. Sí, alguno ha cometido el error de pronunciarlo. Otegi le está diciendo a Sánchez: Yo te tapo tu corrupción a cambio de que tú me des mi nación y lo vamos a llamar plurinacionalidad porque es más fácil de digerir.

P. ¿Otegi tiene capacidad para tapar los escándalos de corrupción?

R. Al sostener a Sánchez en el poder, tapa su corrupción. Bildu tiene un proyecto político que se llama plurinacionalidad y es la ruptura de la paz civil española y de la democracia. Cuanto más acorralado esté, más avanzará Sánchez en esa dirección.

Mariano Rajoy y Felipe González son bastante similares en muchas cosas Cayetana Álvarez de Toledo

P. Cuando la fichó, Casado dijo que era “la Messi del PP”. Por aquella época, Aznar decía de Casado que era “un líder como un castillo”. ¿Dura menos el amor en política?

R. Soy bastante leal en mis amores, también en los políticos, y eso no quiere decir que no pueda sufrir decepciones. Pero no soy ni de grandes hipérboles ni partidaria del rencor posterior.

P. ¿A quién quiere más: a Rajoy o a Felipe González? ¿Qué discurso le gusta más?

R. Rajoy y Felipe González son bastante similares en muchas cosas. Son defensores del orden constitucional y democrático nacido en 1978, entienden que merece ser preservado. Es la coincidencia entre una socialdemocracia y un liberalconservadurismo.

Si el PP hace todo aquello que debe hacer, Vox dejaría de existir Cayetana Álvarez de Toledo

P. Dijo recientemente en el Congreso: “España vive un eclipse moral, pero volverá a salir el sol”. ¿Hasta qué punto le preocupa que Santiago Abascal haga de luna, o sea, de vicepresidente del Gobierno?

R. Yo prefiero una mayoría absoluta del Partido Popular y trabajo para eso. La gente me mira con incredulidad, pero, socialmente, en España hay una mayoría de centro derecha que quiere una regeneración de la vida pública. ¿Me da miedo que Abascal sea vicepresidente? No, me da mucho más terror tener una continuidad de Sánchez con fuerzas políticas que destruyen el orden democrático y de convivencia.

P. ¿Por qué cree que ha engordado tanto el partido escisión, Vox? ¿Les ha alimentado la matriz, es decir, el PP; la coyuntura o ambas?

R. Si el PP hace todo aquello que debe hacer, Vox dejaría de existir. Si tenemos un gran proyecto político, eso irá diluyendo la fuerza que tiene Vox. Hay una ola en muchos países de la que Vox forma parte, y en contra de la autoflagelación típica de la derecha en España; mientras los clásicos liberalconservadores en Europa están siendo arrasados por las fuerzas a su derecha, el PP está resistiendo de una forma extraordinaria.

Milei puso a trabajar a un país en el que la mentalidad era esperar la paguita Cayetana Álvarez de Toledo

P. Ha compartido charlas y piropos con Iván Espinosa de los Monteros, que abandonó Vox en 2023. ¿Qué ve más probable: que él termine en su partido o usted en el suyo?

R. Iván no tiene partido y no creo que hagan falta más partidos. Soy partidaria de unir por la base. En su día propuse que Inés Arrimadas, que estaba en Ciudadanos y es muy amiga mía, fuera número uno por Barcelona. Si no podemos unirnos entre nosotros, ¿cómo vamos a unir a la nación?

P. Usted votó a Ciudadanos.

R. Sí, cuando me fui del PP.

P. El presidente argentino, Javier Milei, dice que tiene “la peor de las opiniones” sobre usted. ¿Es mutuo?

R. No. Discrepo con él y creo que los liberales tenemos que ser capaces de asumir críticas no solo de los adversarios, sino también de los presuntamente amigos y afines. Yo estoy bloqueada [en redes sociales] por dos personas: Óscar Puente y Javier Milei. Debo ser una centrista. Puente es un marrullero, una persona que ha hecho del insulto una forma de estar en política. No sé si aspira a suceder a Sánchez y cree que así va a conseguir agitar a la militancia, pero yo quiero acabar con esa forma de hacer política. Soy dura y reivindico el ser firme en política, pero creo que las formas perfeccionan la verdad y que hay que tener un respeto por el lenguaje, por el interlocutor e incluso por la belleza en el discurso público.

P. Usted también insulta.

R. Yo no reivindico el derecho a insultar, sí a decir la verdad, por dura que sea.

P. El “me gusta la fruta”, que en realidad era “hijo de puta”, de Isabel Díaz Ayuso a Sánchez, ¿qué le pareció?

R. Ella se lo dijo para sí misma en la tribuna [del Congreso] después de que Sánchez, que ahora reivindica la presunción de inocencia, acusase a su hermano de corrupto. A ella le leyeron los labios.

P. Pero si de eso se hicieron hasta camisetas...

R. Sí, luego, efectivamente, hacen una campaña de reivindicación, hábil propaganda de su entorno. ¿Me gusta? No, yo no utilizo el insulto en la política.

P. ¿Fue un error que Díaz Ayuso entregara a Milei una medalla “por su defensa de la libertad”?

R. Para nada. Milei ha hecho algo admirable en Argentina: una revolución cultural. Les dijo al país: para salir adelante, tenéis que trabajar, no vivir del subsidio. Los políticos populistas que dicen que ellos lo van a pagar todo engañan a la gente y destruyen al país. Argentina era un país destruido con generaciones enteras saliendo al exilio. Lo que le falta es el respeto institucional.

P. ¿No le suena raro mezclar cultura y Milei? Sus discursos son zafios, llenos de insultos.

R. Estoy hablando de algo mucho más profundo. No me gustan sus formas. La intolerancia de la crítica es muy poco liberal. Digo cultural en el sentido de mentalidad: puso a trabajar a un país en el que la mentalidad era esperar la paguita.

P. ¿Cree que Argentina está mejor ahora?

R. Argentina está saliendo del pozo profundísimo en el que lo hundió el populismo.

P. ¿Milei no es un populista?

R. Sus formas pueden ser demagógicas, estridentes y el insulto es intolerable.

P. ¿Dónde se ve en el futuro? ¿Le gustaría dar el salto de las ideas a la gestión?

R. Por supuesto. La gestión son ideas encarnadas. El gran error de la derecha, no solo en España, es pensar que las ideas son una cosa y la gestión, otra. La buena gestión son buenas ideas encarnadas y ese es el objetivo final de cualquier político.

P. ¿Se ve en un ministerio, llevando una cartera?
