World.title: Albanian Graduates Hit Hardest by ‘Outdated’ North Macedonia Ranking System
World.content:
In early 2025, when Emine Haxhiu Memishi applied for the post of Junior Associate at North Macedonia’s Ministry of Economy and Labour, she did so armed with a degree in economics from Istanbul Commerce University, an average grade of 9.88, a year of professional training behind her, and a readiness to return to her homeland when so many like her do not.

There was another grade, however, that Haxhiu Memishi hadn’t factored in, one that did not feature on her diploma, in her grade average, or the recommendation letters written by her professors – 0.5, the coefficient assigned by North Macedonia to any foreign university that does not feature on the three big international rankings lists.

Haxhiu Memishi fell at the very first stage of the recruitment process.

“I felt disappointed and treated unfairly,” the 31-year-old told BIRN.

World.title: Iraq earns $18.6 billion from oil exports in H1 2026
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s State Organization for Marketing of Oil (SOMO) revealed last week that the country’s oil revenues hit $18.67 billion during the first half of 2026 as exports reached approximately 268 million barrels of crude oil.

SOMO data indicated Iraq’s oil exports in the first half of 2025 were 606.58 million barrels, more than double the quantity exported in the same period in 2026.

The reported revenues for just the first four months of 2025 reached nearly $27.514 billion, exceeding the total oil revenues generated during the entire first half of 2026.

The figures show a considerable decline in both crude oil export volumes and income in the first half of 2026 compared to the same time last year.

The Iraqi Ministry of Oil reported last Tuesday that the country’s crude oil exports during May and June 2026 totaled approximately 32.11 million barrels, averaging over 16 million barrels per month.

The country’s oil exports reached 9.88 million barrels in April and around 18.6 million barrels in March.

Iraqi oil export earnings in May and June 2026 reached approximately $2.33 billion, averaging $1.16 billion per month, compared to $1.87 billion in April, $1.95 billion in March, and approximately $6.81 billion in February.

The decline in exported volumes and produced profits coincides with regional tensions that negatively impacted the region’s energy supply chains and maritime traffic in recent months.

World.title: Iraq offers discounts on Basrah crude during August
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s State Organization for Marketing of Oil (SOMO) has offered considerable discounts on Basrah crude during August to attract customers to load shipments from within the Strait of Hormuz, according to a document reviewed by Reuters.

SOMO asked potential term purchasers to designate contractual volumes of Basrah Medium or Basrah Heavy crude for complimentary onboard delivery from the Basrah Oil Terminal or other port-related infrastructure.

SOMO provided discounts ranging between $25 and $27 per barrel on Basrah Medium, according to the loading period. It provided discounts of $27.80 to $29.80 a barrel for Basrah Heavy.

According to shipping statistics released on Monday, maritime activity in the strategic waterway of the Strait of Hormuz has slowed over the weekend due to reports of assaults on vessels.

Maritime traffic in the strait decreased due to ongoing military operations in the region and heightened shipping security risks.

The significant price reduction aims to compensate for rising maritime insurance costs and freight expenses by transferring transit risk to purchasers.

World.title: US forces gradually withdraw from northern Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – US forces have begun a phased withdrawal from Iraqi Kurdistan as part of a plan to redeploy and end their military presence in the country.

Reports indicate that US military convoys have left the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Erbil, in the past few days, heading towards neighboring countries.

The withdrawal is being carried out in successive phases according to a set timetable, while the transfer of equipment and troops from US bases in the region continues.

The US Department of War has not yet issued an official statement regarding the details of these recent movements.

Reports also mentioned that the United States has begun withdrawing its remaining forces from Iraq ahead of the September 30 deadline, with Patriot air defense systems already removed from Erbil.

The pullout comes as regional security concerns rise, with Iranian-backed armed groups continuing to threaten the Kurdistan Region. These assaults have generated fears that reducing the United States’ military presence may make the region more vulnerable to security challenges.

The withdrawal is part of understandings reached between Baghdad and Washington over the past two years to end the mission of the US-led international coalition and transition to a new phase based on bilateral security and military cooperation.

Despite reducing its military presence, the United States has repeatedly affirmed its commitment to continued cooperation with Iraqi forces in training, intelligence sharing, and countering ISIS within a bilateral framework that does not require a large-scale military presence.

The withdrawal begins at a time when tensions in the region have risen in the past few weeks, following military operations by the US and Iran, as well as frequent drone and missile attacks on Iraqi Kurdistan.

World.title: Iraq, Iran discuss developments in the Strait of Hormuz
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein and his Iranian counterpart, Abbas Aragchi, discussed on Sunday the latest developments in the Strait of Hormuz and prospects for regional de-escalation.

In a phone conversation, the two sides evaluated the most recent developments in the Strait of Hormuz during the last two days, as well as the implications for maritime security and regional stability, according to a statement released by the Iraqi Foreign Ministry.

Hussein emphasized Iraq’s support of dialogue and diplomacy as effective approaches to address disagreements and settle unresolved concerns, thereby helping to improve security and stability in the region.

The discussion also addressed the recent military assaults targeting Iraq and the significance of avoiding any actions that may escalate tensions in the region.

Aragchi reviewed the most recent developments and briefed Hussein on ongoing efforts to reach an agreement that would help reopen the Strait of Hormuz and ensure the smooth flow of maritime navigation.

Iraq is closely monitoring ongoing developments and expects to reach agreements that will facilitate the reopening of the Strait as soon as possible. This effort aims to ensure the security and stability of both the region and the global economy, according to Hussein.

Given the rapidly changing situation, Hussein emphasized the necessity of ongoing coordination between the two parties, as well as his support for steps taken to enhance dialogue.

World.title: Three drones target northern Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Three drones targeted the cities of Sulaimaniyah and Erbil in the Kurdistan region of Iraq early on Sunday before they were shot down without causing any casualties.

According to reports, two drones entered the skies over Sulaimaniyah. One of the two drones resulted in a fire that was eventually extinguished.

In Erbil, the C-RAM air defense system destroyed a drone early this morning without causing any damage.

These strikes follow the unexpected 72-hour pullout of US, British, French, and German forces from Erbil International Airport, which included hundreds of troops and heavy air defense equipment.

US forces have begun a phased withdrawal from Iraqi Kurdistan as part of a plan to redeploy and end their military presence in the country.

Reports indicate that US military convoys have departed from Erbil in the past few days, heading toward neighboring countries.

The US Department of War has not yet issued an official statement regarding the details of these recent movements.

The international coalition’s air defense systems in Erbil intercepted several earlier drones targeting the US consulate and its associated logistics base.

The recent escalation in Iraqi Kurdistan, which largely included drone assaults over Erbil, comes amid rising tensions between the United States and Iran, the most serious since a cease-fire deal was reached in mid-June.

World.title: Iraq forms security committee to prevent attacks against neighboring states
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, Ali al-Zaidi, chaired an emergency meeting on Saturday to discuss security developments in the region.

Al-Zaidi emphasized the need to prevent any violation or threat emerging from Iraqi land toward neighboring nations, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The prime minister directed the establishment of a joint security committee to address current challenges and to follow deterrent procedures to prevent attacks or potential violations against neighboring countries.

Al-Zaidi also directed Iraqi security forces to enhance stability, protect sovereignty, and maintain good neighborly relations.

The meeting addressed the Iraqi army’s readiness to counter any attempt to strike neighboring nations, as well as Iraq’s unwavering commitment to prevent the use of its territory to launch attacks against other countries.

The formation of a joint security committee is part of Iraq’s responsibility to preserve national sovereignty and uphold the principles of good neighborliness and international law.

The decision to form this committee follows substantial regional triggering events in recent days.

The United States and Saudi Arabia launched coordinated attacks on targets in several Iraqi provinces. The alliance declared that these were retaliation strikes in response to drone and missile assaults on regional oil infrastructure and military targets.

Prior to the security meeting, Jordan and Syria cautioned Baghdad about Iran-backed armed groups operating in Iraq, warning that cross-border threats would not go unnoticed.

World.title: Iraqi court recovers IQD 20 billion in corruption and money laundering cases
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq’s Rusafa Investigative Court, which specializes in integrity and money laundering cases, has recovered 20 billion Iraqi dinars (approximately $15.3 million) linked to financial corruption, administrative misconduct, and fraud, the country’s judiciary announced on Sunday.

In a statement, the judiciary’s media office said the recovered funds were tied to investigations involving financial and administrative corruption as well as financial fraud.

The court said the recovery forms part of ongoing legal efforts to pursue individuals accused of using illegal methods to obtain profits at the expense of public funds.

Authorities stressed that legal proceedings against those involved remain underway, reaffirming their commitment to combating corruption and protecting state resources.

The judiciary did not disclose additional details regarding the individuals or entities involved, nor did it specify when the alleged offenses occurred.

World.title: US Embassy in Iraq urges Americans to leave the Middle East
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The US Embassy in Baghdad and the US Consulate General in Erbil advised American citizens on Saturday to leave the Middle East as tensions in the region remained high.

The US mission said in a statement that due to heightened tensions in the Middle East, the security environment remains complex with the potential for unforeseen escalation.

The mission added that Americans presently in the Middle East should exercise extreme caution and alertness and be prepared for flight cancellations, frequent airspace closures, and possible travel difficulties.

Some regional airlines have postponed the restart of previously scheduled flights, while others have cancelled some routes.

Americans in the region are advised to consider departing or to be ready to leave if tensions escalate.

In a statement, the US Embassy in Baghdad advised that those who choose to travel to or from the region should closely monitor updates regarding airport and airline operations.

US diplomatic installations, especially those outside the Middle East, have been attacked. Iran and pro-Iran groups may attack additional US interests abroad or at areas connected with the US and Americans across the world, such as US corporations and institutions, according to the statement.

The Iranian leadership is unpredictable, as seen by recent moves to strike regions without notice, as well as to expand assaults to previously untargeted territories such as Egypt, according to the US Embassy in Iraq.

The US Embassy advised Americans to remain vigilant, as the absence of past attacks on US interests or businesses in a country does not ensure their safety.

World.title: India gets 101st 'Ramsar' site as Arunachal Pradesh's Glaw Lake joins elite global list of protected wetlands
World.content:
Glaw Lake in Himachal Pradesh

NEW DELHI: Indiaâs one more wetland, Glaw Lake of Arunachal Pradesh, has entered the global list of protected wetlands as a Ramsar site. It is the countryâs 101st such site and the stateâs first to join the elite club for additional care and conservation.Located within the Kamlang Tiger Reserve and Wildlife Sanctuary, Glaw Lake is a pristine freshwater lake in the Eastern Himalayas and a biodiversity hotspot. The lake is fed by perennial mountain streams and is surrounded by lush vegetation, supporting rich floral diversity.âEvery new Ramsar site strengthens our resolve to protect nature while securing the future of communities that depend on these invaluable ecosystems,â said Union environment minister Bhupender Yadav while announcing the development on X on Monday.The Glaw Lake wetland has over 150 tree species and 49 orchid species recorded within the site and its catchment, underscoring its ecological significance and surrounding landscape.âFrom 26 Ramsar sites in 2014 to 101 today, this remarkable journey reflects our unwavering commitment to environmental protection, biodiversity conservation, and sustainable development,â said Yadav.Globally, there are nearly 2,600 such designated wetlands under the Ramsar Convention.India has the highest number of such wetlands in Asia and third highest in the world after the UK (176) and Mexico (144).Wetlands are land areas covered by water, either temporarily/ seasonally or permanently. These are critical ecosystems that play a significant role in supporting biodiversity, and providing various ecosystem services such as flood control, water supply, food, fibre and raw materials.

World.title: SKM to restart farmers' protests at 100 locations, including Delhi, from November 26
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Emboldened by the success of the studentsâ protests here at Jantar Mantar, the Samyukt Kisan Morcha (SKM)âthe umbrella organisation of farmer groups involved in the anti-farm laws agitation five years agoâon Monday announced that it would restart protests at 100 locations, including Delhi, across India from November 26 - the day which will mark the sixth anniversary of the year-long farmersâ protest, which culminated in the repeal of the three farm laws in December 2021.

The protests will demand a law guaranteeing minimum support price (MSP), repeal of all free trade agreements and no India-US FTA, and a comprehensive loan waiver to address rural indebtedness.

The SKMâs demand list also includes four other demands such as scrapping of four labour codes; minimum wage of Rs. 31,000 payable to all workers as well as restoration of the previous rural job guarantee scheme; withdrawal of Electricity Privatisation Bill 2025, the Seed Bill 2025, and the NFSA Amendment Bill; and no forceful land acquisition.

World.title: NDA states acted firmly against recruitment scams; opposition failed to curb irregularities: CM Dhami
World.content:
on Monday said that NDA-ruled states have taken firm action against recruitment scams and examination-related irregularities, while alleging that opposition-ruled states failed to curb such malpractices and were marked by widespread irregularities in recruitment processes.

Speaking to reporters here, Dhami said that the Uttarakhand government had acted decisively against the "cheating mafia" by arresting and jailing over 100 people and enacting a stringent anti-cheating law.

"In all NDA-ruled states, wherever instances of cheating occurred, action was taken against the perpetrators. In Uttarakhand, we took action against a hundred members of the 'cheating mafia,' jailed them, and enacted a law specifically to curb cheating.

Furthermore, recruitment drives were conducted and fully completed in strict accordance with the scheduled calendar," Dhami said.

The Chief Minister contrasted this with states such as Jharkhand and Punjab and also referred to the previous Samajwadi Party government in Uttar Pradesh, alleging that recruitment processes between 2012 and 2017 were marred by irregularities.

"In contrast, consider states like Jharkhand, Punjab, or others.





Previously, between 2012 and 2017, Uttar Pradesh witnessed massive irregularities in recruitment and widespread cheating," he said.

Targeting opposition parties, Dhami alleged that the Congress, Samajwadi Party, Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), and their alliance partners were responsible for such irregularities.

"Be it the Congress Party, the Samajwadi Party, the AAP, or any of their alliance partners--they are the ones who committed all these wrongs, and the youth of the country understands this," he said.

Referring to the Prime Minister's approach towards young people allegedly involved in such incidents, Dhami said the focus was on taking action against the masterminds rather than punishing those who may have been influenced.

"The PM chose not to subject these young people, who may have been misled or misguided for whatever reason, to legal hassles or punishment; instead, he forgave them," Dhami said.

Launching a sharp attack on Opposition leaders following the registration of an FIR against Congress MP Rahul Gandhi, Independent MP Pappu Yadav, and Samajwadi Party MP Awadhesh Prasad over an alleged insult to Sanatan Dharma, Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Monday stated that defaming saints represents the "lowest form of conduct imaginable."

Addressing reporters in Dehradun, CM Dhami condemned the actions of the leaders, alleging that Pappu Yadav and his associates have consistently worked to malign Sanatan Dharma.

"To defame the saints is the lowest form of conduct imaginable. I had stated earlier as well that Pappu Yadav and the 'Pappu gang' have been working in tandem to continuously malign Sanatan Dharma," CM Dhami said.

Taking a dig at the Opposition leaders over their stance on religious events, the Chief Minister pointed out that despite being extended invitations to the historic Ram Mandir Pran Pratishtha ceremony, none of them attended.

"When the Ram Mandir was being built, they were invited to the event, yet none of them attended; and today, they are engaging in this manner to defame our community of saints. I believe this reveals their true mindset regarding Sanatan Dharma," Dhami added.

Highlighting his state administration's public outreach programs, Chief Minister Dhami also elaborated on the progress of the state government's 'Jan-Jan ki Sarkar' initiative.

He emphasised that the drive is designed to bridge the gap between governance and citizens, especially those residing in remote regions.

"The objective of the 'Jan-Jan ki Sarkar' initiative is to bring the entire government administrative machinery to the people to resolve their issues," CM Dhami said. World.title: TRAI revamps 'TRAI MyCall' mobile app to assess voice call quality
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The

has revamped the "TRAI MyCall', a mobile application that enables telecom consumers to directly assess and report the voice-calling experience. A citizen-centric digital platform that allows telecom consumers to share real-time feedback on their voice-calling experience, TRAI MyCall app gives telecom service providers (TSPs) information on areas where network performance needs improvement and take targeted corrective measures.

TRAI says the revamped app offers instant rating of voice calls through a simple 1-5 star feedback system; reporting of specific issues such as call drops, echo during calls, audio delay, cross connection, voice breaking, one party unable to hear the other, and calls taking too long to connect, which shall be available to respective service provider for corrective action; automatic post-call feedback and coverage test feature to assess signal strength.

TRAI chairman Anil Kumar Lahoti said: âEvery telecom consumer experiences network quality first-hand. The revamped TRAI MyCall app is expected to strengthen consumer participation feedback on telecom service quality by enabling subscribers to provide immediate and perceived feedback on their call experience. The feedback will assist Telecom Service Providers in identifying network deficiencies and taking corrective measures, enhanced customer satisfaction, and a better overall mobile communication experience.

The initiative reinforces TRAI's commitment to a consumer-centric, transparent, and data-driven approach to improving the quality of telecom services. I encourage all mobile users to download the TRAI MyCall application and regularly share their feedback. Every feedback matters, and together we can build a better calling experience for every telecom consumer.â

âWith over one billion telecom subscribers in India, voice calling remains the most fundamental telecom service and is often the first indicator of network quality experienced by consumers. World.title: NEET (UG) protests: Gujarat latest BJP-ruled state to order withdrawal of FIRs against demonstrators
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Gujarat government has directed the state police to withdraw all criminal cases registered against students, youths, and others who took part in recent protests over the alleged NEET-UG examination paper leak, officials said on Monday.

With this, Gujarat has become the latest BJP-ruled state to order withdraw of cases against NEET protesters. Similar decisions have already been taken by the BJP governments in Assam, Bihar, Delhi, and Maharashtra.

In a July 31 letter to the state Director General of Police GS Malik, the Gujarat home department cited the Supreme Court's July 28 judgment restraining police from taking coercive action against minor student protesters and directed the immediate withdrawal of all existing cases.

The department instructed the police not to initiate any adverse legal or penal action against individuals who participated in the protests in the state. It further directed that if any FIRs or criminal cases had already been registered against protesters, the legal process for their withdrawal should be completed immediately.

The communication, however, did not specify how many FIRs or criminal cases would be withdrawn.





Protests were held in Gujarat's Ahmedabad and several other cities in support of demonstrations at Delhi's Jantar Mantar against alleged irregularities in the NEET-UG examination.

The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), an online satirical outfit that had been leading an indefinite sit-in at Jantar Mantar since June 21, called off its protest on July 25 following the resignation of then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.

Besides seeking Pradhan's resignation, the CJP had demanded that no action be taken against its members or any NEET protesters across the country.

The CJP has repeatedly warned that it would resume its agitation if the FIRs are not withdrawn.

Meanwhile, the Supreme Court also clarified on Monday that the expression "criminal antecedents" in its July 28 order on releasing student protesters referred only to those involved in grave and heinous offences, and said states could close or withdraw FIRs against the remaining students in accordance with law.

World.title: 'Want to place NEET question paper safeguards on record': Centre tells SC
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Centre on Monday told the Supreme Court that it wants to place on record the process and safeguards adopted right from the printing of the NEET question paper to its distribution among students.

Appearing for the Centre, Solicitor General (SG) Tushar Mehta informed a bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe that the government would explain the methodology and place it on record through an affidavit. Mehta sought time for hearing on Thursday or Friday.

The bench replied that it would also like to know the process and posted a batch of pleas seeking additional safeguards for NEET question papers for hearing on Thursday.

During an earlier hearing on June 24 too, the Supreme Court had said it would "closely monitor" the steps taken to curb future NEET examination paper leaks.

The top court was then hearing a batch of petitions, including one filed by the Federation of All India Medical Association (FAIMA). It told Mehta that the government should indicate the steps taken towards ensuring transparency, implementing the recommendations of the Radhakrishnan Committee and following the IIT model.





"Students' futures can't be jeopardised. We are going beyond the Radhakrishnan Committee. I assure you that the government is walking 10 extra miles. I can assure you everything is being supervised at the highest level," the ASG had submitted at the time.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

On May 12, the National Testing Agency (NTA) cancelled the NEET-UG examination held on May 3 amid allegations of a paper leak. The retest was conducted on June 21.

The paper leak allegations are being investigated by the CBI.

After allegations of NEET-UG question paper leaks in 2024, the Supreme Court had refused to cancel the medical entrance test but issued various directions aimed at preventing paper leaks and laid down criteria for cancelling public examinations.

Following the 2024 leak, the ministry of education had constituted a seven-member committee headed by former Isro chief K Radhakrishnan to recommend reforms in the examination process, improvement in data security protocols, and the structure and functioning of the NTA.

World.title: How Prashant Kishor breached BJP's bastion
World.content:
The first electoral verdict after the nationwide Gen Z protests has delivered one of the biggest political surprises in recent years.

has lost Bankipur, one of its safest seats in Bihar, to

, giving Jan Suraaj its first-ever electoral victory.

The result carries significance beyond a single assembly bypoll. It is also the first major electoral test for BJP in Bihar under the leadership of CM Samrat Choudhary after he assumed charge of the state government. The outcome suggests that the party failed to retain its grip over a constituency that had remained virtually impregnable for three decades.

The fall of a BJP fortress

Bankipur has been synonymous with BJP's dominance since 1995.

The party won the seat four consecutive times through Navin Sinha before his son, BJP national president Nitin Nabin, retained it for five successive elections.

The constituency had long been regarded as one of BJP's safest urban seats. Nitin Nabin secured more than 50% of the vote in every election he contested, including around 63% in the 2025 Assembly election. Against that backdrop, the bypoll result represents a dramatic political reversal.





From electoral debut disaster to historic victory

The bypoll attracted unusual national attention largely because Prashant Kishor decided to contest personally.

Only nine months ago, Jan Suraaj had suffered a crushing setback in the

. The party fielded candidates in 238 of the state's 243 constituencies but failed to win a single seat, while forfeiting deposits in 236 constituencies. Despite an extensive campaign built around Prashant Kishor's personal credibility, the party could not convert public attention into votes.

The obvious question, therefore, is: what changed in just nine months?

A changing political mood

Political observers believe the 2025 Assembly election was heavily influenced by welfare promises, including direct financial assistance for women and free electricity, helping the NDA secure a decisive victory. Since then, Bihar's political environment appears to have shifted considerably.

The transition from Nitish Kumar to Samrat Choudhary as Chief Minister coincided with a series of developments that reportedly generated dissatisfaction among sections of BJP's traditional support base.

Controversies surrounding the UGC guidelines, the Bharat Tiwari encounter, and widespread anger over repeated paper leak incidents created fresh political fault lines, particularly among students and young voters.

Why youth turned towards Prashant Kishor

Education has remained at the centre of Prashant Kishor's political messaging. His repeated emphasis on education reforms appears to have resonated with young voters seeking systemic change.

He has consistently questioned the academic credentials of Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary while projecting education reform as one of Bihar's most urgent priorities. His image as an educated professional has helped him emerge as a credible alternative, especially among urban youth.

Following the nationwide Gen Z protests, Bihar witnessed some of the strongest student mobilisations over paper leak controversies.

While the state has made visible improvements in roads and infrastructure over the past decade, concerns over the quality of education and the continued migration of young people remain widespread.

For many first-time and young voters, Prashant Kishor increasingly appeared to represent change.

Tejashwi Yadav's absence created political space

Equally significant was the growing disappointment among sections of the opposition's traditional support base.

Many voters expected Leader of the Opposition Tejashwi Yadav to aggressively raise issues affecting students and other public concerns. According to political observers in Patna, his perceived lack of visibility during debates over the Bharat Tiwari encounter and student protests created a vacuum in opposition politics.

Many voters reportedly believed that while one bypoll would not alter the government's stability, electing Prashant Kishor would strengthen the opposition's voice inside the Assembly.

Core voters turned away from the BJP, RJD

The final extent of vote transfer will become clearer only after the Election Commission releases detailed voting data. However, reporters on the ground believe Prashant Kishor attracted support from both BJP's and RJD's traditional voter bases.

RJD candidate Rekha Kumari appears to have suffered the sharpest decline. After securing 46,363 votes in the 2025 Assembly election, she is now estimated to have polled fewer than 15,000 votes.

There are also indications that sections of BJP's upper-caste support base were unhappy over issues such as paper leaks, the UGC guidelines and the Bharat Tiwari encounter.

BJP's candidate switch added to the narrative

The BJP's last-minute change of candidate also became a major talking point during the campaign. The party's nominee, Abhishek Kumar Sinha, withdrew his nomination on July 10 citing personal reasons. The withdrawal came just hours after Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary had campaigned for him in Bankipur.

World.title: Hard-right Reform U.K. vow to use navy to stop small boats
World.content:
The hard-right Reform U.K. party unveiled plans on Monday (August 3, 2026) for, if it wins power, "the largest military operation" in the Channel "since World War II" to stop migrants crossing on small boats.

The proposal — which experts and other political parties promptly rubbished — comes days after tens of thousands of migrants entered Spain's North African exclave of Ceuta from neighbouring Morocco, reigniting Europe's debate over irregular migration.

"What happened in Ceuta over the weekend shows you just how serious this situation is," Brexit campaigner Nigel Farage, who leads the anti-immigration Reform, told a press conference unveiling the new policy in a 28-page document.

It details plans to deploy Britain's Royal Navy to return small boats to France, something proposed and swiftly abandoned by the Conservative government in 2020. Reform would need to win the next general election — not due until 2029 — to implement the proposals.

They come as Mr. Farage and Reform — which led national polls for around 18 months but have seen that lead disappear in recent weeks — are embroiled in a series of scandals and official probes into their finances.

In the latest, Parliament's standards commissioner said on Monday (August 3, 2026) he had last week opened an investigation into an alleged "failure to declare" a financial interest by the party's deputy leader Richard Tice.

The commissioner was already probing Mr. Farage for a separate alleged parliamentary rules breach. But that was suspended when the Reform head resigned as an MP to trigger a by-election next week that he is contesting.

Meanwhile, London police have confirmed launching a probe in February last year over donations to Reform ahead of the 2024 general election, following a referral from the Electoral Commission watchdog.

'Doesn't add up'

However, Mr. Farage denied the announcement was a distraction stunt.

"We're very confident that our policy of securely picking people up and safely taking them back to France ... falls within other conventions of international law," he said, predicting Reform would stop the boats "within a fortnight".

The party's home affairs spokesman Zia Yusuf insisted any French resistance "would be a crime against humanity".

"If the Elysee Palace refuses, make no mistake: His Majesty's Royal Marines will disembark them safely on the very shore they left that morning," he added.

He said the plans would be "the largest military operation in the English Channel since World War II".

But Tom Sharpe, a former Royal Navy commander, told AFP that deploying the navy was "not really where the solution lies".

"There's a lot the navy can do but the idea of ... ferrying people back to France, against the French's will, to me just doesn't add up."

Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who replaced Keir Starmer two weeks ago, vowed on Sunday (August 2, 2026) to be "relentless" in curbing the crossings.

Since taking power in 2024, centre-left Labour has sought to "smash the gangs" that facilitate the journeys, including through increased cooperation with France.

In April, London signed a new three-year deal with Paris over the crossings, agreeing to pay up to €766 million ($897 million) to boost French law enforcement.

The British government argues the strategy is working, noting year-on-year migrant small boat arrivals in the first half of 2026 were down more than 42 percent to just over 14,000 people.

However, recent weeks have seen a spike, with a daily record for the year set on July 29 when 752 people arrived.

World.title: UDF govt. in Kerala aiding roll-out of “RSS-BJP agenda”: CPI

World.title: Vishaal Promoters launch new residential project at Thoppur
World.content:
Vishaal Promoters Private Limited have launched a new residential project ‘Vismaya’ at Thoppur.

Speaking at the launch function, Vishaal group chairman R. Illankovan said the property was ideally located near the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) hospital. “We have plans to expand in this zone as there is huge demand for compact homes on a secure campus.”

As may as 156 residences would come up in about three years. Each of the 2 BHK homes would be constructed in 902 to 1,003 square feet carpet area.

Rajarathinam Illankovan and Arunachalam Illankovan of Vishaal Group said that ‘Vismaya’ would have a club house, multipurpose hall, indoor badminton court, creche, mini-theatre, children play area, gym, zumba and aerobics, among other amenities. Above all, the residential complex would have ample open space well-crafted for residents to have a connect with nature. There were also plans to have rainwater harvesting structure in the complex, more green space and natural light for residents.

With the RERA approval and other mandatory clearances obtained from the Tamil Nadu government, the construction would be completed in August 2029 and handed over to the rightful owners for occupation. The 98-cent sprawling property would have basement, stilt and 13 floors. Each floor would have 12 units.

The company had announced a special launch price of ₹5,999 per sq ft for the first 30 bookings, Mr. Rajarathinam Illankovan said and added that the response was encouraging on day one.

Velammal group chairman M. V. Muthuramalingam released the brochure on the occasion and Kappalur Industrial Estate Association president P. N. Ragunatha Raja received the first copy.

World.title: UG-NEET counselling schedule announced; DME yet to submit seat matrix
World.content:
The Medical Counselling Committee (MCC) has announced the schedule for UG NEET 2026 counselling for the 2026-27 academic year. The first round will begin on August 13. However, Karnataka’s Department of Medical Education (DME) is yet to submit the medical seat matrix to the Karnataka Examinations Authority (KEA), which is likely to delay the NEET counselling process in the State.

According to the MCC schedule, the first round of counselling will be held from August 13 to 15, the second round from August 31 to September 8, and the third round from September 16 to 26. The stray vacancy round will be conducted from October 3 to 5.

The academic session for undergraduate (UG) medical courses is scheduled to commence on September 8.

In the current academic year, a total of 15,395 MBBS seats are available across 75 medical colleges in the State, including 24 government and 51 private colleges. The National Medical Commission (NMC) has approved these seats. However, the admission process is yet to begin as the State government has not submitted the seat matrix to the Karnataka Examinations Authority (KEA).

Speaking to The Hindu, H. Prasanna, Executive Director of KEA, said, “The MCC has already announced the NEET counselling schedule, and we have to start the counselling process. Students and parents are waiting. The Department of Medical Education (DME) has been requested several times to submit the seat matrix. However, it has not been received yet.”

“We will start the counselling process as soon as we receive the seat matrix. The mock allotment list can then be published, giving students sufficient time for option entry. It will also provide a clear idea of the colleges in which they are likely to secure seats,” he said.

However, B.L. Sujatha Rathod, Director, DME, said the delay was due to a combination of factors. “Even after approving the final seat matrix, the NMC has recently sanctioned an additional 50 seats each for the government medical colleges in Mandya and Karwar. With this, the number of medical seats in the State has increased to 15,495. Four more government medical colleges are also likely to get seat enhancement. We are awaiting this, as any further increase in seats after finalising the seat matrix will disrupt the roster. Further, it has been decided to reserve 15% of seats under the Non-Resident Indian (NRI) quota in government medical colleges from this year, and the proposal is likely to receive approval at the next Cabinet meeting.”

World.title: Kerala University to establish Ganapati Sastri Chair
World.content:
Kerala University will establish a special academic chair named Ganapati Sastri Chair in memory of the distinguished Sanskrit scholar and manuscriptologist T. Ganapati Sastri on the occasion of his death centenary.

Vice Chancellor in-charge Mohanan Kunnummal made the announcement while inaugurating a national seminar jointly organised by the Manuscript Library and the Oriental Research Institute at the Karyavattom campus.

Speaking on the occasion, Prof. Kunnummal said that Ganapati Sastri’s contributions were unparalleled, particularly in recovering and presenting to the world rare Indian texts such as the Bhasa’s plays and Kautilya’s Arthashastra.

He said the Ganapati Sastri Chair is being established to provide specialised training for the younger generation in palm-leaf manuscript research and script reading, while also prioritising the modern digitisation of ancient manuscripts.

World.title: Riverbanks, low-lying areas of Ernakulam district remain on alert despite relief from heavy rain
World.content:
A total of 110 people remained in relief camps across the district on Monday (August 3) following heavy downpours over the past few days. The day passed without much rain-related trouble.

Eight camps remained active in the district—four in Muvattupuzha taluk and two each in Kunnathunad and Kothamangalam—while four had been closed. Those who have taken shelter in camps include 51 women, 40 men, and 19 children.

Though the district did not witness incessant rain on Monday, the authorities advised people residing along the Muvattupuzha and Thodupuzha rivers, as well as in low-lying areas, to remain alert as the water levels in the rivers remained above the warning marks.

Authorities said the water level at the Malankara dam had touched the red-alert mark of 41.30 metres in the evening as inflow from the catchment area remained heavy. Excess water had been discharged from the dam by gradually raising its shutters since Sunday night (August 2), they said.

Though a flood-like situation prevailed along the Pooyamkutty river in Kothamangalam following heavy rain on Sunday night, it eased later as weather conditions improved. The Manikandanchal causeway across the river, which serves as a critical link between interior tribal hamlets and villages such as Manikandanchal and Kallelimedu and the mainland, was submerged in the morning. However, the water receded by afternoon, officials said.

Minister visits Chellanam

Higher Education Minister Roji M. John, who is in charge of the district, visited different wards of the Chellanam grama panchayat that had been severely affected by heavy rain and sea surge. Stating that the situation in the region required a permanent solution, the Minister said the government would shortly initiate steps to complete the construction of a seawall. Mr. John was accompanied by Kochi MLA Muhammed Shiyas.

World.title: APCRDA launches grama sabhas to discuss Amaravati village road plans
World.content:
The Andhra Pradesh Capital Region Development Authority (APCRDA) on Monday (August 3, 2026) launched a series of grama sabhas (meetings) in capital villages to prepare village circulation and integration plans as part of the Amaravati Master Plan. The first meetings were held at Abbarajupalem and Rayapudi in the North-West Grid.

The consultations were organised to familiarise residents with the proposed village road circulation plan, integration plan and the road network envisaged under the Amaravati Master Plan while seeking suggestions from local communities before finalising the proposals.

APCRDA officials explained how the existing village roads would be integrated with the proposed road network in the Land Pooling Scheme (LPS) zones. They also outlined plans for strengthening infrastructure to meet future development needs and improve connectivity between villages and the capital city.

Officials said detailed surveys of the existing village road circulation pattern and the proposed LPS road network were being undertaken to collect comprehensive data. The findings would be used to prepare effective village circulation and integration plans and support future infrastructure development.

Residents shared their suggestions and views on the proposed plans during the meetings. APCRDA officials said the feedback would be examined before finalising the plans for each village.

According to the authority, grama sabhas will be conducted in all Amaravati capital villages in phases. Officials from the Planning, Development Promotion, Social Development and Estates wings of APCRDA, along with technical experts from The Urbaniser, will participate in the consultations and interact directly with residents to gather their inputs.

World.title: Train services on Mangaluru-Bengaluru sector resume after two-day suspension
World.content:
The South Western Railway (SWR) commenced normal passenger train services on the Mangaluru-Bengaluru sector with the resumption of night train services, except the Karwar-KSR Bengaluru Panchaganga Express, from Monday.

Services on the sector were suspended following the accumulation of debris on the track caused by heavy rain-induced landslips on Saturday night, between Shiribagilu and Yadakumari stations on the Subrahmanya Road-Sakleshpur Ghat section.

Mangaluru Central-Vijayapura-Mangaluru Central (Train No. 17378/17377), KSR Bengaluru-Karwar Panchaganga (Train No. 16595), KSR Bengaluru-Kozhikode-KSR Bengaluru (Train No. 16511/16512), and SMVT Bengaluru-Murdeshwar-SMVT Bengaluru (Train No. 16585/16586) Expresses will run normally from Monday night, SWR Mysuru Division Divisional Railway Manager Mudit Mittal told The Hindu. A track-fit certificate was issued to operate trains through the affected stretch at 7.25 p.m. on Monday, he added.

As the Bengaluru-Karwar Panchaganga Express was detained at Sakleshpur on Saturday and did not reach Karwar, the Karwar-Bengaluru Panchaganga Express (Train 16596) will not operate on Monday for want of a rake, he clarified.

With track clearance given late in the evening, all night services are operating behind schedule, delayed by a minimum of two hours.

Some trains diverted

Following the suspension of services through the ghat section, the Railways operated the KSR Bengaluru-Kozhikode-KSR Bengaluru and SMVT Bengaluru-Murdeshwar-SMVT Bengaluru Expresses via Shoranur and Palakkad, while the Vijayapura-Mangaluru Central-Vijayapura Express was operated via Londa and Madgaon on Sunday night. It cancelled the Panchaganga Express and daytime train services on the Yeshwantpur-Mangaluru Junction and Karwar-Yeshwantpur routes on Sunday and Monday.

Day and night work

Immediately after the track disruption was reported around 8.45 p.m. on Saturday, SWR’s Mysuru Division rushed a relief train with personnel and material to the location. Earthmovers were pressed into service to remove debris while personnel stabilised the affected slope with sandbags and other support material.

Mr Mittal supervised the restoration work on Sunday. He said emergency lights were provided to facilitate debris clearance through the night, enabling the track to be cleared. Late on Monday evening, the track-fit certificate was issued, he said.

World.title: Death toll from suicide bombing near police station in Swat rises to 17
World.content:
SWAT: The death toll from Sunday’s suicide bombing near a police station in Swat rose to 17 on Monday, including several policemen.

The suicide bombing had taken place near the Kabal Police Station while a protest against lawlessness was under way at the adjoining public square. Police said that the suicide bomber had detonated his explosives after police personnel atte­mpted to stop and search him at the entrance to the police station.

According to a list of casualties shared by Swat police spokesperson Nasir Iqbal Karimi, seven policemen and 10 civilians have lost their lives in the incident while 18 policemen and nine civilians have been injured.

Police have revised down the death toll from an earlier tally of 19, which they shared in a statement earlier in the day.

Karimi said in the statement that a large-scale rescue operation had been launched immediately after the attack, in which more than 50 Rescue 1122 personnel participated.

“Rescue teams provided first aid at the scene before shifting the injured to various hospitals for further treatment. Authorities are continuing relief efforts as investigations into the suicide attack remain under way,” it said.

In a separate statement, Swat police said the funeral prayers of two policemen martyred in the suicide attack were held at Javed Iqbal Shaheed Police Lines on Monday.

A smartly turned-out police contingent presented a guard of honour to Constable Mukarram Khan and Constable Hussain Khan, and floral wreaths were laid on their coffins.

The ceremony was attended by Malakand Regional Police Officer (RPO) Syed Fida Hassan Shah, Swat District Police Officer (DPO) Muhammad Umar Khan, Superintendent of Police (operations) Ghulam Sadiq Khan, Superintendent of Police (headquarters) Ataullah, and other senior police officers.

Security personnel and law enforcers have been coming under attack in KP, which continues to face terrorism.

According to the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies’ (PICSS) monthly security assessment released on Saturday, Security personnel deaths in terrorism incidents in KP, excluding merged districts, increased from 12 in June to 38 in July and terrorist deaths from 37 to 108, reflecting a rise by 192pc. But civilian deaths fell from 26 to seven, a decline by 73pc. One peace committee member was also killed.

Security personnel deaths in merged districts rose from six to 11 and terrorist deaths fell from 72 to 55. Civilian deaths, meanwhile, rose by 86pc, increasing from seven to 13.

CM visits Swat

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi reached Swat on Monday to meet with the martyrs’ families. He was accompanied by Special Assistant for Home Affairs Tariq Saeed, Chief Secretary Shahab Ali Shah and the KP inspector general (IG) of police, according to a statement issued by the CM office.

In Swat, he visited Sheikh Zayed Al Nahyan Hospital in Saidu Sharif and inquired about the health of those injured in the suicide attack.

The chief minister directed the hospital administration to ensure the provision of the best possible medical treatment to all the injured, the statement said.

It added that the CM also chaired a high-level meeting at the Jirga Hall in Saidu Sharif. At the meeting, which was also attended by senior officials, the CM was briefed on the overall law and order situation in Malakand Division and its Swat district.

Reaffirming the government’s commitment to restoring peace, the chief minister said there would be no compromise on law and order in Swat and Malakand. He directed the relevant authorities to launch a full-scale operation against terrorists and ensure that peace and stability were restored.

Meanwhile, KP Inspector General of Police (IG) Zulfikar Hameed visited the injured personnel and civilians in the hospital, according to a post on the KP Police’s X account.

“Our police personnel have high morale. The cowardly attacks of terrorists will be given a befitting response,” he is quoted as saying.

Lawyers, traders observe strike

Lawyers across Swat and Upper Swat observed a complete strike on Monday to condemn Sunday’s suicide bombing. Court proceedings remained suspended as members of the legal fraternity expressed solidarity with the victims and called for stronger measures for eliminating terrorism.

A shutter-down strike was also observed across Kabal tehsil, where markets remained closed.

Separately, elders of the Swat Qaumi Jirga, traders, lawyers, and youth representatives have announced a protest demonstration at Nishat Chowk in Swat’s Mingora on August 7 to condemn the recent wave of terrorism in the region.

The organisers said the planned demonstration was aimed at expressing solidarity with the victims of terrorist attacks. It was being organised to demand lasting peace and urge the government to take decisive action against terrorist groups operating in the area, they said.

World.title: PM Shehbaz congratulates PML-N after party maintains lead in second phase of AJK polls
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif congratulated the PML-N’s leadership and successful candidates on Monday after unofficial results of the second phase of elections in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) showed it had won 14 of 18 seats up for grabs the previous day.

The PML-N’s main rival in the contest and also its ally in the Centre, the PPP, has accused the PML-N of electoral malpractices, rigging and violence during Sunday polls — as it had during the first phase of the elections in Mirpur division on July 27. The PML-N secured nine of the 13 seats in the first phase while the PPP won the remaining four.

Elections in AJK are being held in three phases over security concerns, with polling having been held on seven seats of Muzaffarabad division and 12 refugee seats — reserved seats for refugees from India-occupied Kashmir — on Sunday. In the third phase, elections will be held in 11 constituencies of Poonch division on August 10.

‘Results reflect people’s confidence in PML-N’s policies’

A statement released by the PM’s Office on Monday said the premier congratulated PML-N’s leadership and successful candidates after their win in the second phase.

“The continuity of this success is a result of the hard work of PML-N President Nawaz Sharif and the entire PML-N team,” the statement quoted PM Shehbaz as saying

According to the statement, the premier noted that Nawaz and the PML-N team had conducted a successful electoral campaign in AJK and the party’s success “reflects the confidence of the people of AJK in PML-N’s policies”.

He said the development and prosperity of AJK and the welfare of its people remained PML-N’s top priority.

PM Shehbaz added that political parties had actively participated in the second phase of the AJK elections, which he said would further strengthen the democratic process.

Results breakdown

Earlier in the day, state broadcaster Radio Pakistan reported the unofficial results of Sunday’s elections, citing AJK Chief Election Commissioner Justice (retd) Ghulam Mustafa Mughal’s press talk in Muzaffarabad.

During the press briefing, he announced that the PML-N had won 14 seats and the PPP four, the report said.

Unofficial results

LA-25 bagged by PML-N’s Ghulam Qadir

LA-26 bagged by PPP’s Mian Abdul Waheed Khan

LA-29 bagged by PPP’s Sardar Mukhtar Ahmad Khan

LA-30 bagged by PML-N’s Mustafa Bashir Abbasi

LA-31 bagged by PML-N’s Saqib Majeed Khan

LA-32 bagged by PML-N’s Raja Farooq Haider Khan

LA-34 (Jammu-I) — PML-N’s Nasir Hussain Dar

LA-35 (Jammu-II) —PML-N’s Chaudhry Muhammad Ismael

LA-36 (Jammu-III) — PML-N’s Muhammad Ahsan Raza

LA-37 (Jammu-IV) — PML-N’s Maryam Javed

LA-38 (Jammu-V) — PML-N’s Zeeshan Ali

LA-39 (Jammu-VI) — PML-N’s Raja Muhammad Siddique Khan

LA-40 (Kashmir Valley-I) — PPP’s Amir Abdul Ghaffar Khan

LA-41 (Kashmir Valley-II) — PML-N’s Muhammad Amir Shah

LA-42 (Kashmir Valley-III) — PML-N’s Syed Shoukat Ali Shah

LA-43 (Kashmir Valley-IV) — PML-N’s Muhammad Yasin Lone

LA-44 (Kashmir Valley-V) — PML-N’s Ahmad Raza Qadri

LA-45 (Kashmir Valley-VI) — PPP’s Abdul Majid Khan

Polling was postponed until Tuesday in LA-27 Muzaffarabad-I (Kutla) and at 71 of the 174 polling stations in LA-28 Muzaffarabad-II (Lachhrat) as polling staff and election material could not reach the constituency because of landslides and bad weather that resulted in blocked roads.

According to preliminary results issued by the AJK Election Commission, the refugee seat of LA-37 saw a tough contest between PML-N’s Maryam Javed and Jammu & Kashmir United Movement’s (JKUM) Usman Aleem.

Javed emerged as the winner with 28,547 votes, while Aleem was the runner-up with 22,937 votes.

According to a document showing results for constituencies LA-34 through LA-45, PPP candidates were the runner-ups to PML-N in LA-36, LA-39, LA-42 and LA-43.

All Jammu and Kashmir Muslim Conference was the runner-up in LA-44 and LA-45, while independents placed second in LA-34, LA-35 and LA-41.

CEC hints at no polling in Rawalakot, Tharor on Aug 10

For the third phase of the AJK elections, the CEC said that considering the situation in Poonch division, the commission would conduct polling on August 10 in three constituencies in Bagh, one in Haveli and one in Abbaspur.

However, the constituencies of Baloch and Palandri (in Sudhnoti district) were also under consideration, he said.

“If we receive positive reports from there and the way people in Muzaffarabad rejected all pressures and tactics, came out of their homes and cast their votes, people in Poonch also extend the same cooperation, God-willing, we are ready to hold elections in all constituencies except for Rawalakot city and Thorar.”

“Our preparation is complete for all constituencies. However, the law and order situation and the demands of the safety of voters play an important role in holding elections.”

Responding to a question, he said that under the AJK constitution, the current Legislative Assembly ceases to exist after August 4.

“Even if elections cannot be held in two or a few more constituencies, one cannot say that the house is not complete or those who have returned cannot take oath or perform their functions,” he explained.

He said the new assembly would still take oath after the completion of the August 10 polls.

For LA-27, where the election had been postponed across the constituency, he said polling will be held at all 197 polling stations tomorrow (Tuesday).

Polling would be held on Tuesday from 8am to 5pm at 54 polling stations in three union councils (UCs) of LA-28 Muzaffarabad-II (Lachhrat).

Polling staff and election material could not reach these areas in time due to road blockades. At two of these polling stations, supporters of a candidate had set ballot boxes on fire.

The CEC affirmed that adequate arrangements had been made to reopen the roads following bad weather.

After security personnel returned from other areas, additional forces had been deployed in view of the sensitivity of these constituencies to ensure the electoral process was completed peacefully. He added that polling staff had already been dispatched to their respective stations under security escort.

AJK Election Commissioner retd Justice Ghulam Mustafa Mughal addresses the media on Aug 3, 2026. — Photo provided by Tariq Naqash

Speaking on yesterday’s elections, the AJK CEC said voter turnout in the seven constituencies stood at 53 per cent.

“This was certainly a difficult election, and given the circumstances that were created, this is by no means a low turnout,” retired Justice Mughal noted.

“I congratulate the people for making the right decision. They rejected the path of violence and chose the power of the vote instead — a path of positive change that will produce beneficial results.”

Expressing regret over allegations levelled against the Election Commission, CEC Mughal said the electoral watchdog was a constitutional and autonomous institution whose responsibility was to conduct free, fair and impartial elections without favouring any party.

He said it was the state’s responsibility to provide full security and assist the Election Commission.

“We perform our duties in accordance with the Constitution and the law, and our conscience is clear.”

In view of Tuesday’s polling, the Muzaffarabad deputy commissioner has declared a public holiday across the district.

PML-N now has ‘simple majority’ to form govt: Rana Sana

As the unofficial results were released, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs and PML-N leader Rana Sanaullah said his party had now gained the “simple majority” needed to form a government in AJK.

He was addressing a press conference alongside Minister for Kashmir Affairs and Gilgit-Baltistan Amir Muqam.

“We have the government-forming number,” he said, adding that “there are a total of 45 seats […] and out of 45, PML-N has so far secured 23 seats”.

The PML-N leader said his party had won in four of the seven territorial constituencies in Muzaffarabad while the PPP, which had been “attempting to build a rigging narrative since 10:30am yesterday”, had secured three.

Sanaullah demanded that the PPP must tell the people how they managed to secure three seats despite the alleged rigging.

“Did they succeed because of rigging or because of a free and fair election?”

Sanaullah further stated that the PML-N had also secured 10 out of 12 refugee seats while the PPP had won two.

“A democratic government, which has the people’s mandate, will now be formed in AJK, and it will work on ideological, economic, and political affairs of the region,” he said.

He added that a parliamentary party session of the PML-N would be called after the conclusion of the third phase of the elections for future decisions.

Speaking about PPP’s rigging allegations, the PML-N leader dismissed them and accused PPP of colluding with the proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) to disrupt the election process in Muzaffarabad.

“Anticipating PML-N’s win, PPP along with the action committee planned riots and [..] fired at the police personnel when they got there,” Sanaullah alleged.

He claimed that the incident created an atmosphere of fear in the area, which led to a lower turnout.

“We received at least 3,000 to 4,000 fewer votes due to this,” he claimed.

On PPP’s allegations that an attempt had been made on its candidate AJK Legislative Assembly Speaker Chaudhry Latif Akbar’s life, he accused the party of staging a “drama”. He also claimed that the PPP had refused to get Akbar’s medicolegal examination done.

Sanaullah accused the PPP of employing “dirty tricks” to sabotage the electoral process, saying that the PPP’s actions violated the Charter of Democracy, in which the party leadership had agreed that they would not “malign each other’s mandate with such dirty tricks”.

Replying to a question, he said the PPP had raised doubts over “high turnout” in constituencies where the PML-N’s candidate had won.

“With the kind of societal system in place in AJK, it is certainly possible that if there are 300 people in a village, 290 might show up to vote,” he said.

He asked the PPP to follow due process in case of complaints rather than “building a narrative and disrupting democracy and the election process”.

Federal govt’s last days have begun: Sharjeel

On the other hand, PPP’s Sharjeel Inam Memon said his party would continue to contest until the last phase of the AJK elections for the rights of Kashmiris despite what he described as “historical rigging”.

Addressing a press conference in Islamabad alongside PPP’s AJK chapter president Chaudhry Muhammad Yasin, Memon said, “PPP will fight for our Kashmiri brothers until the last moment.”

The Sindh senior minister accused the AJK CEC of being a PML-N supporter, alleging that the elections were being rigged in favour of the federal ruling party.

Referring to Sanaullah and Muqam’s press conference earlier in the day, Memon said they did not show any signs of guilt; rather, “they were proud of themselves for having stolen AJK’s mandate”.

He said that PPP would not resort to bad language and ridicule the way PML-N did.

Sharjeel claimed that in the Mirpur polls, PML-N candidates “stamped” ballot papers in LA-1, LA-5, LA-9, LA-11 and LA-12. He added that PPP had filed applications before the Election Commission against the alleged action but received no response.

“When the entire country knows that they won the 2024 elections through a donated mandate and rigging, but they have not accepted that to date, so how would they accept the rigging in AJK?” Memon claimed.

“I believe that the federal government’s last days have begun,” the PPP leader remarked.

Memon said that polling in LA-27 was postponed yesterday citing rainfall, despite there being no showers on Sunday in the area.

He contended that the Election Commission did not have the required capacity and could not arrange ballot materials on time.

In LA-28, only seven out of 10 union councils (UCs) were equipped for balloting, according to the Sindh minister. He said elections in the other three UCs would be held on Tuesday.

Memon also reiterated the PPP’s claim that acting AJK President Chaudhry Latif Akbar was attacked by PML-N workers while he was on his way to cast his vote.

He added that a PPP MNA was also fired upon and suffered a bullet injury on his hand when he went to a polling station in the same constituency.

“Kashmiris’ rights have been robbed for PML-N’s personal benefits,” the PPP leader said.

Meanwhile, Yasin noted that at 40 polling stations, voter turnout was between 85 and 99 per cent, adding that, on average, this figure was “no more than 40 to 45pc”.

Yasin also took exception to the phase-wise elections, saying that when the decision was announced, PPP workers had alerted their party chairman Bilawal that it was an “attempt to intensify rigging”.

Reports of violence

During the polling on Sunday, attempts were reportedly made to disrupt polling in some neighbourhoods of Muzaffarabad, but voting continued in most areas. In LA-31, Muzaffa­rabad-V (Khawra), clashes between workers of the PML-N and PPP were reported in Union Council Katkair.

The PPP alleged that one of its workers, Syed Mushtaq Shah, was killed in an attack by PML-N supporters. The PML-N rejected the allegation, claiming the man suffered a cardiac arrest following a scuffle between two groups. There was no independent confirmation of either claim.

PPP candidate and Legislative Assembly Speaker Akbar also wrote to the AJK chief election commissioner, alleging security lapses, firing incidents, interference in polling, prevention of polling agents from entering polling stations and denial of voting rights.

He also claimed there had been an attempt on his life in which Advocate Syed Mumtaz Hussain Naqvi was injured, and called for an investigation and legal action against those responsible. There was no immediate response from the Election Commission.

Clashes between workers of the two major parties, some involving the use of firearms, were also reported from other areas, though no casualties were immediately reported.

Low turnout outside AJK

Outside AJK, Kashmiris voted for their candidates vying for refugee seats at polling stations set up in Chakwal, Jhelum, Rawalpindi, Islamabad, Sialkot, Narowal, Sargodha, Attock, Nawabshah, Hyderabad, Mohmand, Mansehra, Quetta, Dera Ghazi Khan, Peshawar, Sanghar, and Naushahro Feroze.

Polling in these areas largely remained peaceful and recorded a low turnout. In Mohmand, not a single voter turned up at a station set up for the AJK polls. In Dera Ghazi Khan, a single registered female voter cast her ballot at the Govt Elementary School in Maumori, where a polling station had been established just for her.

Out of 12 refugee seats, seven seats are in Punjab, one seat is in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, one seat (Jammu-VI) is divided between Pun­jab, Islamabad, and Khyber Pakhtun­khwa, one seat is divided between Sindh and Balo­chistan (Valley-I), and one seat (Jammu-I) is shared among refugees living in Balochistan, Punjab, and Sindh. Valley-V seat is divided between Punjab and Islamabad.

World.title: Religious scholar killed in explosion at supermarket in South Waziristan's Wana
World.content:
LOWER SOUTH WAZIRISTAN: A religious scholar was killed in an explosion, suspected to have been caused by a pressure bomb, at a supermarket in Lower South Waziristan’s Wana on Monday, police said.

Wana Circle Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) Asghar Ali Shah told Dawn that the explosion occurred on the ground floor of a supermarket located in Rustam Bazaar.

He said Mufti Jana Mir Masti Khel sustained critical injuries in the explosion and was immediately shifted to Wana district headquarters hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries.

The DSP added that he and Wana City Police Station House Officer Usman Wazir, along with a large contingent of police, reached the site of the incident after the explosion, and the area was cordoned off while investigators collected forensic evidence.

DSP Shah said initial investigation suggested the bomb was planted to target the religious scholar.

He said police had filed an initial complaint and further investigation was under way to identify the perpetrators and determine the motive behind the attack.

The incident comes just three days after unidentified gunmen shot dead Maulana Ismail, a cleric affiliated with Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F), in Azam Warsak Bazaar of Lower South Waziristan’s Birmal tehsil.

On July 28, a local cleric was killed and two other people were injured in a suspected quadcopter attack near a mosque in the Landi Doag area of Birmal.

World.title: Islamabad ATC hands Mushtaq Ahmad to police on 3-day physical remand in protest case
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) has handed over former senator Mushtaq Ahmad Khan and other suspects to police on a three-day physical remand in a case registered in connection with a protest.

The police produced the former senator and another person named Daniyal before Duty Judge Rukhsanda Shaheen in the ATC.

During the hearing, the prosecution requested a 30-day physical remand of the suspects, stating that the police needed to recover a vehicle and weapons allegedly connected with the case.

After hearing the arguments, the court granted the police three-day physical remand of Mushtaq and the other suspects and directed that they be produced before the court again upon completion of the remand period.

The first information report (FIR) was registered at Islamabad’s Shalimar Police Station on July 31, on the complaint of Sub-inspector Ghulam Murtaza.

The FIR said Mushtaq and dozens of others had led a crowd of about 400-500 people and gathered in the capital’s F-10.

It accused the former senator of making “incendiary” speeches on loudspeakers, forcing shops to shut down, and chanting slogans against “current government institutions”.

According to the FIR, Mushtaq then led the protesters to Sambal Road with the intention of marching to the Main Jinnah Avenue Road and blocking roads.

The FIR said the district administration told Mushtaq through a loudspeaker to end the gathering as it was being held without a no-objection certificate (NOC), but the former senator and others blocked a main road near Shalimar Plaza at around 7:10pm.

It accused the protesters of vandalising a media DSNG vehicle and other private cars passing by, along with pelting stones and “attacking” police officials. It further claimed that some protesters snatched away anti-riot helmets from personnel and threatened them.

Last Wednesday, Mushtaq’s Pakistan Rights Movement (PRM) alleged that he had been detained by Punjab police on July 28 from Kahuta Bazaar while he was returning from Azad Pattan Bridge after allegedly being denied entry into AJK.

Senior police officers in Punjab had not responded to calls and messages at the time. Police officials in Rawalpindi approached by Dawn for comment spoke off the record and denied that Mushtaq was in their custody.

Mushtaq’s X account said the next day that he had been released. Following this, he had announced a gathering on July 31 in Islamabad’s F-10 to “express condolences, solidarity with Kashmir and for peace and reconciliation”.

Last week, activists in Lahore were detained while holding a peaceful demonstration outside the press club to show solidarity with the proscribed JAAC.

Additional input by Mohammad Asghar

World.title: PM Shehbaz directs completion of privatisation programmes according to agreed timelines
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Monday directed officials to complete all stages of the government’s privatisation programme within the prescribed timelines.

Presiding over a meeting in Islamabad reviewing the privatisation of state-owned enterprises, the prime minister instructed relevant ministries and institutions to work in close coordination to ensure that all targets and deadlines under the privatisation programme were met, according to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The meeting was attended by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Senator Muhammad Ishaq Dar, Federal Ministers Khawaja Muhammad Asif, Jam Kamal Khan, Ahad Khan Cheema, Sardar Awais Khan Leghari and other senior officials, the PMO said.

PM Shehbaz said the privatisation structure for the Zarai Taraqiati Bank Limited (ZBTL) should be designed in a way that safeguards the bank’s primary role in agricultural financing.

“It must be ensured that even after privatisation, the Zarai Taraqiati Bank’s focus on providing agricultural loans and financial resources to small and medium-scale farmers remains intact,” he was quoted as saying by the statement.

The premier noted that improving farmers’ access to financial resources was “essential” for increasing per-acre agricultural productivity, especially for small and medium-scale cultivators, adding that agricultural development remained critical to Pakistan’s economic growth and food security.

Officials from the privatisation ministry briefed the meeting on progress under the government’s privatisation programme and future targets. The meeting was told that 27 state-owned enterprises were included in the programme, which was being implemented in three phases.

According to the briefing, the financial closing process for the privatisation of Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) and First Women Bank has been completed. Officials said the first financial closing and transfer of management control of PIA were completed on June 29.

The meeting also reviewed progress on the planned privatisation of Islamabad Electric Supply Company (Iesco), Faisalabad Electric Supply Company (Fesco) and Gujranwala Electric Power Company (Gepco).

Officials said expressions of interest (EOIs) had been advertised for these companies, with submission deadlines set for Aug 7 for Fesco, Aug 21 for Gepco and Sep 7 for Iesco.

The meeting was also told that international companies have expressed interest in these distribution companies, while roadshows with investors are also underway, according to the PMO.

Fesco, Gepco and Iesco collectively serve more than 14 million consumers across major industrial, commercial and urban centres of Punjab, the Islamabad region, and parts of Azad Jammu and Kashmir.

The transaction offers investors an opportunity to acquire between 51 per cent and 100pc shareholding, along with management control, in each of the three distribution companies.

Officials also updated the prime minister on progress on the privatisation of ZTBL, stating that the transaction structure was being designed to protect the bank’s agricultural lending mandate.

The meeting further reviewed progress on the planned privatisation of Islamabad International Airport, Jinnah International Airport in Karachi and Allama Iqbal International Airport in Lahore.

The PM directed officials to maintain close oversight of all ongoing privatisation transactions and ensure their completion according to the agreed timelines.

The premier issued these instructions three days after Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi’s statement saying that the system had “collapsed”, and that things would not get fixed as long as “the present system is not reset”.

Presiding over a separate meeting on private investment, PM Shehbaz directed officials to prepare, at the earliest, a roadmap for establishing a private equity fund to promote investment, support small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and encourage sustainable economic growth, according to his office.

He asked officials to submit a comprehensive plan for developing both Pakistan’s public equity market and a private equity fund to improve access to investment capital and help attract foreign investment.

“The promotion of private investment is essential for the country’s economic growth,” the premier said according to another statement issued by the PMO.

He said that private equity funds could serve as an effective catalyst for investment, business expansion and job creation, adding that sectors including mining, agriculture, livestock, energy and information technology had the potential to become key drivers of Pakistan’s economic growth.

PM Shehbaz said a stronger public equity market could provide an important financing avenue for investment in these sectors. He noted that the banking sector’s contribution to investment financing remained limited, making the development of alternative sources of capital increasingly important.

The premier noted that the government was prioritising policies aimed at strengthening the economy on a sustainable basis through private sector-led investment, industrial growth and export promotion.

DPM Dar, Minister of State Bilal Azhar Kayani, Special Assistant to the Prime Minister Haroon Akhtar, and senior government officials attended the meeting, the PMO said.

World.title: Bulls in charge as PSX opens week by gaining 2,100 points
World.content:
The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) opened the week in the green on Monday, gaining more than 2,100 points to close above the 178,000 mark.

The development came as global oil prices tumbled on Monday, after United States President Donald Trump said fresh talks with Iran would begin later in the day.

At 11am, the benchmark KSE-100 index had gained 2273.78 points, from the previous close of 176,094.11 points. By 2:18pm, the index’s gains had dropped to 1781.72 points.

However, after an intraday low of 177,759.88 points, it staged a recovery after 2pm to close at 178,200.02 points — up by 2,105.91 (1.20 per cent) from the previous close.

Topline Securities Ltd. said that the rally reflected “renewed risk appetite as investors welcomed signs of easing regional tensions and softer energy prices”.

On the index contribution front, FFC, MEBL, LUCK, PPL, and ENGROH emerged as the top contributors, collectively adding approximately 699 points to the benchmark index, according to the firm.

Market activity also strengthened: the total traded volume rose to 785 million shares, while traded value stood at Rs33bn, it added.

Mettis Global, a web-based financial portal, said the positive momentum at PSX came as “investors took cues from easing geopolitical tensions after Trump called off a planned strike on Iran, reducing immediate concerns over a wider regional conflict”.

Awais Ashraf, director of research at AKD Securities, said investor optimism extended the positive momentum from the previous week, driven by expectations of a swift agreement between the US and Iran.

“Sentiment improved after the US president announced that talks with Iran would resume on Monday, without setting a deadline for reaching an agreement following the cessation of hostilities,” he said.

Ashraf added that “the return of inflation to single digits in July, with the data due to be released today, would provide an additional catalyst for the market by strengthening expectations of monetary easing and further boosting investor confidence”.
